title: Verify Reachability to a New Aggregated Prefix Advertised to a Site
prompt: A Direct Connect gateway is associated with a Transit Gateway. The site receives 10.64.0.0/12 through BGP, as registered in the association's allowed prefixes, but cannot reach the new VPC's 10.65.8.0/22 within that range. The site's route and the VPC's return route have already been verified. What should be checked next?

choices.text: In the TGW route table associated with the Direct Connect attachment, verify that traffic destined for 10.65.8.0/22 is forwarded to the new VPC.
choices.explanation: For the TGW association, the allowed prefixes are advertised from the DX gateway. Receiving the aggregate route at the site does not prove that TGW has a forwarding route to each individual VPC.

choices.text: Because the aggregate route is visible through BGP, assume that TGW can reach every more-specific prefix and update only the VPC's private DNS.
choices.explanation: The presence of an advertisement and successful forwarding are separate matters. If the IP route itself is missing, changing DNS does not resolve the problem.

choices.text: Adjust the site's BGP Local Preference to further prefer the current Direct Connect route for the same aggregate prefix.
choices.explanation: The site has already selected the correct route, so this does not repair a missing route to the destination beyond TGW.

choices.text: Assume that adding the VPC CIDR to the allowed prefixes automatically creates the route through the target VPC attachment.
choices.explanation: Allowed prefixes advertise routes toward the site; they do not automatically complete TGW's forwarding table for VPC destinations.

learning.reason: For the TGW association, the allowed prefixes are advertised from the DX gateway. Receiving the aggregate route at the site does not prove that TGW has a forwarding route to each individual VPC.
learning.concept: Validate DX gateway allowed-prefix advertisements separately from TGW forwarding.

title: Enforce VPC Address-Allocation Rules by Region
prompt: A network team is planning VPCs in multiple Regions that will eventually be connected through Transit Gateway. The parent IPAM pool contains the enterprise-wide range, and nonoverlapping ranges are to be allocated by Region. Each production VPC should receive only a /24 and should be able to receive an allocation only in its own Region. Which design should be used?

choices.text: Create separate IPAM scopes with the same CIDR in each Region and resolve overlaps through longest-prefix matching after interconnecting them.
choices.explanation: A design that permits overlaps in independent scopes does not provide unique address management for networks that are expected to route to one another.

choices.text: Set the allocation rule on the parent pool to /24 and wait for the parent setting to be inherited by Region pools without a locale.
choices.explanation: Rules are not automatically inherited by child pools. A locale is also required for allocating addresses to VPCs in the target Region.

choices.text: Manually specify a fixed CIDR for every VPC and use IPAM only for post-connection reporting.
choices.explanation: Manual allocation and after-the-fact monitoring cannot enforce the locale and required size as pool allocations when new VPCs are created.

choices.text: Create nonoverlapping Regional pools under the parent, specify their locales, and configure a /24 allocation rule in each pool.
choices.explanation: A VPC obtains an allocation from a pool whose locale is the same Region as the VPC. Because allocation rules are not inherited by child pools, the required settings must be applied to each pool.

learning.reason: A VPC obtains an allocation from a pool whose locale is the same Region as the VPC. Because allocation rules are not inherited by child pools, the required settings must be applied to each pool.
learning.concept: Use Regional pool locales and explicitly configured child-pool allocation rules.

title: Provide a UDP Service in Two Regions Without Changing a Partner Allowlist
prompt: A partner registers fixed IP addresses in its firewall. Our UDP service runs on NLBs in two Regions, and during a Regional failure the partner must continue using the same static Anycast IP addresses it registered. A user DNS change or migration to HTTP is not required. What should be configured?

choices.text: Assign a fixed Elastic IP to each NLB and use Route 53 for inter-Region failover.
choices.explanation: The NLB IP address differs by Region, so this does not satisfy the requirement to switch Regions while keeping the same IP address.

choices.text: Register the two Regional NLBs with a standard Global Accelerator UDP listener and distribute static IP addresses.
choices.explanation: This provides a common entry point for UDP and can deliver traffic to an endpoint in a healthy Region.

choices.text: Register custom origins in both Regions with CloudFront and configure UDP ports for forwarding.
choices.explanation: CloudFront is not an entry point for forwarding arbitrary UDP application traffic.

choices.text: Have the user register the UDP NLB from both Regions and switch to the healthy Region's IP in the application.
choices.explanation: This requires the user to identify and switch between Regional IP addresses and does not provide one shared Anycast entry point for both Regions.

learning.reason: This provides a common entry point for UDP and can deliver traffic to an endpoint in a healthy Region.
learning.concept: Static Anycast IP addresses and a UDP listener on a standard accelerator.

title: Separate origin failover design for reads and updates
prompt: A site delivered through CloudFront has a read-only GET operation and an order-submission POST operation. When the primary origin returns 503, the read content should be retrieved from another origin. The order API requires its own idempotent failover design. Where should you use a CloudFront origin group?

choices.text: Allow all HTTP methods and configure both operations to use the same origin group so that both GET and POST fail over.
choices.explanation: Allowing more methods does not expand the methods eligible for origin-group failover.

choices.text: Use an origin group for the read behavior with 503 as the failover condition, and design POST recovery separately.
choices.explanation: The methods for which CloudFront switches to another origin do not include POST.

choices.text: Disable caching for both behaviors so that POST is always sent to the secondary origin when the primary fails.
choices.explanation: Changing cache settings does not enable origin failover for POST.

choices.text: Replace the primary origin's 503 with 200 in CloudFront and treat the order as confirmed solely based on the success response sent to the client.
choices.explanation: Replacing the response code does not guarantee success from an origin that did not process the order.

learning.reason: The methods for which CloudFront switches to another origin do not include POST.
learning.concept: CloudFront origin failover applies to GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS.

title: Design bidirectional routes for inter-Region TGW peering
prompt: VPCs are connected to independent TGWs in Tokyo and Osaka. Inter-Region peering has been approved, and routes to the TGW exist inside each VPC. To forward only the specified CIDRs of the remote Region and allow communication from both sides, what should you add?

choices.text: Add a static route to the remote side only in the Tokyo route table. Do not configure the Osaka side because it can return traffic through the route on which the connection arrived.
choices.explanation: A TGW does not create a return route from the state of an attachment. The Osaka side also needs a route toward Tokyo.

choices.text: In both TGWs, point the remote-side CIDRs to the source VPC attachment in each Region, without specifying a route through the peering connection.
choices.explanation: Traffic leaving for the remote Region requires a route whose next hop is the peering attachment.

choices.text: Enable automatic propagation for the peering attachments on both sides and wait for routes to the remote VPCs to appear in each TGW route table.
choices.explanation: Dynamic propagation between peering attachments is not available.

choices.text: Add static routes in the relevant route tables of both TGWs, pointing the approved remote-side CIDRs to the peering attachment.
choices.explanation: For TGW peering, configure the required static routes for both the forward and return paths instead of relying on automatic propagation.

learning.reason: For TGW peering, configure the required static routes for both the forward and return paths instead of relying on automatic propagation.
learning.concept: Add static routes pointing to the peering connection in the receiving route tables for each Region.

title: Consolidate cloud traffic to a private source range for an on-premises site
prompt: The audit network at an on-premises site allows API requests over DX only when they originate from a specified private CIDR. The addresses of many clients in the VPCs cannot be changed. Connections are initiated only from AWS, and neither public addresses nor the internet may be used. How should this be designed?

choices.text: Place a private NAT gateway in the approved private range and forward traffic destined for the site through the TGW from that gateway.
choices.explanation: This translates the source to the NAT gateway's private address and allows responses from the site to return to the original VPC clients.

choices.text: Have the site allow the public NAT gateway's Elastic IP and make that Elastic IP the source for traffic sent to the TGW.
choices.explanation: A public NAT gateway's Elastic IP is used through an IGW. It cannot be assumed to be the source for traffic sent to a TGW.

choices.text: Send all traffic destined for the site to an internet gateway and verify the source CIDR afterward through the site's DNS.
choices.explanation: An IGW is not the DX path to the site and cannot preserve the private route and specified source range.

choices.text: Aggregate only the routes learned by the site through DX and assume that the packet source will also change to the same prefix.
choices.explanation: Route advertisement aggregation does not rewrite the source address.

learning.reason: This translates the source to the NAT gateway's private address and allows responses from the site to return to the original VPC clients.
learning.concept: Use a private NAT gateway to translate the source of traffic destined for the site into the approved range.

title: Make IPv6 internet access outbound-only
prompt: The subnets in a VPC have globally routable IPv6 addresses. The application initiates connections to IPv6 services on the internet, but new IPv6 connections initiated from the internet must be blocked at the gateway. Existing IPv4 routes must remain unchanged. What should you do?

choices.text: Create a PrivateLink interface endpoint and forward every IPv6 service on the internet through it.
choices.explanation: An interface endpoint provides a route to a specified service; it is not a general-purpose IPv6 internet route.

choices.text: Route the IPv6 default route to a standard IGW and assume that globally routable IPv6 addresses cannot be reached from outside.
choices.explanation: With a standard IGW, inbound IPv6 connections from outside can be established depending on the configuration. It is not an outbound-only boundary.

choices.text: Route only the IPv4 0.0.0.0/0 to a NAT gateway and do not create an IPv6 default route.
choices.explanation: An IPv4 route cannot reach IPv6 destinations.

choices.text: Point the IPv6 default route for the target subnets to an egress-only internet gateway.
choices.explanation: This permits responses to IPv6 connections initiated from the VPC while blocking IPv6 connections initiated from outside.

learning.reason: This permits responses to IPv6 connections initiated from the VPC while blocking IPv6 connections initiated from outside.
learning.concept: Point the IPv6 ::/0 route to an egress-only internet gateway.

title: Operate NLB targets independently by Availability Zone
prompt: To maintain separate failure boundaries for each Availability Zone with an NLB, cross-zone load balancing is disabled. All targets in only one Availability Zone become unhealthy, while the other Availability Zone remains healthy. What happens to a client that newly resolves the destination through DNS?

choices.text: The IP address of the unhealthy Availability Zone is always included in DNS, and the NLB preferentially sends traffic to that Availability Zone as a fail-open behavior when all targets are unhealthy.
choices.explanation: This case differs from one in which all targets are unhealthy.

choices.text: An unhealthy target in one Availability Zone always causes DNS for all Availability Zones on the NLB to be removed, making the healthy Availability Zone unavailable as well.
choices.explanation: An Availability Zone with healthy targets remains available as a DNS destination.

choices.text: The NLB node in the unhealthy Availability Zone distributes traffic directly to healthy targets in another Availability Zone without any configuration change.
choices.explanation: When cross-zone load balancing is disabled, each node does not automatically use targets in other Availability Zones.

choices.text: The NLB IP address in the unhealthy Availability Zone is removed from DNS, and the IP address of the healthy Availability Zone is used for new resolutions.
choices.explanation: With cross-zone load balancing disabled, an NLB determines that an Availability Zone has no healthy targets and removes that Availability Zone from the DNS destinations.

learning.reason: With cross-zone load balancing disabled, an NLB determines that an Availability Zone has no healthy targets and removes that Availability Zone from the DNS destinations.
learning.concept: An NLB removes the IP address of an unhealthy Availability Zone from DNS responses

title: Return a healthy, low-latency entry point from two active Regions
prompt: Two ALBs in different Regions run the same public service. DNS responses should normally prioritize the Region with the lowest latency for the requester, and use the other Region if the ALB in the preferred Region is unhealthy. Which Route 53 records should you create?

choices.text: Create latency alias records with Evaluate Target Health disabled and use a short TTL to exclude the unhealthy Region.
choices.explanation: TTL affects when clients make another query, but it does not add ALB health to the DNS selection criteria.

choices.text: Create two weighted alias records with the same weight and enable Evaluate Target Health.
choices.explanation: This can exclude an unhealthy entry point, but normal selection is based on weights and does not consider the requester's latency.

choices.text: Create a latency alias record for the ALB in each Region and enable Evaluate Target Health.
choices.explanation: Route 53 can use regional latency information and the health of each alias target to select a healthy destination.

choices.text: Create a failover record with a fixed primary and always use the same Region while both ALBs are healthy.
choices.explanation: A fixed primary and secondary prevent normal traffic from using both Regions according to requester latency.

learning.reason: Route 53 can use regional latency information and the health of each alias target to select a healthy destination.
learning.concept: Latency alias records pointing to ALBs with target health evaluation

title: Eliminate multiple single points of failure in a dedicated connection
prompt: For Direct Connect supporting a critical system, the design must tolerate not only the failure of a single physical connection but also the failure of a single AWS-side device and a single connection location. Device failures within each location must also be covered by the design. Which Resiliency Toolkit option and physical connectivity should you choose?

choices.text: Aggregate multiple connections on the same AWS device in the same location and use a LAG to prepare for a facility failure.
choices.explanation: A LAG provides connection redundancy but leaves the same device and the same location as failure points.

choices.text: Choose Maximum resiliency and distribute the connections across different devices in two locations.
choices.explanation: This provides separate physical paths for device failures within each facility and for the loss of an entire facility.

choices.text: Create one connection in each of two locations and depend on only one device within each location.
choices.explanation: This separates the connection locations but does not meet the requirement to use different devices within each location.

choices.text: Create multiple VIFs on one physical connection and use a different prefix for each VIF to separate equipment failures.
choices.explanation: Splitting logical interfaces does not separate the physical connection and connection equipment, which remain the same failure points.

learning.reason: This provides separate physical paths for device failures within each facility and for the loss of an entire facility.
learning.concept: Maximum resiliency distributes connections across separate locations and different AWS-side devices in each location

title: Reduce the long-distance public-network segment of an encrypted VPN
prompt: A remote site uses an Internet VPN to connect to AWS, and you want to reduce the variability of long-distance Internet paths. Using a supported Region for a new connection and NAT-T devices, you want to keep IPsec while using the AWS edge network. What should you choose?

choices.text: Choose a Transit Gateway and create an Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN.
choices.explanation: This uses Global Accelerator to bring traffic into the AWS network from an AWS edge location near the site.

choices.text: Configure a standard Site-to-Site VPN from the remote site and add a VPC NLB to Global Accelerator.
choices.explanation: Application traffic destined for the VPC NLB can be accelerated separately, but the Internet path between the site and the VPN tunnel endpoint does not change.

choices.text: Create two Site-to-Site VPN tunnels with acceleration disabled and use BGP to provide redundant paths to AWS.
choices.explanation: This provides tunnel failover but does not add a mechanism to bring the long-distance Internet segment into the AWS network earlier.

choices.text: Convert an existing VPN terminated on a Virtual Private Gateway to an Accelerated VPN.
choices.explanation: Acceleration is configured on a new VPN terminated by a TGW; an existing VGW connection is not converted in place.

learning.reason: This uses Global Accelerator to bring traffic into the AWS network from an AWS edge location near the site.
learning.concept: Create a new Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN terminated by a TGW

title: Connecting an SD-WAN Appliance to a TGW with GRE and BGP
prompt: A virtual SD-WAN appliance exists in an existing VPC. The VPC already has reachability to a Transit Gateway through an existing VPC attachment, and you need to add GRE-based forwarding and BGP-based route exchange between the appliance and the TGW. Which configuration meets the requirements?

choices.text: Create a TGW peering connection with the virtual appliance and exchange GRE through BGP within the peering connection.
choices.explanation: TGW peering connects TGWs to each other; it does not provide a GRE/BGP connection with a virtual router.

choices.text: Add the BGP peer IP directly to the regular VPC attachment without creating a Connect attachment.
choices.explanation: A regular VPC attachment alone does not provide a Connect Peer that terminates GRE/BGP with the virtual appliance.

choices.text: Create a TGW Connect attachment that uses the VPC attachment as its transport, and configure a Connect Peer with the appliance.
choices.explanation: This enables GRE to be established over the existing underlying connection and routes to be exchanged using BGP.

choices.text: Create a Site-to-Site VPN between the virtual appliance and the TGW, and use the same GRE implementation on an appliance that does not support IPsec.
choices.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN tunnels use IPsec and do not provide the required GRE connection to the TGW.

learning.reason: GRE can be established over the existing underlying connection, and routes can be exchanged using BGP.
learning.concept: Configure a TGW Connect attachment and Connect Peer over the existing VPC transport

title: Offering Only a Shared TCP Service to Consumers in Another Region
prompt: A provider's TCP service runs behind an NLB in a single Region and cannot be moved because of internal policy. A partner VPC in another Region wants private access to only this service without establishing broad network connectivity. Both Regions are supported. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Allow only the provider's Region in the service and assume that consumers in another Region can select it by specifying the same service name.
choices.explanation: The consumer's Region must be added as a supported Region before a new endpoint can be created from that Region.

choices.text: Allow the consumer's Region and principal in the provider's endpoint service, then have the consumer create an endpoint that specifies the service.
choices.explanation: This allows the provider and consumer to use different Regions while limiting connectivity to the endpoint service.

choices.text: Make the NLB internet-facing, add each partner's fixed IP address to an allow list, and publish the service through public DNS.
choices.explanation: This creates a public network entry point and does not satisfy the requirement for private connectivity.

choices.text: Connect both VPCs with inter-Region peering and add a route to the entire provider VPC CIDR in the consumer VPC.
choices.explanation: This does not limit connectivity to a single service and creates the broad network path that the requirement rules out.

learning.reason: The provider and consumer can use different Regions while connectivity remains limited to the endpoint service.
learning.concept: Approve the consumer Region in the PrivateLink endpoint service and create an endpoint

title: Designing Records for the Same Domain Used Publicly and Internally
prompt: The public zone for example.com contains app and docs. A private zone with the same name is associated with an internal VPC, and an internal address was added only for app. In the VPC, app resolves but docs returns NXDOMAIN. How can you make docs resolve internally without changing DNS for public users?

choices.text: Change app to the private IP address in the public zone and return the same public DNS information to internal and external clients.
choices.explanation: This changes the existing external record and does not meet the requirement to separate public and internal use.

choices.text: Define the required docs record in the private zone as well and specify the destination to use from inside the organization.
choices.explanation: When a query matches the associated private zone but no record is found, Route 53 does not search the public zone again; it returns NXDOMAIN.

choices.text: Disassociate the private zone from the VPC and keep app's internal address only in the internal zone configuration.
choices.explanation: Although docs could resolve publicly, the VPC could no longer use app's internal record after the association was removed.

choices.text: Shorten the TTL of the public docs record and wait for fallback to the public zone.
choices.explanation: Changing the TTL does not change the rule that the associated private zone takes precedence.

learning.reason: If a matching record is not found in the associated private zone, Route 53 returns NXDOMAIN instead of searching the public zone again.
learning.concept: A same-name private zone does not fall back to the public zone when a record is missing

title: Passing a Correlation ID to the Origin Without Fragmenting the Cache
prompt: CloudFront serves cacheable public content whose content does not vary based on the viewer's X-Trace-Id. You want to use the correlation ID in the origin logs only when a request is sent to the origin, without adding a cache key for each ID. Where should you add it?

choices.text: Add X-Trace-Id to the origin request policy, but not to the cache policy key.
choices.explanation: This separates headers sent to the origin from headers included in the cache key.

choices.text: Set X-Trace-Id as a cache policy key and exclude it from the origin request policy.
choices.explanation: A value included in the cache key is also included in the origin request, but the cache is fragmented by ID.

choices.text: Set X-Trace-Id only in the response headers policy and assume that the viewer header value reaches the origin.
choices.explanation: Response settings do not control forwarding request headers to the origin.

choices.text: Disable caching and send every request to the origin, leaving viewer headers at their defaults.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to retain caching and does not guarantee that the custom header is forwarded.

learning.reason: Headers sent to the origin can be separated from headers included in the cache key.
learning.concept: Add the header only to the origin request policy

title: Observe Test-Environment Packets Without Changing Routes
prompt: A network team is performing a vendor protocol validation in a test VPC it manages. In addition to flow aggregation, the team needs to send packets from an authorized test ENI to an analysis appliance. It must not switch routes to place the inspection device inline. What should the team use?

choices.text: Change the Transit Gateway routes to place the appliance inline with existing traffic.
choices.explanation: Inline inspection violates the requirement not to change the existing routes.

choices.text: Enable every VPC Flow Logs field and reconstruct packets from the aggregated records.
choices.explanation: Flow Logs record traffic metadata. The original packets are not included in each flow record.

choices.text: Send Route 53 Resolver query logs to the analysis device and obtain the contents of the target protocol traffic from the same logs.
choices.explanation: Resolver query logs record DNS queries and do not duplicate packets from other protocols.

choices.text: Configure Traffic Mirroring with the target ENI as the source and send copies of packets that pass the filter to the analysis target.
choices.explanation: Traffic Mirroring can duplicate packets for inspection without changing the application's forwarding route.

learning.reason: Traffic Mirroring can duplicate packets for inspection without changing the application's forwarding route.
learning.concept: Observe copies with Traffic Mirroring by using an ENI, a filter, and a target.

title: Match Name-Resolution Paths to Their Conditions
prompt: An environment connects on premises to AWS VPCs, and three types of name resolution must be designed. Select one function for the first function used on the AWS side or the function used to forward queries from the AWS side, as applicable. Use each candidate exactly once.

choices.text: A Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint
choices.explanation: It provides the entry point through which an on-premises DNS resolver forwards queries to the VPC.

choices.text: AmazonProvidedDNS in the VPC
choices.explanation: In a VPC associated with the hosted zone, it can resolve names in the zone without forwarding them to another network.

choices.text: A Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint associated with a forwarding rule
choices.explanation: It can forward queries for a specific namespace received in the VPC to on-premises DNS servers.

learning.reason: An inbound Resolver endpoint provides the entry point for on-premises DNS queries to the VPC. An outbound endpoint can forward queries for a specific namespace from the VPC to on-premises DNS servers. AmazonProvidedDNS resolves names in an associated hosted zone locally within the VPC.
learning.concept: Distinguish Resolver inbound and outbound paths across on-premises networks and VPCs from local resolution within a VPC.

prompts.text: On-premises DNS needs a connection point to resolve a private hosted zone associated with the VPC.
An application in the VPC resolves a name managed by on-premises authoritative DNS. Only that name is forwarded outside the VPC.
An application in the VPC looks up an A record in a zone associated with the same VPC. No DNS forwarding rule exists.

title: Separate Production and Development Routes Through Shared Infrastructure
prompt: A production VPC, a development VPC, and a shared-services VPC are connected to the same Transit Gateway. Production and development must each reach only the shared services, and return traffic to both is required. Which Transit Gateway configuration separates production from development?

choices.text: Add the shared VPC route to the spoke tables and register only the shared VPC route in the shared-services table.
choices.explanation: The outbound path works, but there are no return routes from the shared services to either spoke.

choices.text: Associate the production and development spokes with their respective tables and register only the shared VPC route in each; register routes to both spokes in the shared-services table.
choices.explanation: The tables used by the source attachments contain only the required destinations, while the shared-services side has return routes to both spokes.

choices.text: Associate all VPCs with the default table and propagate routes for all VPCs into the same table.
choices.explanation: This creates routes from every attachment to both production and development, so the required route isolation is not met.

choices.text: Add only the other VPC's route to each of the production and development tables.
choices.explanation: The required route to the shared VPC is missing, and a route to the VPC that should be isolated is present.

learning.reason: Place only the required destinations in the table used by each source attachment, and provide return routes from the shared-services side.
learning.concept: With a Transit Gateway, select route-table associations and destination-route propagation or registration independently.

title: Provide Only a TCP Service to VPCs with Overlapping Addresses
prompt: A business integration has increased the number of consumer VPCs with overlapping CIDR ranges. A shared VPC has one TCP service exposed through an existing NLB, and neither side can reassign its CIDR range. All VPCs are in the same Region. The provider must not initiate connections to consumers and must provide only the existing TCP service. How should each VPC use this service?

choices.text: Peer each consumer VPC directly with the shared VPC and add the overlapping CIDRs to the routes.
choices.explanation: VPC peering cannot be created with overlapping CIDRs, so this does not work under these conditions.

choices.text: Associate a private hosted zone containing an alias for the provider NLB with each consumer VPC, without adding connectivity between the VPCs.
choices.explanation: Name resolution for the NLB can be provided, but associating a name alone cannot establish a TCP connection when no path exists.

choices.text: Create an endpoint service that uses the existing NLB, and create the corresponding interface endpoint in each consumer VPC.
choices.explanation: Consumers reach the service through a local IP in their VPC, without exchanging routes for the entire provider VPC CIDR.

choices.text: Propagate all VPCs into the same Transit Gateway route table.
choices.explanation: Overlapping CIDRs cannot be treated as simultaneously effective propagated routes, and this does not isolate access at the service level.

learning.reason: Consumers connect to a local IP in their VPC to reach the service, so the entire provider VPC CIDR does not need to be exchanged.
learning.concept: A PrivateLink endpoint service connects interface endpoints in consumer VPCs to the provider's NLB.

title: Connecting an IPv6-only application to an IPv4-only dependency
prompt: An application in an IPv6-only subnet connects by name to an on-premises repository that has only an A record. The IPv4 route from the NAT gateway to the on-premises site is already configured, and the existing IPv6 routes must remain. Which settings are required? Choose two.

choices.text: Use only the NAT gateway and have the application continue using the IPv4 address returned from the A record as before.
choices.explanation: An IPv6-only client cannot use an IPv4 address directly; synthesis is required during name resolution.

choices.text: Do not use NAT; route the synthesized prefix to an egress-only IGW.
choices.explanation: An egress-only IGW controls IPv6 connectivity but does not translate the destination to IPv4.

choices.text: Add a route for 64:ff9b::/96 to the NAT gateway.
choices.explanation: This sends the synthesized destination for NAT64 processing so traffic can be forwarded to the IPv4-only dependency.

choices.text: Route only the application's 0.0.0.0/0 to NAT and do not add a route for the IPv6 synthesized address.
choices.explanation: The IPv6 packets actually sent by the application do not match the IPv4 route.

choices.text: Enable DNS64 in the application's subnet.
choices.explanation: This produces a synthesized AAAA response that the application can use from the A record of a destination that has only IPv4.

learning.reason: DNS64 can produce a synthesized AAAA response usable by the application from the A record of an IPv4-only destination, and the synthesized destination can be sent to NAT64 processing for forwarding to the IPv4 dependency.
learning.concept: DNS64 synthesis and a synthesized-prefix route to NAT64

title: A third VPC cannot be reached through two peering connections
prompt: A–B and B–C are each connected by peering, and their CIDR blocks do not overlap. You need to add private connectivity from A to C without adding a central gateway or transit router. What should you configure?

choices.text: Route traffic from A to C through A–B, route traffic from C to A through B–C, and forward the traffic between them in B's route tables.
choices.explanation: VPC peering does not allow traffic received from one peering connection to be forwarded through another peering connection.

choices.text: Create A–C peering and configure routes and permissions in both participating subnets.
choices.explanation: A and C become directly connected, so B does not need to be used as a transit VPC.

choices.text: Enable DNS resolution for each peering connection and consider the connection established if A can resolve C's private IP address.
choices.explanation: Resolving a private address does not create a transitive route between peering connections.

choices.text: Change the A–B route to a broad aggregate that includes C and leave the peering connection and routes on the C side unchanged.
choices.explanation: Aggregation does not allow traffic to be relayed through a peering connection to a VPC beyond the connected VPC.

learning.reason: A and C must be connected directly, without using B as a transit VPC.
learning.concept: Because VPC peering is nontransitive, peer A and C directly.

title: Use existing ALB URL routing behind PrivateLink
prompt: You need to expose an internal web service to a consumer VPC through PrivateLink while retaining the existing ALB's path-based rules and TLS termination. A new NLB can be placed in the same account and VPC as the ALB. Which integration is appropriate?

choices.text: Replicate the ALB's URL path rules on an NLB TCP listener and forward traffic directly from the NLB to each HTTP target.
choices.explanation: An NLB TCP listener does not evaluate HTTP URL path conditions.

choices.text: Select only the existing ALB as the load balancer for the endpoint service and accept the consumer's connections directly.
choices.explanation: This PrivateLink endpoint service is not exposed by using the existing ALB alone.

choices.text: Forward the NLB TCP listener to a target group of type alb that has the existing ALB registered.
choices.explanation: This makes the NLB the PrivateLink entry point while allowing the ALB to perform TLS termination and HTTP routing.

choices.text: Register the ALB's current resolved addresses once as IP targets on the NLB and continue using them when the ALB nodes change.
choices.explanation: ALB node IP addresses are not fixed registration targets. Using the target type for an ALB avoids managing node IP addresses.

learning.reason: The NLB can serve as the PrivateLink entry point while the ALB continues to perform TLS termination and HTTP routing.
learning.concept: Forward from an NLB TCP listener to a target group of type alb

title: Use separate certificates for different domains on the same ALB
prompt: Two public domains use port 443 on the same ALB. Their certificates must be managed separately, and all clients send TLS SNI. How can the ALB return the certificate matching the destination domain without adding another listener?

choices.text: Assign each target and certificate to an HTTP host-condition rule and have the certificate selected during routing.
choices.explanation: The TLS certificate is presented before HTTP rules are evaluated. Routing rules do not select certificates.

choices.text: Use one certificate containing both domains in its SAN as the default certificate for the HTTPS listener.
choices.explanation: This covers both domains with TLS, but it does not satisfy the requirement to manage and select two certificates independently.

choices.text: Use a separate TLS certificate for each target group and attach only the default certificate to the internet-facing listener.
choices.explanation: The target-side certificates are used between the ALB and the backends; they are not the certificates returned to viewers.

choices.text: Register each domain's certificate in the certificate list of the existing HTTPS listener.
choices.explanation: During TLS negotiation, the ALB can select the certificate that matches the SNI.

learning.reason: During TLS negotiation, the ALB can select the certificate matching the SNI.
learning.concept: Use the HTTPS listener certificate list and SNI to select the certificate presented

title: Associate a central private DNS zone with a VPC in another account
prompt: A private hosted zone is in a shared services account, while the application VPC is in a different account. The zone must not be duplicated and must be associated only with the application VPC. When using the Route 53 API, which division of responsibilities is correct? Select two.

choices.text: The application VPC owner creates the authorization for the zone itself, so no action is required from the zone owner.
choices.explanation: The account that owns the private hosted zone creates the authorization.

choices.text: The account that owns the VPC uses the authorization to associate the VPC with the zone.
choices.explanation: The association is performed from the VPC side, allowing the zone to be resolved from within the VPC.

choices.text: The account that owns the zone authorizes the association with the target VPC.
choices.explanation: The zone owner creates the authorization by specifying the VPC and Region.

choices.text: The zone owner creates only the authorization and considers the VPC association complete as soon as the notification is received.
choices.explanation: Creating the authorization and performing the actual association are separate operations.

choices.text: A tag with the same domain name as the zone is added to the VPC's subnets, and the zone is referenced when the tags match.
choices.explanation: Adding tags does not create an association between the VPC and the private zone.

learning.reason: The zone owner authorizes the VPC by specifying the VPC and Region. The VPC owner then performs the association so that the zone can be resolved from within the VPC.
learning.concept: The zone owner authorizes the VPC, and the VPC owner performs the association

title: Pass the original API path to a private backend
prompt: The prod stage of an API Gateway HTTP API reaches an existing internal ALB through a VPC Link. Clients continue to use the stage URL that includes prod, but the ALB expects /items as the backend route and returns 404 when the stage name is included. How should this be fixed without changing the clients?

choices.text: In the integration parameter mapping, overwrite the path sent to the backend with $request.path.
choices.explanation: This removes the stage name, which is added by default for a private integration, from the path sent to the backend.

choices.text: Rename the API route to /prod/items and leave the ALB rule unchanged.
choices.explanation: This changes the route used by clients and does not solve the stage-name issue added by the integration.

choices.text: Delete the client stage prod and move it to $default, then redirect users of the original URL during the next update.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement to preserve the clients' existing stage URL.

choices.text: Recreate the VPC Link with the same private subnets and reuse the permitted security group.
choices.explanation: The VPC Link network settings do not change the request path used by the integration.

learning.reason: The stage name added by default for a private integration can be removed from the path sent to the backend.
learning.concept: Specify $request.path in the HTTP API private integration parameter mapping

title: Use two VPN tunnels during normal operation
prompt: A site-to-site VPN to a TGW must distribute multiple flows for a particular site prefix across redundant tunnels. Both tunnels are under your control, and the site devices support equal-cost routes. What is required for distribution during normal operation, rather than only failover to a standby tunnel? Select two.

choices.text: Use dynamic routing for the VPN and maintain equivalent BGP attributes for the same destination on both tunnels.
choices.explanation: Static VPNs cannot use ECMP. The BGP preference conditions must also match so that multiple paths remain candidates.

choices.text: Enable VPN ECMP support on the Transit Gateway.
choices.explanation: The TGW can use multiple qualifying VPN paths at equal cost.

choices.text: Make the AS_PATH longer on one tunnel to establish a preference for the primary tunnel.
choices.explanation: Paths with different preferences do not meet the requirement for equal-cost distribution.

choices.text: Create a static route in the TGW route table pointing to one tunnel and learn the other route dynamically.
choices.explanation: A static route that gives one tunnel priority does not provide matching equal-cost dynamic paths.

choices.text: Replace the VPN termination with a Virtual Private Gateway and use ECMP with the same configuration.
choices.explanation: AWS Site-to-Site VPN ECMP is used with a TGW configuration.

learning.reason: The TGW can use multiple qualifying VPN paths at equal cost. Static VPNs cannot use ECMP, so BGP preference conditions must also match to make multiple paths candidates.
learning.concept: Combine TGW VPN ECMP with equivalent BGP paths

title: An EC2 router specified in a subnet route cannot forward traffic
prompt: An EC2 router under test in a VPC has OS forwarding enabled, and the subnet route points to the router's ENI. The security group and network ACL allow the test flow. Packets addressed to the EC2 instance itself arrive, but packets that it should forward to another host are not forwarded. What should be checked on the EC2 instance?

choices.text: Point the existing default route to the IGW and process in-transit VPC traffic through the same exit.
choices.explanation: This does not resolve the cause of the EC2 router's forwarding failure and would remove the existing in-transit VPC path.

choices.text: Disable source/destination checking on the router.
choices.explanation: A normal EC2 instance is configured to handle traffic for which it is the source or destination; an explicitly configured intermediary must have this check disabled to forward traffic.

choices.text: Replace the destination IP of every packet forwarded by the router with the router's own IP and configure no return path.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve the destination required of a normal router and cannot establish bidirectional communication.

choices.text: Assign the IP address of every forwarding target as a secondary address on the router's ENI and retain the same IP on each host.
choices.explanation: This assigns the same destination addresses to different ENIs and does not enable forwarding.

learning.reason: A normal EC2 instance is configured to handle traffic for which it is the source or destination, so an explicitly configured intermediary must have source/destination checking disabled to forward traffic.
learning.concept: Disable source/destination checking only on an EC2 instance acting as a router

title: Using the Same Physical AZ from Different Accounts with Shared Subnets
prompt: The network owner account and the application account map Availability Zone names to physical Availability Zones differently within the same Region. To ensure that a related resource in another account is placed in the same physical Availability Zone as the shared subnet's resources, what should be matched?

choices.text: Match the endings of the subnet CIDRs for both resources and assume that they are assigned to the same physical Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: The physical Availability Zone cannot be determined from a subnet's address range.

choices.text: Select the Availability Zone whose name ends in a in the same Region in both accounts.
choices.explanation: Because Availability Zone name assignments differ, the same suffix does not identify the same physical location.

choices.text: Create IAM roles with the same name in both accounts and use AWS RAM sharing to align the Availability Zone names.
choices.explanation: IAM role names and sharing settings do not change the mapping of Availability Zone names between accounts.

choices.text: Match the shared subnet's AZ ID with the ID of the Availability Zone selected for deployment.
choices.explanation: An AZ ID identifies the physical zone consistently across accounts. Display names can differ between accounts.

learning.reason: An AZ ID identifies the physical zone consistently across accounts. Display names can differ between accounts.
learning.concept: Use an AZ ID to identify a physical zone across accounts

title: Automatically Deploying a Network Baseline to New Accounts
prompt: Deploy audit VPC Flow Logs and related template resources to a specified OU in the same organization. The deployment must cover both existing and future members, and the operation should avoid manually creating execution roles or stacks in each account. Which implementation is appropriate?

choices.text: Use trusted access in Organizations to deploy a service-managed StackSet to the target OU and enable automatic deployment.
choices.explanation: The same template can be deployed to new accounts added to the OU with the required permissions prepared automatically.

choices.text: Create a self-managed StackSet and manually register an execution role in each member account.
choices.explanation: This can deploy to existing accounts, but it does not automate the required role creation and deployment to new accounts.

choices.text: Apply an SCP to the target OU to restrict changes to Flow Logs and use the SCP to create VPC resources that do not yet exist.
choices.explanation: An SCP controls which operations are permitted, but it does not execute the process that creates template resources.

choices.text: Create only one ordinary CloudFormation stack in the management account and assume that its resources will be created separately in each account.
choices.explanation: Creating an ordinary stack alone does not deploy the same resources to member accounts.

learning.reason: The same template can be deployed to new accounts added to the OU with the required permissions prepared automatically.
learning.concept: Specify an OU for a service-managed StackSets deployment and enable automatic deployment

title: Keeping S3's Standard Name While Separating VPC and Site Connectivity
prompt: Both the VPC and the on-premises environment use the same S3 Regional API name. The VPC must use a gateway endpoint without data-processing charges, while the site must connect from an inbound Resolver endpoint to the private IP address of an interface endpoint. Both endpoints are already available. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Enable private DNS for the S3 interface endpoint only for the inbound Resolver.
choices.explanation: The site can use the interface endpoint's private IP address, while clients in the VPC can use the gateway endpoint's route through the same service name.

choices.text: Enable the interface endpoint's private DNS universally, including name resolution within the VPC.
choices.explanation: This would direct VPC clients to the interface endpoint and would not meet the requirement to use the gateway endpoint.

choices.text: Delete the interface endpoint and configure the on-premises environment to use the gateway endpoint as its forwarding destination.
choices.explanation: An S3 gateway endpoint does not provide a private IP address for connections from an on-premises environment.

choices.text: Standardize on an interface-endpoint-specific DNS name and update all VPC and site clients.
choices.explanation: This would not preserve the standard API name, and VPC clients would also use the interface endpoint.

learning.reason: The site can use the interface endpoint's private IP address, while clients in the VPC can use the gateway endpoint's route through the same service name.
learning.concept: Apply interface endpoint private DNS only to the inbound Resolver

title: Validating Client Certificates at Targets Behind an NLB
prompt: A partner service uses an NLB as its TCP entry point. An existing application server is responsible for validating client certificates, and the TLS session must remain established all the way to that server. Which listener should be used on the NLB?

choices.text: A TCP listener on port 443 that forwards the TLS connection unchanged to the application server.
choices.explanation: Because TLS terminates at the backend, the existing mechanism can validate the client certificate.

choices.text: Terminate TLS at the NLB and use TLS for the target group, assuming that the original client certificate will reach the server.
choices.explanation: The two TLS connections are separate, so the client's original TLS session is not preserved to the application.

choices.text: Create a TLS listener on the NLB, validate the certificate at the NLB, and pass the same TLS session to the application.
choices.explanation: An NLB TLS listener terminates TLS and does not provide mTLS at the NLB.

choices.text: Switch to a UDP listener on port 443 and have the existing TCP clients use the same certificates.
choices.explanation: An existing TLS protocol over TCP cannot be accepted unchanged through a UDP configuration.

learning.reason: Because TLS terminates at the backend, the existing mechanism can validate the client certificate.
learning.concept: Use an NLB TCP listener to pass TLS through transparently to the target

title: Implement ALB forwarding and health checks for a gRPC service
prompt: A gRPC microservice is exposed through an ALB. The nodes implement a gRPC health method and return gRPC code 0 when healthy. You want health to be evaluated using that RPC code rather than HTTP 200. What should you configure?

choices.text: Periodically verify only reachability of the TCP port from the ALB, without evaluating the RPC response code.
choices.explanation: TCP reachability alone does not verify that the application responds successfully to the specified RPC.

choices.text: Set HTTP 200 as the target group's success code so that it is automatically treated as equivalent to gRPC 0.
choices.explanation: A gRPC health check evaluates a gRPC code. An HTTP value does not represent success for the specified RPC.

choices.text: Forward from an HTTPS listener to a target group with the gRPC protocol version, and specify the health method and success code 0.
choices.explanation: The ALB can call the gRPC RPC path and determine health from the response's gRPC code.

choices.text: Use HTTP/1.1 for the target connection and consider only HTTP 200 successful regardless of the gRPC status.
choices.explanation: An HTTP status does not have the same meaning as the RPC processing success code.

learning.reason: The ALB can call the gRPC RPC path and determine health from the response's gRPC code.
learning.concept: The gRPC target protocol and the health-check method and success code

title: Map Direct Connect virtual interfaces to services
prompt: Assign the appropriate type of virtual interface to each of three requirements that use the same Direct Connect connection. Each candidate can be used only once.

choices.text: Transit virtual interface
choices.explanation: Used to connect to a Transit Gateway through a Direct Connect Gateway.

choices.text: Private virtual interface
choices.explanation: Targets a VPC's virtual private gateway and provides access to the VPC using private IP addresses.

choices.text: Public virtual interface
choices.explanation: Used to reach public IP addresses of AWS public services such as S3.

learning.reason: A public virtual interface reaches public IP addresses of AWS public services such as S3. A private virtual interface targets a VPC's virtual private gateway and reaches the VPC using private IP addresses. A transit virtual interface connects to a Transit Gateway through a Direct Connect Gateway.
learning.concept: The type of VIF determines the Direct Connect destination and the resources that can be reached.

prompts.text: Access the public IP address of an AWS S3 public endpoint from on premises.
Connect directly to an existing virtual private gateway without using a Transit Gateway.
Connect to multiple VPCs through a Transit Gateway associated with a Direct Connect Gateway.

title: Deliver BGP-learned routes to an application's subnet
prompt: A Site-to-Site VPN terminates on a virtual private gateway, and the customer gateway can advertise on-premises prefixes through BGP. Existing subnets are reachable, but the dedicated route table for a new subnet has no route to the corporate network. Which action will reflect future advertisement changes without manually registering them?

choices.text: Add the corporate CIDR as a destination in the application's security group's outbound rules.
choices.explanation: Adjusting a traffic filter does not create destination routes in a route table.

choices.text: Register only the current corporate CIDR statically with the virtual private gateway as the target.
choices.explanation: This configures the current route, but static routes must be updated when new BGP advertisements are received.

choices.text: Have the customer gateway re-advertise the VPC's BGP routes.
choices.explanation: The VPC route table needs information about destinations in the on-premises network; this action also does not enable propagation to the route table.

choices.text: Enable route propagation from the virtual private gateway in the VPC route table for the new subnet.
choices.explanation: This reflects the routes currently learned by the VPN and their updates in the route table used by the subnet.

learning.reason: This reflects the routes currently learned by the VPN and their updates in the route table used by the subnet.
learning.concept: VPN routes from a virtual private gateway are received by enabling propagation in the target VPC route table.

title: Resolve one-way access failure through an interface endpoint over VPN
prompt: The private IP address of an S3 interface endpoint is resolved correctly by a backup appliance at the other end of a VPN connection. Clients in the same VPC can connect, and the return route for the corporate CIDR and the network ACL have been verified, but the endpoint ENI's security group allows HTTPS 443 only from the VPC CIDR. What should be changed?

choices.text: Add a rule to the endpoint ENI's security group allowing TCP 443 from the CIDR of the authorized on-premises backup appliance.
choices.explanation: The on-premises source is not within the VPC CIDR, so explicitly allowing it on the port accepted by the endpoint enables connectivity.

choices.text: Add permission for the corporate CIDR to the S3 bucket policy.
choices.explanation: A bucket policy affects evaluation of S3 requests; it cannot establish a connection that is blocked by the security group first.

choices.text: Add an S3 gateway endpoint to the VPC route table.
choices.explanation: This does not change the security-group evaluation for traffic addressed to the existing interface endpoint.

choices.text: Add only an outbound TCP 443 rule for the backup appliance to the endpoint's security group.
choices.explanation: For a connection initiated by the client, the missing permission is inbound access to the destination endpoint.

learning.reason: The on-premises source is not within the VPC CIDR, so explicitly allowing it on the port accepted by the endpoint enables connectivity.
learning.concept: Allow inbound connections from the source in the interface endpoint's security group.

title: Concentrating AWS-bound and on-premises traffic on the same primary circuit
prompt: Two private VIFs, a primary and a standby, are operated on a Direct Connect connection in the same Region. AWS receives the same prefixes over both VIFs, and the on-premises CIDR is advertised from both sides with the same prefix length. You can configure the on-premises Local Preference for traffic destined for AWS, and AWS evaluates both routes toward the on-premises network with the same AWS Local Preference. Select two actions that direct traffic to the primary VIF in both directions during normal operation.

choices.text: Prepend the AS_PATH for the on-premises CIDR advertised from the primary VIF to AWS.
choices.explanation: When AWS assigns the same Local Preference to both routes, it will prefer the shorter AS_PATH on the standby path.

choices.text: Prepend the AS_PATH when advertising the on-premises CIDR from the standby VIF to AWS.
choices.explanation: When AWS assigns the same Local Preference to both routes, the shorter AS_PATH on the primary path can be preferred over the standby path.

choices.text: Stop the BGP session on the standby VIF.
choices.explanation: This separates the paths during normal operation, but removes the always-available standby route.

choices.text: Set a higher Local Preference on premises for AWS prefixes received from the primary VIF.
choices.explanation: The on-premises routers will prefer the primary exit when selecting a route.

choices.text: Set a higher Local Preference for the standby path received on premises.
choices.explanation: The on-premises routers would send traffic to AWS over the standby path, which is the opposite of the normal-operation requirement.

learning.reason: Use different route attributes for selecting the local exit and for advertising routes to the peer. A higher on-premises Local Preference selects the primary exit, while equal AWS Local Preference lets the shorter primary AS_PATH win after prepending the standby AS_PATH.
learning.concept: The attributes evaluated for local exit selection differ from those evaluated by the peer for routes you advertise.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Identifying the blocking point after a configuration change
prompt: The network team changed the route tables and security groups. After the change, TCP 8443 connectivity between two EC2 instances fails. You can inspect the IAM permissions of both ENIs and the VPC configuration, but logging in to the instances and sending test packets are prohibited. Which option identifies the path and the first blocking factor to check?

choices.text: Mirror both ENIs with VPC Traffic Mirroring and inspect the connection attempts.
choices.explanation: This duplicates existing packets; if no traffic is sent, the blocking point cannot be determined from the configuration alone.

choices.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs on both ENIs and read records for new connections.
choices.explanation: Because the target traffic cannot be sent during the permitted observation period, no new records for that traffic will be created.

choices.text: Probe the pair of ENIs with CloudWatch Network Monitor and wait for the result.
choices.explanation: This requires an active probe and is not intended to determine blocking by components in the VPC configuration.

choices.text: Run Reachability Analyzer with both ENIs and TCP 8443 specified.
choices.explanation: It statically analyzes routes and filters and identifies the path or the configuration component that blocks it.

learning.reason: Reachability Analyzer can statically analyze routes and filters and identify the path or configuration component that blocks the specified traffic.
learning.concept: Reachability Analyzer analyzes a specified path from the VPC configuration model.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Identifying original sources passing through a shared NAT gateway
prompt: Several applications share one NAT gateway. In Internet-bound records recorded at the NAT ENI, the default srcaddr field cannot distinguish the applications. Which option lets you continue collecting records at the NAT ENI and correlate the original source with the amount of traffic?

choices.text: Collect interface-id and bytes, then aggregate by interface.
choices.explanation: The observation point is the common NAT ENI, so applications cannot be distinguished within the same interface.

choices.text: Include pkt-dstaddr and bytes, then assign the source application by destination.
choices.explanation: Applications using the same external API cannot be uniquely distinguished by the destination IP.

choices.text: Recreate the records with srcaddr and bytes, then group only by srcaddr.
choices.explanation: The srcaddr representing the observed NAT ENI groups multiple applications under the same value.

choices.text: Include pkt-srcaddr and bytes in a custom format, then aggregate by the applications' private IP addresses.
choices.explanation: Packet-level address observation distinguishes the original source from the address of the transit ENI.

learning.reason: Observe the address field at the packet level to distinguish the original source from the address of the transit ENI.
learning.concept: pkt-srcaddr distinguishes the packet's original source through observation at an intermediate network layer.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Measuring VIF imbalance when the physical connection is healthy
prompt: A single Direct Connect connection has two virtual interfaces. ConnectionState is UP, and the optical levels show no variation. After a migration, you want to determine whether traffic from AWS to the site is concentrated on one VIF more than expected. Which metrics should you compare?

choices.text: Compare ConnectionBpsEgress by connection ID.
choices.explanation: This aggregates the entire connection and cannot identify imbalance between the two VIFs on the same connection.

choices.text: Compare VirtualInterfaceBpsEgress by VirtualInterfaceId.
choices.explanation: Even when the VIFs share one physical connection, this separates the bit rate sent from AWS to each VIF.

choices.text: Compare VirtualInterfaceBpsIngress by VirtualInterfaceId.
choices.explanation: This is a VIF-level metric, but it counts traffic received by AWS, which is the opposite direction from the traffic being checked.

choices.text: Compare the increase in ConnectionErrorCount.
choices.explanation: This counts connection errors and does not show how much error-free traffic flowed through each VIF.

learning.reason: This separates the bit rate sent from AWS to each VIF even when both share one physical connection.
learning.concept: VirtualInterfaceBpsEgress represents the AWS-side outgoing bit rate for each VIF.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Investigating a Tunnel Failure at the IKE Stage
prompt: After updating an on-premises device, one IPsec tunnel of an AWS Site-to-Site VPN does not come up. TunnelState shows 0. You want to use evidence from the AWS side to determine at which IKE or IPsec negotiation stage the failure occurs. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Search AWS CloudTrail for the history of DescribeVpnConnections calls.
choices.explanation: This can show API calls, but it does not record the tunnel negotiation stage at either endpoint.

choices.text: Change TunnelState to the minimum statistic and determine the IKE phase from the samples.
choices.explanation: Changing the statistic does not add information about the negotiation stage.

choices.text: Deliver VPN logs for the affected tunnel to CloudWatch Logs and inspect the negotiation states and errors.
choices.explanation: The IKE phases and IPsec negotiation messages allow investigation beyond a simple up-or-down status.

choices.text: Aggregate the IKE phases by the action in VPC Flow Logs.
choices.explanation: This field indicates whether traffic was accepted or rejected; it does not represent negotiation states processed by the VPN service.

learning.reason: The IKE phases and IPsec negotiation messages allow investigation beyond a simple up-or-down status.
learning.concept: CloudWatch Logs for VPN tunnels record IKE and IPsec negotiation states and errors.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Only Large TCP Transfers Stop
prompt: With Site-to-Site VPN, short HTTPS requests succeed, but a large transfer on the same connection stops. The router on the intermediate path cannot be changed, but the TCP settings on the customer gateway under your control can be changed. The issue started immediately after the IPsec encryption method was changed. Which option fits TCP's outgoing segments within the tunnel's effective size?

choices.text: Always enable NAT traversal and leave the TCP settings unchanged.
choices.explanation: NAT-T uses UDP encapsulation to traverse NAT; it is not a substitute for an MSS derived from the effective MTU.

choices.text: Standardize the ENIs of the VPC-side EC2 instances on jumbo frames.
choices.explanation: Increasing the MTU inside the VPC does not reduce the segment size that fits through the IPsec path.

choices.text: Shorten the BGP Keepalive interval and Hold Time.
choices.explanation: These settings change route-failure detection, not the TCP segment length.

choices.text: Confirm the value for the selected IPsec method and adjust TCP MSS on the customer gateway.
choices.explanation: Accounting for encapsulation overhead limits the TCP data size and addresses the cause of only the large segments being lost.

learning.reason: Accounting for encapsulation overhead limits the TCP data size and addresses the cause of only the large segments being lost.
learning.concept: AWS provides effective MTU and TCP MSS values for VPN encryption methods.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: An Aggregation That Underreports the Number of Queries
prompt: An application in a VPC looked up one name 200 times in a short period. The application counts each DNS request it sends, but the Route 53 Resolver query logs show only the first query for each TTL period. Before proceeding with an investigation based on missing data, which explanation should you adopt?

choices.text: Aggregate the number of VPC Flow Logs packets by name.
choices.explanation: There are restrictions on traffic to the Amazon-provided DNS server, and this would not count queries by DNS name.

choices.text: Switch to authoritative DNS logs; all Resolver cache hits will then appear.
choices.explanation: As long as the response comes from the cache, no query is sent to the authoritative DNS server.

choices.text: Queries served from the Resolver cache are not logged, so derive the total number of requests from the application's measurements.
choices.explanation: Repeated lookups for the same name do not create log lines while the cache entry is valid, explaining why the source totals do not match.

choices.text: Increase the CloudWatch Logs retention period to restore the lines that were sampled out.
choices.explanation: Retention applies to logs that were received; it cannot restore lines that Resolver did not send.

learning.reason: Repeated lookups for the same name do not create log lines while the cache entry is valid, explaining why the source totals do not match.
learning.concept: Responses handled by the Resolver cache are not recorded by Query Logging.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Measuring Errors Caused by the Load Balancer
prompt: HTTP 5xx errors have increased for a service behind an ALB. No corresponding errors are visible on the backend. You want to first use CloudWatch to determine whether the ALB itself has returned more 5xx errors. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Use the maximum TargetResponseTime value and count slow responses.
choices.explanation: This measures the time until a response begins, but it cannot identify the number of 5xx errors generated by the ALB.

choices.text: Use the minimum HealthyHostCount value and count the decrease in hosts judged healthy.
choices.explanation: Health-check status does not show the number of HTTP status codes generated by the ALB itself.

choices.text: Check the Sum of HTTPCode_ELB_5XX_Count for the load balancer.
choices.explanation: This counts 5xx errors generated by the ALB; 5xx errors originating from target responses are counted separately.

choices.text: Check the Sum of HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count for the target group.
choices.explanation: This counts 5xx errors generated by the backend for requests that were successfully forwarded.

learning.reason: This counts 5xx errors generated by the ALB; 5xx errors originating from target responses are counted separately.
learning.concept: 5xx errors generated by the ALB and 5xx errors returned by targets are monitored with separate metrics.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Temporarily bypassing a failure isolated to one Availability Zone
prompt: An application is being served by an ALB across three Availability Zones. Zonal shift integration and cross-zone load balancing are enabled, and the remaining two Availability Zones have enough capacity to handle all traffic. Because an unidentified failure continues in one Availability Zone, you want to stop new forwarding for only 30 minutes from the ALB's zone-specific entry point and from targets in the impaired Availability Zone. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Deregister all targets in the impaired Availability Zone from the ALB target group.
choices.explanation: This removes the targets, but it does not automatically withdraw the zone-specific ALB entry point from DNS and restore it when the time limit expires.

choices.text: Configure primary and secondary failover for the ALB alias in Route 53.
choices.explanation: This selects a DNS failover destination for the ALB as a whole; it does not temporarily drain traffic from a specific Availability Zone within the same ALB.

choices.text: Reduce only the failure threshold for the ALB health checks.
choices.explanation: This changes how individual targets are evaluated; it does not perform a time-limited evacuation of a specific Availability Zone.

choices.text: Start a 30-minute ARC zonal shift for the impaired Availability Zone on the ALB resource.
choices.explanation: This moves traffic away from the impaired Availability Zone and restores the Availability Zone when the expiration time is reached. Existing connections may take time to terminate.

learning.reason: Traffic is moved away from the impaired Availability Zone and the Availability Zone is restored when the expiration time is reached. Existing connections may take time to terminate.
learning.concept: An ARC zonal shift temporarily removes a specified Availability Zone from a load-balancing resource.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Directly monitoring an internal endpoint from a VPC
prompt: Using Route 53, you want to directly health check a private IPv4 internal HTTPS endpoint in a VPC in the same account. Publishing it externally and using custom CloudWatch alarms are prohibited, and you can reserve subnets in three Availability Zones for the checks. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Redo the association between the existing private hosted zone and the VPC.
choices.explanation: This changes private name resolution; it does not directly health check the endpoint.

choices.text: Enter the same private IPv4 address in an HTTPS health check for a public endpoint.
choices.explanation: Public endpoint checks and private endpoint checks differ in their monitoring source and reachability requirements.

choices.text: Create a health check source that uses three Availability Zones in the target VPC, configure its security group, and use that source for an HTTPS health check of the private endpoint.
choices.explanation: The health check source defines the probe origins within the VPC, and the check specifies the private address over HTTPS.

choices.text: Determine the HTTPS status from a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint.
choices.explanation: A Resolver endpoint handles DNS query input and output; it does not send HTTPS probes to the target application.

learning.reason: The probe origins within the VPC are defined by a health check source, and the check specifies the private address over HTTPS.
learning.concept: A private endpoint health check uses a health check source connected to subnets in three Availability Zones.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Stopping only new traffic to a Region
prompt: A single standard Global Accelerator receives production traffic for multiple Regions. You want to move new connections to another Region while maintaining existing connections in the Region undergoing maintenance. The other Regions on the same listener have healthy endpoints and sufficient capacity. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Remove the service port from the relevant listener of the accelerator.
choices.explanation: The listener is used across Regions, so healthy Regions would also stop accepting new connections on the same port.

choices.text: Set the traffic dial to 0 in the endpoint group for the Region being maintained.
choices.explanation: This drains new traffic destined for that endpoint group. Changing the dial does not terminate existing connections.

choices.text: Delete the endpoints in the target Region and register them again after maintenance.
choices.explanation: Deleting endpoints is not an operation for maintaining existing connections. A traffic dial affects only new connections while keeping the endpoints registered.

choices.text: Delete only the maintenance Region's DNS record for the accelerator in Route 53.
choices.explanation: Because a shared accelerator is used, its record does not identify individual backend Regions.

learning.reason: New traffic destined for the endpoint group is drained. Changing the traffic dial does not terminate existing connections.
learning.concept: A traffic dial affects new traffic to an endpoint group.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Immediately observing only a problematic cache behavior
prompt: A CloudFront user is currently reporting errors on a specific API path. From the target cache behavior, you want to stream-analyze a 10% sample of selected fields at intervals of a few seconds. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Filter the API user's specified path in the AWS CloudTrail event history.
choices.explanation: This is an operation history for CloudFront management APIs, not real-time logs of delivery requests.

choices.text: Associate a real-time log configuration with a 10% sampling rate with the target behavior and send the logs to Kinesis Data Streams.
choices.explanation: You can specify the sampling rate, fields, scope, and immediate streaming delivery.

choices.text: Choose S3 delivery for CloudFront standard access logs and filter the target path afterward.
choices.explanation: The path can be filtered after output, but this does not provide streaming delivery at the configured rate on a seconds-level interval.

choices.text: Stream the 5xxErrorRate metric using CloudFront CloudWatch metrics.
choices.explanation: This is an aggregate value and does not provide selected request-level fields or samples.

learning.reason: The sampling rate, fields, scope, and immediate streaming delivery can be specified.
learning.concept: CloudFront real-time logs can be configured per behavior and delivered to Kinesis Data Streams.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Planned failover test for only the specified VIF
prompt: During regular training for redundant Direct Connect paths, you want to stop BGP on only one private VIF during an approved maintenance window and verify that traffic switches to the other VIF. The other VIF on the same physical connection and the connection itself must remain available. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Start a Direct Connect failover test on the target VIF and verify connectivity through the backup path.
choices.explanation: This stops BGP for the target VIF during the test without requiring the other VIF to be taken down at the same time.

choices.text: Start the failover test first on the backup VIF.
choices.explanation: This stops the standby path, so it does not verify that traffic switches to the standby path when the active path is stopped.

choices.text: Disable the physical port on the router hosting the target VIF.
choices.explanation: Other VIFs using the same physical connection would also be affected, so the failure scope would not be limited.

choices.text: Adjust the threshold of the primary VIF's CloudWatch alarm to put the alarm into an alarm state.
choices.explanation: This can test monitoring notifications, but it does not withdraw the BGP path or verify that production traffic is rerouted.

learning.reason: BGP for the target VIF is stopped during the test window, so the other VIFs do not need to be taken down at the same time.
learning.concept: A Direct Connect Resiliency Toolkit failover test temporarily stops BGP for the target VIF.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Preferred TGW path when the same prefix is received
prompt: The same destination CIDR is propagated by BGP from a Direct Connect Gateway and a Site-to-Site VPN to a Transit Gateway. Both routes are processed in the same TGW route table, and there is no static route or more-specific match for the CIDR. Which path is used for forwarding during normal operation, and which path is used after the dedicated-link BGP route is withdrawn?
