choices.text: The Direct Connect Gateway is preferred during normal operation, and the VPN path is used when that propagation disappears.
choices.explanation: For the same CIDR, the Direct Connect Gateway propagation is preferred; after it is withdrawn, traffic moves to the available VPN propagation.

choices.text: The VPN is always preferred, and traffic moves to the Direct Connect Gateway only when the VPN goes down.
choices.explanation: This reverses the device-type priority for propagated routes with the same CIDR.

choices.text: The Direct Connect Gateway is preferred, and the VPN is not used after withdrawal until a route is registered manually.
choices.explanation: When another usable BGP propagation exists in the same table, traffic does not remain dependent on the withdrawn dedicated-link route.

choices.text: Both paths are used as ECMP during normal operation, and only the VPN path remains after withdrawal.
choices.explanation: This combination of different attachment types does not cause the TGW to use the routes as ECMP.

learning.reason: For the same CIDR, the Direct Connect Gateway propagation is preferred; after it is withdrawn, traffic moves to the available VPN propagation.
learning.concept: A TGW applies device-type priority to propagated routes for the same destination.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Scaling appliances while maintaining transparent inspection
prompt: You need to transparently inspect outbound IP traffic from multiple VPCs. The inspection appliances support GENEVE, and you must inspect the source and destination IP addresses. Which approach provides a route-based entry point in each VPC while allowing appliances to be added or replaced based on health?

choices.text: Register the inspection appliances with an NLB TCP listener and specify the NLB DNS name as the subnet's default route.
choices.explanation: A subnet route cannot specify an NLB DNS name, and this does not provide a transparent inspection path for arbitrary IP traffic.

choices.text: Receive HTTP and HTTPS traffic with an ALB listener and distribute it to each appliance based on the host header.
choices.explanation: Listener conditions for HTTP cannot provide network-layer inspection for arbitrary IP traffic.

choices.text: Register the inspection appliances with a Gateway Load Balancer and direct subnet routes in each VPC to a GWLBE.
choices.explanation: The GWLBE provides the route entry point, and the GWLB can transparently forward traffic to GENEVE-capable targets.

choices.text: Use Traffic Mirroring to deliver copies to the inspection appliances and send only copies that pass inspection to the destination.
choices.explanation: Mirroring provides observational copies; it is not a path that synchronously permits or blocks the original traffic.

learning.reason: The GWLBE provides the route entry point, and the GWLB can transparently forward traffic to GENEVE-capable targets.
learning.concept: A Gateway Load Balancer forwards traffic to virtual appliances using GENEVE, and its endpoint can be specified in routes.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Do not infer rejected packets from flow-log counts
prompt: You are investigating traffic that passes through AWS Network Firewall. A suspicious flow is configured to be dropped first by a stateless rule, and it does not appear at all in the Network Firewall flow logs for the same time. Which explanation is appropriate?

choices.text: Traffic dropped by the stateless engine does not reach the stateful engine, so it cannot be seen in those flow logs.
choices.explanation: Firewall logs are recorded from the stateful engine, and the packet is outside the processing scope of those logs.

choices.text: Changing the destination from S3 to CloudWatch Logs makes drops by the stateless engine visible.
choices.explanation: Changing the destination does not change the processing scope for which logs are generated.

choices.text: Adding a stateful alert log records the same stateless drop.
choices.explanation: Logs from stateful alert rules also require the packet to reach the stateful engine.

choices.text: Because flow logs record drops from both engines, the packet never reached the firewall.
choices.explanation: The premise about the log scope is incorrect; the absence of a log entry alone does not establish that the packet never reached the firewall.

learning.reason: Firewall logs cover packets forwarded to the stateful engine, so the target packet is outside the logs' processing scope.
learning.concept: Network Firewall flow logs cover packets forwarded to the stateful engine.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Apply source-IP limits only to login requests
prompt: An application on a public ALB needs to reduce concentrated login requests. Without including usage of other paths in the limit calculation, apply a temporary request-rate limit to only POST /login for each client IP. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Use an AWS WAF rate-based rule with the IP address as the aggregation key, and narrow the method and URI path with a scope-down statement.
choices.explanation: Only matching POST /login requests become evaluation candidates, and the request count is evaluated per IP within that scope.

choices.text: Use a rate-based rule that aggregates GET and POST under one constant key.
choices.explanation: A constant key cannot evaluate request counts per user IP, and it does not satisfy the method requirement.

choices.text: Create a Block rule that uses only a string match for POST /login.
choices.explanation: It blocks requests from the first matching POST /login request, so it does not limit requests based on the number sent by one IP.

choices.text: Apply an IP-based rate-based rule to all paths and use a separate Count rule to measure POST /login requests.
choices.explanation: The aggregation scope of the rate-based rule is not narrowed, so other paths are included in the count used for limiting.

learning.reason: Only matching POST /login requests become evaluation candidates, and the request count is evaluated per IP within that scope.
learning.concept: An AWS WAF rate-based rule can specify both an aggregation key and a narrowed evaluation scope.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Observe automatic L7 mitigation before blocking
prompt: An ALB protected by Shield Advanced has an associated Web ACL. The security team wants to test automatic mitigation for attack patterns detected by Shield. Until the team reviews the results, it wants to measure only matches from automatically generated custom mitigation rules. Existing protection must remain in place. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Set the action for automatic application-layer DDoS mitigation to Block and set the Web ACL default action to Allow.
choices.explanation: The matching Block rule is processed before the default Allow action, so requests may be blocked.

choices.text: Remove Shield protection and aggregate the Web ACL capacity usage.
choices.explanation: A WAF capacity metric does not observe request matches, and this does not test mitigation managed automatically by Shield.

choices.text: Leave automatic mitigation disabled and enable anomaly detection in the ALB target group.
choices.explanation: Observing backend anomalies is separate from verifying the behavior of Shield's application-layer defense rules.

choices.text: Enable automatic application-layer DDoS mitigation for the protected resource and set its action to Count.
choices.explanation: This observes matches from Shield-managed protection without blocking requests through the action of the automatic mitigation.

learning.reason: This observes matches from Shield-managed protection without blocking requests through the action of the automatic mitigation.
learning.concept: Shield Advanced automatic application-layer mitigation supports Count and Block actions.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Report deviations from an organization-defined allowlist
prompt: Existing security groups in a specific OU within an organization must be inspected. Report rules that exceed the organization-specified CIDR and port ranges, without changing the membership or rule contents of the existing security groups. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Share the reference security group with all members using AWS RAM.
choices.explanation: Sharing grants access but does not compare existing security groups and report violations.

choices.text: Run Reachability Analyzer once in each VPC and compare the full range of allowed rules.
choices.explanation: Reachability Analyzer analyzes a specified path; it does not audit an OU's security-group rules by comparing them with a reference security group.

choices.text: Create a custom security-group-content audit policy in Firewall Manager, specify the reference security group as the allowed range, and disable automatic remediation.
choices.explanation: This detects rules outside the specified range in the target OU and uses the reference security group without associating it with production resources.

choices.text: Use a common security-group policy in Firewall Manager to automatically associate the same security group with existing target resources.
choices.explanation: Automatic association under a common policy changes resources and is not limited to comparing each current rule with the reference range.

learning.reason: This detects rules outside the specified range in the target OU and uses the reference security group without associating it with production resources.
learning.concept: Firewall Manager content auditing can compare the rules in a reference security group with those in target security groups.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Complete the trust chain after signing a child zone
prompt: DNSSEC signing has been enabled for a public Route 53 hosted zone, and the key-signing key is Active. The authoritative servers show that signing is working, but validating resolvers cannot follow the chain from the parent to the child zone's signatures. What should be done next at the registrar that manages the parent zone?

choices.text: Enable DNSSEC validation for Route 53 Resolver in the VPC.
choices.explanation: This configures validation by the VPC's recursive resolver; it does not establish the domain's public trust chain.

choices.text: Obtain the values required for the DS record from Route 53 and register the DS record for the parent zone at the registrar.
choices.explanation: The DS record on the parent side connects trust to the key of the signed child zone.

choices.text: Shorten the NS TTL at the registrar and do not register a DS record.
choices.explanation: Changing delegation cache time does not publish the data required to trust the child zone's key.

choices.text: Add the same DS record to the child zone itself and leave the parent delegation unchanged.
choices.explanation: An external validation chain requires the parent to publish a signed DS record.

learning.reason: The DS record on the parent side connects trust to the key of the signed child zone.
learning.concept: In public DNSSEC validation, the parent zone's DS record links to the child zone's key.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Block a Specific VPC While Preserving Public DNS Responses
prompt: A target FQDN must be prevented from resolving only through AmazonProvidedDNS for workloads in an isolated VPC. DNS responses for other VPCs and the internet must remain unchanged. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Delete the default route to the internet gateway.
choices.explanation: This affects connectivity outside the VPC, but it does not configure the VPC's AmazonProvidedDNS to reject only the specified name.

choices.text: Add a DNS deny rule to the isolated VPC's network ACL with the target FQDN as the destination.
choices.explanation: Network ACLs evaluate CIDRs and ports; they cannot use the name in a DNS query as a condition.

choices.text: Create a Block rule that uses a domain list containing the target FQDN, and associate the DNS Firewall rule group only with the isolated VPC.
choices.explanation: The name can be evaluated for the target VPC's Resolver without changing authoritative responses for other VPCs or external clients.

choices.text: Delete the record for the FQDN from the public hosted zone.
choices.explanation: This would also change the public response received by users outside the isolated VPC.

learning.reason: The name can be evaluated for the target VPC's Resolver without changing authoritative responses for other VPCs or external clients.
learning.concept: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rule groups are associated on a per-VPC basis.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Allow Only Responses at a Restricted Subnet Boundary
prompt: An EC2 instance with a public IPv4 address provides HTTPS from a public subnet. A permitted external partner establishes a TCP 443 connection, and the security group allows the response for that traffic. After a custom network ACL is configured to allow only inbound port 443, the response does not return. Which outbound permission should be added?

choices.text: Also add outbound TCP ephemeral-port access to the partner CIDR in the security group, and keep the ACL unchanged.
choices.explanation: Although security-group connection tracking allows the response, the independent outbound restriction in the network ACL remains.

choices.text: Add inbound TCP ephemeral ports from the partner CIDR.
choices.explanation: The missing permission in this case is for traffic leaving the subnet toward the client.

choices.text: Allow only outbound TCP 443 to the partner CIDR.
choices.explanation: Port 443 is the server's listening port; the response is addressed to the client's ephemeral port.

choices.text: Allow outbound traffic to the partner CIDR for the range of TCP ephemeral ports used by the client.
choices.explanation: The response packet's destination port is the port opened by the client, and the ACL must explicitly allow the return direction.

learning.reason: The response packet's destination port is the port opened by the client, and the ACL must explicitly allow the return direction.
learning.concept: Network ACLs are stateless, so responses to the client's ephemeral ports must also be allowed.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Encrypt Hybrid Communications Without Using the Public Internet
prompt: On-premises infrastructure and multiple VPCs are consolidated through a Transit Gateway. Direct Connect is used as the underlying circuit, the outer tunnel addresses must also be private, and the entire connection must be encrypted with IPsec. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Connect a transit VIF to a Direct Connect Gateway and do not configure a VPN.
choices.explanation: This connection by itself does not provide IPsec encryption.

choices.text: Provision a separate private VIF for the gateway in each VPC and remove the VPN to the Transit Gateway.
choices.explanation: This does not provide both Transit Gateway aggregation and IPsec encryption over the circuit.

choices.text: Use a Direct Connect transit VIF to connect to the Transit Gateway, and configure a Site-to-Site VPN whose outer addresses are private IPv4 addresses.
choices.explanation: Direct Connect is used as the VPN transport, allowing an IPsec connection to the Transit Gateway without public outer addresses.

choices.text: Create a public VIF and connect it to a standard Site-to-Site VPN with public outer IP addresses.
choices.explanation: This uses IPsec, but it does not meet the requirement that the outer tunnel addresses also be private.

learning.reason: Direct Connect is used as the VPN transport, allowing an IPsec connection to the Transit Gateway without public outer addresses.
learning.concept: A private IP VPN on a Transit Gateway can terminate IPsec through a Direct Connect transit VIF.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Close a Public S3 Bucket While Maintaining Delivery
prompt: CloudFront delivers static files. It is currently configured with an S3 website endpoint as a custom origin, but direct access to S3 must be prevented. Website-endpoint-specific redirect functionality is not required. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Switch to a standard S3 bucket origin, sign requests with OAC, and allow read access only to the specified distribution.
choices.explanation: This blocks public access to S3 and allows the bucket policy to permit signed requests from the CloudFront service.

choices.text: Require signed CloudFront URLs while leaving the current S3 website endpoint public.
choices.explanation: This controls access through CloudFront, but a path for direct access to S3 remains.

choices.text: Leave the website endpoint public and configure CloudFront to redirect to HTTPS.
choices.explanation: This changes the protocol from the viewer to CloudFront, but it does not restrict direct access to S3.

choices.text: Keep the website endpoint and associate OAC to disable public access.
choices.explanation: A website endpoint is a custom origin and does not support OAC, which is for S3 bucket origins.

learning.reason: This blocks public access to S3 and allows the bucket policy to permit signed requests from the CloudFront service.
learning.concept: CloudFront OAC signs requests to standard S3 bucket origins; website endpoints are not supported.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Allow traffic only to buckets owned by the company’s AWS account
prompt: A processing environment in a private subnet uses Amazon S3 only through an S3 gateway endpoint. The company wants to prevent reading buckets owned by external accounts through the endpoint, without rewriting the policy whenever a new company-owned bucket is added. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Split the S3 prefix list routes in the route table by the name of each company-owned bucket.
choices.explanation: The S3 service prefix represents IP destinations; it does not provide a way to separate buckets by owner within the same service.

choices.text: Add aws:SourceVpce to the policies of the company-owned buckets.
choices.explanation: This can restrict entry to company-owned buckets, but it does not affect requests that use the same endpoint to access buckets owned externally.

choices.text: In the endpoint policy, use s3:ResourceAccount as a condition to limit access to resources owned by the company’s account.
choices.explanation: Because the condition is evaluated against the account that owns the target resource, individual bucket names do not need to be listed.

choices.text: In the endpoint policy, restrict only aws:PrincipalAccount to the company’s account.
choices.explanation: This condition applies to the account of the calling principal; it does not prevent a company principal from specifying a bucket owned externally.

learning.reason: Because the condition is evaluated against the account that owns the target resource, individual bucket names do not need to be listed.
learning.concept: s3:ResourceAccount can be used as a condition on the AWS account that owns the requested S3 resource.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Audit unexpected multiple paths from a defined scope
prompt: After a network change, the network team wants to inspect all at once whether there are any paths from an internet gateway into each ENI in a specific private VPC. The combinations of source ENIs and ports cannot be enumerated. Which option discovers potential paths within the target scope without sending actual traffic?

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer to list external access to the roles of the target EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: This feature examines whether permissions are exposed; it does not inspect packet paths.

choices.text: Analyze a Network Access Analyzer scope with the internet gateway as the source and the target VPC as the destination.
choices.explanation: The scope can express the unexpected reachability condition and find all matching potential paths together.

choices.text: Evaluate one selected pair of ENIs with Reachability Analyzer as an example.
choices.explanation: This checks one specific path but does not explore the remaining candidates in the VPC.

choices.text: Search the target VPC’s VPC Flow Logs for past ACCEPT entries.
choices.explanation: This observes traffic that actually flowed, so it cannot identify potential paths that have not been used.

learning.reason: The scope can express the unexpected reachability condition and find all matching potential paths together.
learning.concept: Network Access Analyzer lists potential paths that match an access scope.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Block unmanaged internet ingress across the organization
prompt: The organization’s network team governs a specified Region in one account. It wants to centrally block unintended public ingress even when new VPCs are created. Updates retrieved through a NAT gateway from existing private subnets must continue to work. Which configuration meets these requirements without registering exceptions?

choices.text: Enable VPC Block Public Access with Bidirectional and no exceptions.
choices.explanation: This blocks outbound traffic through an internet gateway in addition to ingress, causing NAT-based update retrieval to fail.

choices.text: Remove public CIDR ranges from the security groups of all existing EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: This affects the current resources but cannot centrally govern all VPCs created later in the Region.

choices.text: Enable VPC Block Public Access with Ingress-only for the target account and Region.
choices.explanation: It blocks connections initiated from the public side while preserving outbound NAT gateway traffic and its responses.

choices.text: Delete all routes to internet gateways from public subnets in the target Region.
choices.explanation: This also removes the routes used by NAT gateways to reach the internet and does not provide governance for new VPCs.

learning.reason: It blocks connections initiated from the public side while preserving outbound NAT gateway traffic and its responses.
learning.concept: Region-level VPC Block Public Access with Ingress-only blocks public ingress while allowing corresponding NAT egress.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Continuously detect public IPv6 SSH access
prompt: AWS Config is used to continuously evaluate SSH rules in existing security groups. The team wants rules that allow SSH from any IPv4 address or any IPv6 address to be reported as violations, respectively. SSH from approved restricted CIDR ranges and other ports must remain unchanged. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Report a violation only when VPC Flow Logs show an increase in ACCEPT entries for TCP 22.
choices.explanation: Configuration exposure and actual connections are different; this would miss a configuration violation when no connection attempt has occurred.

choices.text: Use the AWS Config managed rule restricted-ssh without configuring automatic remediation.
choices.explanation: The rule evaluates unrestricted SSH exposure for both IPv4 and IPv6 and reports the result without changing the security group configuration.

choices.text: Stop sshd in the EC2 user data and do not register a Config rule.
choices.explanation: This changes the guest operating system and does not continuously evaluate the existing security group configuration.

choices.text: Use AWS Config to evaluate only whether the EC2 instance has a public IPv4 address.
choices.explanation: An instance address attribute does not show whether the security group allows SSH from any IPv6 address.

learning.reason: The rule evaluates unrestricted SSH exposure for both IPv4 and IPv6 and reports the result without changing the security group configuration.
learning.concept: The AWS Config restricted-ssh rule marks security group rules that expose TCP 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 as noncompliant.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Keep Flows in the Same AZ for Inline Inspection
prompt: Multiple inspection VPCs in different AZs are attached to a single Transit Gateway. Although routes pass through the inspection VPC, a stateful appliance that sees the outbound path can sometimes receive the return path in a different AZ and lose the connection. Which setting is required on the TGW attachment?

choices.text: Enable IPv6 support on the inspection VPC attachment.
choices.explanation: This supports IPv6 traffic but does not keep the outbound and return paths in the same AZ.

choices.text: Enable appliance mode on the inspection VPC's Transit Gateway VPC attachment.
choices.explanation: This allows the TGW to use the same AZ in the inspection VPC for both directions of a flow.

choices.text: Extend the connection-tracking timeout in the inspection appliance's security group.
choices.explanation: Changing the timeout cannot synchronize state for the outbound path that an appliance in another AZ did not see.

choices.text: Configure appliance mode only on each attachment of the source workload VPC.
choices.explanation: This setting does not apply to the inspection VPC attachment, where path consistency is required.

learning.reason: The TGW can use the same AZ in the inspection VPC for both directions of a flow.
learning.concept: Appliance mode on an inspection VPC attachment causes the TGW to select the same AZ while the flow remains active.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Blackhole Only Part of an Aggregate Route Centrally
prompt: The shared TGW route table has a propagated route for the internal 10.40.0.0/16 network. Multiple sources using the same route table must have only 10.40.8.0/24 discarded by the TGW while continuing to use the other internal networks. What should be done?

choices.text: Add a static blackhole route for 10.40.8.0/24 to the shared TGW route table.
choices.explanation: Only destinations matching the more specific /24 are discarded; existing propagation continues to apply to other destinations in the /16.

choices.text: Add a static route for 10.40.8.0/24 that points to the original on-premises attachment.
choices.explanation: The longest match would forward the /24 to the on-premises site, so it would not be discarded within the TGW.

choices.text: Add a 10.0.0.0/8 blackhole route to the shared TGW route table.
choices.explanation: For the target /24, the existing more specific /16 would continue to be selected.

choices.text: Remove propagation for 10.40.0.0/16.
choices.explanation: This would affect all destinations covered by the /16, including internal traffic that should remain available.

learning.reason: Only destinations matching the more specific /24 are discarded, while existing propagation applies to other destinations in the /16.
learning.concept: A more specific blackhole route in the TGW can discard traffic for the selected destination range.

title: Concentrate Simultaneous Requests to the Origin from Multiple Regions
prompt: CloudFront delivers video segments. The cache key and TTL have been appropriate for some time, but newly published segments experience simultaneous cache misses at edge locations in North America, Europe, and Asia, causing the origin to process multiple requests to retrieve the same object. The segments cannot be preloaded before publication. Which design can consolidate retrievals to the origin?

choices.text: Configure an origin group and use the secondary origin only for specific 5xx errors.
choices.explanation: This provides failover for errors; it does not consolidate the first retrieval of the same object from a healthy origin.

choices.text: Change the origin request policy to forward all viewer headers to the origin.
choices.explanation: This adds request metadata but does not create a setting that consolidates retrieval requests from each region into a common cache.

choices.text: Extend the minimum TTL and retain the existing cache hierarchy.
choices.explanation: This can help caches that have already retrieved an object, but it does not consolidate the first cross-region misses for a segment that was not previously published.

choices.text: Enable Origin Shield in a Region close to the origin.
choices.explanation: Even when the same cache key misses at multiple cache locations, the common layer can consolidate retrievals to the origin.

learning.reason: Even when the same cache key misses at multiple cache locations, the common layer can consolidate retrievals to the origin.
learning.concept: CloudFront Origin Shield acts as a common cache layer in front of the origin and consolidates retrievals for the same object.

title: Separate Contractual Delivery Restrictions from a Shared Catalog
prompt: The sales page is available worldwide. Only viewers in Japan and South Korea should be able to access the full-length videos, and direct access to the origin is already restricted. The full-length videos can be separated onto a different hostname, and no viewer-side code or external geolocation service may be introduced. How should this be designed?

choices.text: Create a distribution dedicated to the full-length videos and add Japan and South Korea to its allowlist.
choices.explanation: The country restriction applies to the entire video distribution, while the existing catalog distribution can remain independent.

choices.text: Configure CloudFront geographic restrictions only on the video cache behavior in the same distribution.
choices.explanation: The standard setting cannot be scoped to a cache behavior; it applies to the entire distribution.

choices.text: Use Route 53 geolocation routing to return the video CloudFront address only to the target countries.
choices.explanation: DNS selection does not reject HTTP access to a known distribution URL.

choices.text: Include CloudFront-Viewer-Country in the full-length video's cache key and add no origin access decision.
choices.explanation: Separating the cache by country does not by itself reject responses to viewers in unauthorized countries.

learning.reason: The country restriction applies to the entire video distribution, while the existing catalog distribution can remain independent.
learning.concept: CloudFront native geographic restrictions apply by country to the entire distribution.

title: Move Part of an Adjacent Region to Another Site
prompt: Two sites host a public API, and Route 53 geoproximity routing directs users to the closer site. Because the capacity of one site will be reduced, you need to shrink only the geographic area sending traffic to the lower-capacity site rather than dividing traffic uniformly at a national border. Both sites must remain in use. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Set a positive bias on the geoproximity record for the site whose capacity will be reduced.
choices.explanation: This expands the site's coverage area and causes it to accept requests in the opposite direction from the requirement.

choices.text: Set a negative bias on the geoproximity record for the site whose capacity will be reduced.
choices.explanation: This preserves proximity-based routing while shrinking that site's coverage area and expanding the adjacent site's coverage area.

choices.text: Replace the records with failover records that designate the target site as secondary.
choices.explanation: This removes proximity-based distribution between the two sites while the primary site is healthy.

choices.text: Use two weighted records and reduce the weight of the lower-capacity site.
choices.explanation: This can adjust the response ratio, but it does not move the geographic boundary between the sites.

learning.reason: This preserves proximity-based routing while shrinking the target site's coverage area and expanding the adjacent site's coverage area.
learning.concept: A negative geoproximity bias shrinks a site's geographic coverage area.

title: Return a Common Entry Point for Unmatched Countries
prompt: Route 53 returns dedicated sites to users from Japan and Australia. You also want to return a common site to users from all other countries and to users whose location cannot be determined from the source IP address. Keep the existing country records. What should you add?

choices.text: Add a geolocation default record with the same name and type that points to the common site.
choices.explanation: This preserves dedicated country matching while answering queries from users with no matching country and users whose location is unknown.

choices.text: Add continent records for Asia and Oceania under the same name.
choices.explanation: This expands coverage for locations whose continent can be identified, but does not cover unknown locations or queries from other continents.

choices.text: Keep the country records and add a latency record for the common site with the same name and type.
choices.explanation: A geolocation routing group with the same name and type cannot be supplemented for unmatched locations by using a different routing policy.

choices.text: Add records pointing to the common site for every continent so that unknown locations are covered without a default record.
choices.explanation: Defining every continent still does not match an IP address whose location cannot be identified.

learning.reason: This preserves dedicated country matching while answering queries from users with no matching country and users whose location is unknown.
learning.concept: A geolocation default record handles queries with no matching configured location and queries from unknown locations.

title: Serve the Correct Compression Format for the Same URL
prompt: A CloudFront distribution uses HTTPS, and the origin returns uncompressed JavaScript. The current behavior uses legacy cache settings. When a viewer supports Brotli, CloudFront must generate Brotli; when a viewer supports only Gzip, CloudFront must generate Gzip. Which two actions allow this without changing the application's URLs? Select two.

choices.text: Enable automatic object compression for the behavior.
choices.explanation: This allows CloudFront to compress eligible objects that it retrieves from the origin.

choices.text: Only add a setting to forward the viewer's Accept-Encoding header to the origin.
choices.explanation: This does not configure CloudFront automatic compression or compression formats for an origin response that is fixed as uncompressed.

choices.text: Set Content-Encoding: br in a response headers policy.
choices.explanation: Adding the header does not compress the content and would provide incorrect information to clients that do not support it.

choices.text: Manually add only the original Accept-Encoding value to the cache key in the legacy cache settings.
choices.explanation: Although this distinguishes values in the cache, legacy settings do not provide Brotli functionality.

choices.text: Switch to a cache policy with Gzip and Brotli enabled.
choices.explanation: This records support for both formats in the cache configuration and allows the suitable representation to be served.

learning.reason: Enable CloudFront to compress eligible objects retrieved from the origin, and reflect support for both formats in the cache configuration so the suitable representation can be served.
learning.concept: CloudFront automatic compression uses the behavior's compression setting together with a cache policy that supports Gzip and Brotli.

title: Send All Players to Their Assigned Game Session
prompt: A game matchmaking service assigns each running match to a private EC2 IP address and UDP port. It gives each client a fixed internet-facing entry point and a match-specific port, and must land players from different regions and network paths on the same instance port. Which approach should you choose?

choices.text: Register all game servers in the target group of a single NLB and distribute the same UDP listener port for every match.
choices.explanation: This balances flows, but it cannot expose the server selected by the game application through a match-specific external port.

choices.text: Register the target VPC subnets with a custom routing accelerator and distribute the external port corresponding to the destination assigned by matchmaking.
choices.explanation: Because the mapping to a specific EC2 instance and port within a subnet is predetermined, all clients in the same match can be directed to the same destination.

choices.text: Use a standard accelerator and multiple NLBs, routing clients according to proximity.
choices.explanation: This uses regional or health-based routing and does not pin users to the specific matched instance and port.

choices.text: Create a common name for all servers with Route 53 multivalue answer routing and let the players' DNS resolution choose the destination.
choices.explanation: This can return multiple server addresses, but it does not specify the assigned destination for the same match through a common name.

learning.reason: Because the mapping to a specific EC2 instance and port within a subnet is predetermined, all clients in the same match can be directed to the same destination.
learning.concept: Global Accelerator custom routing maps public listener ports to destination IP addresses and ports on EC2 instances.

title: Recovery Design When the Canary Deployment Fails Completely
prompt: An ALB weighted forward action is configured with a weight of 95 for the stable target group and 5 for the canary. Design an operating procedure that sends all new requests to the stable version if all canary targets become unhealthy. Target group stickiness is disabled. Which option meets the requirement?

choices.text: Shorten only the canary health check interval and rely on it to automatically shift all traffic after the failure.
choices.explanation: This detects the failure sooner, but it does not change how weights behave between target groups.

choices.text: Enable Evaluate Target Health for the ALB DNS alias.
choices.explanation: Alias health affects DNS-level selection of load balancers; it does not rewrite the canary weight inside the ALB.

choices.text: Shorten the deregistration delay for the canary target group.
choices.explanation: This controls how long in-flight traffic is allowed to finish during deregistration; it does not change the percentage selected by the listener rule.

choices.text: When all canary targets are detected as unhealthy, implement a process that sets the canary weight in the listener rule to 0.
choices.explanation: Weighted target groups do not automatically fail over to one another, so the rule's proportions must be changed when the failure occurs.

learning.reason: Weighted target groups do not automatically fail over to one another, so the rule's proportions must be changed when the failure occurs.
learning.concept: ALB weighted forward does not automatically shift traffic to a healthy group when the other group is empty or all its targets are unhealthy.

title: Gradually Increasing Load Immediately After a Health Check Succeeds
prompt: A container takes 120 seconds for its CPU cache to warm up, although its health check succeeds immediately after startup. New targets are registered individually on a rolling basis in an ALB target group that already contains healthy targets. The goal is to gradually increase the traffic distribution to each new target over 120 seconds after it is deemed healthy. The current algorithm is Round Robin. Which option meets the requirement?

choices.text: Set Slow start to 120 seconds for the target group and keep Round Robin.
choices.explanation: The existing healthy targets continue serving traffic while the share assigned to each newly added target gradually increases.

choices.text: Set the deregistration delay of the group containing the new targets to 120 seconds.
choices.explanation: This protects in-flight traffic during deregistration; it does not stage traffic when a target is added.

choices.text: Set target group stickiness on the ALB rule to 120 seconds.
choices.explanation: This keeps clients associated with a target group; it does not control the warm-up of individual newly added targets.

choices.text: Switch to Least outstanding requests and assign traffic to the new target with the fewest TCP connections.
choices.explanation: This distributes traffic based on outstanding requests; it does not define a gradual allocation period beginning when the target becomes healthy.

learning.reason: The existing healthy targets continue serving traffic while the share assigned to each newly added target gradually increases.
learning.concept: ALB Slow start linearly increases the allocation of requests to a target after the target is determined to be healthy.

title: Treating Insufficient Bandwidth in a Bundled Dedicated Connection as a Failure
prompt: Four 10-Gbps dedicated connections are combined on the same Direct Connect device. If two or fewer connections remain operational, the bandwidth is considered insufficient, and the logical link should be taken down so that traffic can switch to another path. Individual BGP filters must not be used to declare the failure. Which option meets the requirement?

choices.text: Split the four connections across different Direct Connect devices and register them in one LAG.
choices.explanation: Member connections in a single LAG must terminate on the same AWS-side device.

choices.text: Add the four connections to a LAG and set the minimum number of operational connections to 3.
choices.explanation: When fewer than 3 connections remain operational, the entire LAG becomes inactive, allowing traffic to switch to the configured alternate path.

choices.text: Create one VIF per connection and configure only a CloudWatch alarm for bandwidth usage.
choices.explanation: This can notify you about load or failures, but it does not automatically change link state based on the number of operational connections.

choices.text: Add the four connections to a LAG and set the minimum number of operational connections to 2.
choices.explanation: The LAG remains operational while two connections are still available, so it does not meet the condition to switch when two or fewer remain.

learning.reason: When fewer than 3 connections remain operational, the entire LAG becomes inactive, allowing traffic to switch to the configured alternate path.
learning.concept: A Direct Connect LAG allows you to set the minimum number of member connections required for the LAG to remain operational.

title: Routing Only Corporate VPC Destinations Through the VPN
prompt: Remote users reach two corporate VPCs through AWS Client VPN. They want video conferencing and other internet services, as well as their local user network, to continue using the existing endpoint-side egress path. Without distributing individual routes to the devices, which design sends only the two non-overlapping VPC CIDRs through the VPN?

choices.text: Enable split tunneling, add routes for the corporate VPCs to the Client VPN route table, and do not add a default route.
choices.explanation: The routes for the two corporate VPCs are sent to connected devices, while other destinations use the devices' normal local routes.

choices.text: Enable split tunneling, add 0.0.0.0/0 to Client VPN, and retain only authorization rules for the corporate VPC destinations.
choices.explanation: Distributing a default route also affects the path used for non-corporate traffic. Authorization rules cannot select routes for different destinations.

choices.text: Configure a default route to the NAT gateway in the load-balancing subnets on the VPC side.
choices.explanation: This can configure the egress after traffic enters the VPN, but it does not satisfy the requirement for users' devices to exit directly through their existing path.

choices.text: Use full tunneling and register only the corporate VPC destination CIDRs in the Client VPN authorization rules.
choices.explanation: Restricting authorization does not exclude ordinary internet traffic from the routes configured for a full tunnel.

learning.reason: The routes for the two corporate VPCs are sent to connected devices, while other destinations use the devices' normal local routes.
learning.concept: With Client VPN split tunneling, destinations in the endpoint route table are distributed to connected devices.

title: Automatically Create an NLB for an Internal-Only TCP Service
prompt: A TCP application will be deployed in a private EKS Auto Mode cluster. The service must provide an entry point only to sites connected to the internal VPC, and Kubernetes must update the publishing targets when backend Pods are replaced. The default NLB class is available, and no additional controller may be installed. Which option is correct?

choices.text: Create an NLB in the EC2 console and manually register only the current Pod IP addresses.
choices.explanation: This can forward traffic initially, but it cannot continuously reflect Pod replacements based on the Kubernetes Service.

choices.text: Use a LoadBalancer-type Service with the class set to eks.amazonaws.com/nlb, and specify the NLB scheme as internal.
choices.explanation: The cluster manages the private NLB and its targets, restricting service access to connected networks.

choices.text: Create a LoadBalancer-type Service, specify the NLB scheme as internet-facing, and register an internal DNS name.
choices.explanation: Using an alias internally does not change the created NLB to an internal scheme.

choices.text: Create only a ClusterIP-type Service and advertise the ClusterIP to the sites' route tables.
choices.explanation: ClusterIP is for services within the cluster and does not provide an NLB entry point managed for the sites.

learning.reason: The cluster manages the private NLB and its targets, restricting service access to connected networks.
learning.concept: EKS Auto Mode determines how a service is exposed from the NLB class and scheme configured on a LoadBalancer-type Service.

title: Extend a VPC While Preserving an Existing Site Route
prompt: The VPC's primary CIDR is 10.2.0.0/16. One route table in the VPC has an existing route to 10.0.8.0/24, which must continue to be used for a site reached through a VPN. IPAM presents 10.0.0.0/16, 10.0.8.0/24, and 10.3.0.0/16 as candidates. Which option is valid while preserving the existing route?

choices.text: Add 10.0.0.0/16 and rely on longest-prefix matching to give priority to the existing /24 site route.
choices.explanation: Adding a CIDR that contains an existing route is rejected before longest-prefix matching is applied during forwarding.

choices.text: Use 10.3.0.0/16 as the secondary CIDR and use both the added local route and the existing site route.
choices.explanation: It does not overlap with either the existing primary range or the site's destination and can be associated as an internal VPC range.

choices.text: Add the same 10.0.8.0/24 as the existing route and prioritize the VPN after association.
choices.explanation: A CIDR identical to an existing route destination cannot be added, regardless of the configured priority.

choices.text: Create a new route table without the site route and associate 10.0.0.0/16 only with that table.
choices.explanation: A secondary CIDR is associated at the VPC level. Creating a new route table does not remove the constraint on the existing table.

learning.reason: It does not overlap with either the existing primary range or the site's destination and can be associated as an internal VPC range.
learning.concept: When associating a CIDR with a VPC, you cannot add a range identical to an existing route destination or a range that contains an existing destination.

title: Forward to a Service in Another VPC Without Moving the Load Balancer
prompt: An existing public-facing ALB and the EC2 instances for a new application are in different VPCs. VPC peering has established routes in both directions, and the backend can be reached using approved private IPv4 addresses. Which design uses the current ALB without adding another load balancer?

choices.text: Register the instances in the peer VPC by their instance IDs in an instance-type target group.
choices.explanation: Registering by instance ID targets instances in the VPC associated with the target group.

choices.text: Change the target group to ip type, register the application instances' public IPv4 addresses, and send traffic through the peering connection.
choices.explanation: Publicly routable IP addresses cannot be used as targets.

choices.text: Register the peer VPC's private DNS name in an ALB listener rule and return an HTTP redirect.
choices.explanation: A redirect requires the user to reconnect directly, which does not satisfy the requirement that external users reach the service through the ALB.

choices.text: Create an ip-type target group on the existing ALB in the VPC and register the private IPv4 addresses of the EC2 instances in the peer VPC.
choices.explanation: Registering IP addresses allows forwarding and health checks for reachable targets in another VPC.

learning.reason: Registering IP addresses allows forwarding and health checks for reachable targets in another VPC.
learning.concept: An ALB ip-type target group can register the private IP addresses of instances in a reachable peer VPC.

title: Add Central DNS Forwarding to an Application VPC
prompt: The VPC in a connectivity account has a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint and a rule that forwards corp.example to the site's DNS servers. A new application account must use the same conditional forwarding. Without adding entries to the site's DNS allowlist or adding source networks, which option enables name resolution from the new VPC?

choices.text: Only configure the application to use the inbound endpoint in the connectivity account and switch the names handled by the VPC Resolver.
choices.explanation: The existence of an endpoint alone does not apply a conditional forwarding rule for the domain to the Resolver in the new VPC.

choices.text: Create a new outbound endpoint in the application VPC and use the same site DNS servers as the forwarding destinations.
choices.explanation: This requires a new route and source authorization from each VPC, so it does not reuse the central source as required.

choices.text: Share the forwarding rule from the connectivity account using AWS RAM, and have the application account associate it with its VPC.
choices.explanation: When a name matches the rule, it is forwarded to the specified central outbound endpoint, so no additional forwarding source is needed.

choices.text: Share only a private hosted zone from the connectivity VPC and direct all corp.example queries to the zone.
choices.explanation: A hosted zone alone does not conditionally forward queries to the site's authoritative DNS servers.

learning.reason: When a name matches the rule, it is forwarded to the specified central outbound endpoint, so no additional forwarding source is needed.
learning.concept: Sharing a Resolver rule with AWS RAM allows the associated VPC to use the outbound path linked to that rule.

title: Return each backend's destination port through DNS
prompt: Backends in a private VPC are registered under the same service name, but the TCP listening port changes dynamically in each execution environment. Clients obtain the destination and port through standard DNS. Without introducing an SDK, which record should be used with AWS Cloud Map?

choices.text: Define the Cloud Map service discovered through DNS with an SRV record, and provide the port when registering each instance.
choices.explanation: An SRV response directly returns the service hostname and the port for each registered target.

choices.text: Use a Cloud Map service with an A record and register the port as part of the IPv4 address.
choices.explanation: A DNS A record contains IPv4 address information and does not represent a destination port.

choices.text: Return each host's name from a shared service name by using a CNAME.
choices.explanation: A CNAME points to another name; it has no field for the registered target's listening port.

choices.text: Register each port in an AWS Cloud Map HTTP namespace and query it through DNS from clients in the VPC.
choices.explanation: Discovering an HTTP namespace requires an API, so it does not meet the requirement for DNS-query-only integration.

learning.reason: An SRV response directly returns the service hostname and the port for each registered target.
learning.concept: In Cloud Map, AWS_INSTANCE_PORT supplied during registration can be included in the service's SRV record.

title: Encrypt name resolution from an on-premises site
prompt: An on-premises site accesses an AWS private hosted zone over a VPN. The site's resolver supports DNS over HTTPS. For auditing, the DNS session itself must be encrypted over HTTPS, and new queries from the site to AWS must not be accepted as plaintext DNS. Which option meets the requirement?

choices.text: Configure the Resolver inbound endpoint for Do53 only and allow only TCP 53.
choices.explanation: Using TCP for DNS and DNS over HTTPS are different protocols; TCP 53 itself does not encrypt DNS with HTTPS.

choices.text: Configure DoH on a VPC outbound endpoint and send queries from the site to the application VPC.
choices.explanation: An outbound endpoint sends queries from the VPC to external DNS systems; it is not the destination for queries originating from the site.

choices.text: Configure the Resolver inbound endpoint to use DoH only and allow HTTPS connections from the site.
choices.explanation: Queries from the site are accepted through an HTTPS entry point in the VPC, without enabling Do53.

choices.text: Enable DNSSEC on a public Route 53 hosted zone and retain plaintext DNS from the site.
choices.explanation: DNSSEC validates the authenticity of DNS records; it does not turn the DNS session between the site and AWS into HTTPS.

learning.reason: Queries from the site are accepted through an HTTPS entry point in the VPC, without enabling Do53.
learning.concept: A Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint can accept queries over DoH by selecting DoH as its protocol.

title: Manage multicast recipients as they join and leave
prompt: Multiple VPCs in the same Region receive UDP multicast traffic from a source EC2 instance. The sender and receivers use a TGW-compatible configuration, and the receivers support IGMPv2. Because recipients repeatedly start and stop, which option automatically lets them join and leave without statically registering members?

choices.text: Associate the relevant subnets with a multicast-supporting TGW domain that has IGMPv2 enabled, and have receivers join the group.
choices.explanation: Membership is learned from IGMPv2 on the receivers, so individual static member registrations are unnecessary.

choices.text: Connect the VPCs through peering and create routes through the peering connections to the multicast group address.
choices.explanation: VPC peering does not support multicast forwarding.

choices.text: Register the ENIs of all receivers in the TGW's static multicast configuration and let the application manage joining and leaving.
choices.explanation: Static members are managed in the control plane, so this does not meet the requirement for dynamic management through IGMP.

choices.text: Register all receivers with an NLB that has a UDP listener and distribute the NLB's name to the sender.
choices.explanation: Load balancing sends a flow to a selected target; it does not provide multicast delivery to multiple joined receivers.

learning.reason: Membership is learned from IGMPv2 on the receivers, so individual static member registrations are unnecessary.
learning.concept: Transit Gateway handles group membership in an IGMPv2 multicast domain.

title: Use an internal ALB behind edge delivery without exposing it
prompt: An internal ALB in a private subnet is behind CloudFront. Users access it over HTTP only through CloudFront. An internet gateway is already attached to the VPC, and the subnet has available IPv4 addresses. Which configuration uses the ALB without changing it to an internet-facing scheme and without adding another proxy?

choices.text: Move to a public ALB to create an internet entry point, and restrict access with a custom header to the origin.
choices.explanation: Even if the application layer can restrict access, changing to an internet-facing scheme violates the stated condition.

choices.text: Specify only the internal ALB's DNS name as the existing custom origin.
choices.explanation: Specifying the internal ALB's DNS name alone does not add private-network reachability for CloudFront.

choices.text: Associate CloudFront OAC with the internal ALB without configuring a connection to the VPC.
choices.explanation: Authorization for the origin alone does not provide a private path to the internal ALB.

choices.text: Configure the internal ALB as a CloudFront VPC origin and allow traffic from CloudFront at the origin.
choices.explanation: CloudFront uses service-managed ENIs to connect to the internal resource, without creating an internet entry point for the ALB.

learning.reason: CloudFront uses service-managed ENIs to connect to the internal resource, without creating an internet entry point for the ALB.
learning.concept: A CloudFront VPC origin can connect to an internal ALB in a private subnet through a service-managed network path.

title: Choose an Endpoint in the Same AZ as the Application
prompt: An application uses interface endpoints in two AZs of the same VPC. The application manages failover, and during normal operation it must always select the endpoint ENI in the same physical AZ as each application instance. There is no requirement to use a regional shared service name transparently. Which name should be used?

choices.text: Specify the same Regional endpoint DNS name for all applications.
choices.explanation: A Regional name does not pin the configuration to a specific AZ; endpoints in multiple AZs can be candidates.

choices.text: Register the addresses of all endpoint ENIs under one static name and use the same record from every client regardless of AZ.
choices.explanation: Because the configuration returns the same answer with candidates from multiple AZs, it does not guarantee selection in the same AZ.

choices.text: Specify the same private DNS name for the service in every application and disable DNS caching.
choices.explanation: Disabling caching causes name resolution to occur each time, but it does not explicitly identify the endpoint's AZ with an endpoint-specific name.

choices.text: Configure the endpoint-specific zonal DNS name corresponding to each application's AZ.
choices.explanation: Using the name published for each AZ selects the endpoint ENI in the specified AZ.

learning.reason: Using the name published for each AZ selects the endpoint ENI in the specified AZ.
learning.concept: Interface endpoints have a Regional name as well as zonal DNS names that select a specific AZ.

title: Accelerating Detection of a Circuit Failure with No Loss of Physical Signal
prompt: Two Direct Connect connections provide redundancy. If the transit network on one side can no longer forward traffic, the physical links at both ends remain UP, so failover does not occur until the BGP Hold Timer expires. Which mechanism, also supported by the on-premises router, should be used on the VIF to detect the failure early?

choices.text: Set a short-interval alarm on the VIF transmit-side optical power.
choices.explanation: This cannot observe a forwarding failure in the transit network while optical power remains normal.

choices.text: Shorten the standby path's AS_PATH and continue advertising both routes.
choices.explanation: This changes the preference between reachable routes; it does not detect a forwarding failure on the active path sooner.

choices.text: Configure asynchronous BFD for the relevant BGP peer on the on-premises router and confirm that the session is established on both sides.
choices.explanation: BFD monitors the IP path and does not rely only on the existing BGP timers when the physical state remains UP.

choices.text: Wait until ConnectionState becomes DOWN during a failure and use that metric as the sole failover condition.
choices.explanation: When forwarding stops but the physical link remains UP, this failure does not satisfy the failover condition.

learning.reason: BFD monitors the IP path and does not rely only on the existing BGP timers when the physical state remains UP.
learning.concept: When asynchronous BFD supported by AWS is enabled for the customer-side peer as well, reachability failures of the BGP adjacency can be detected sooner.

title: Connecting a Private VIF Created in Another Account
prompt: A connectivity provider created a hosted private VIF on a Direct Connect port that it manages, with the customer's AWS account as the VIF owner. The VIF appears to the customer in a pending state, and the virtual private gateway to which it will connect is in the customer's account. What should the customer do next?

choices.text: The customer should set the Amazon-side BGP ASN on the gateway; the pending VIF will then transition automatically.
choices.explanation: The ASN is a route-exchange setting and does not constitute acceptance of the VIF assignment to the account.

choices.text: The connectivity provider should delete the existing VIF and share the customer's VPC with the provider's account.
choices.explanation: Sharing a VPC does not replace acceptance of the assigned VIF and does not satisfy the customer's selection of the connection target.

choices.text: In the customer account, accept the hosted VIF and select the customer's virtual private gateway as the connection target.
choices.explanation: The customer can establish the connection to its gateway as a customer-owned VIF without transferring ownership of the physical connection.

choices.text: The customer should specify the provider's physical connection ID and recreate the VIF in its own account with the same tag.
choices.explanation: The customer does not own the provider's physical connection. It should accept the VIF assigned to the customer.

learning.reason: The customer can establish the connection to its gateway as a customer-owned VIF without transferring ownership of the physical connection.
learning.concept: A hosted VIF is accepted by the account to which it was assigned before it is used.

title: Resolving a State in Which Only One Redundant Tunnel Allows the Legacy Method
prompt: A Site-to-Site VPN has two tunnels. An audit requires both tunnels to allow only IKEv2, with the on-premises device and AWS configuration matching. During the change, the other tunnel must remain available for operations. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Update the BGP authentication key on both sides and leave the IKE version at its default.
choices.explanation: BGP authentication concerns route exchange after the VPN is established; it does not restrict the IKE versions that can be negotiated.

choices.text: Specify IKEv2 on only one tunnel in AWS and wait for the setting to be replicated between tunnels.
choices.explanation: Allowed IKE versions are configured for each tunnel, so changing only one tunnel does not restrict the allowed method on the other.

choices.text: Continue allowing both IKEv1 and IKEv2 on the AWS side while limiting the Phase 1 encryption algorithms.
choices.explanation: Limiting encryption algorithms does not change the list of allowed IKE versions.

choices.text: Switch the tunnels one at a time during maintenance, configure AWS to allow only IKEv2 for each tunnel, and make the corresponding change on the on-premises device.
choices.explanation: This matches the negotiation conditions on both sides for each tunnel while allowing the standby tunnel to be verified as operational.

learning.reason: This matches the negotiation conditions on both sides for each tunnel while allowing the standby tunnel to be verified as operational.
learning.concept: Allowed IKE versions are configured as options for each tunnel in AWS Site-to-Site VPN.

title: Use the standard PrivateLink service name in a template
prompt: A stack creates an isolated VPC and an interface endpoint for Secrets Manager. The application's SDK accesses the standard Region-specific service name and must resolve the public name to the private IP address of an ENI in the VPC. The subnets and security group are already prepared. Which settings should be specified? Select two.

choices.text: Set AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint to type Interface and set PrivateDnsEnabled to true.
choices.explanation: This enables private DNS so the application can connect using the service's standard name.

choices.text: Set the endpoint type to Gateway and let the SDK's name resolution use the route table.
choices.explanation: Secrets Manager uses an interface endpoint, and a Gateway endpoint does not provide the same private DNS configuration.

choices.text: Set the endpoint's PrivateDnsEnabled to false, specify the subnet ID, and have the standard name be updated automatically.
choices.explanation: The endpoint ENI is created in the subnet, but the standard name is not automatically redirected.

choices.text: Set both EnableDnsSupport and EnableDnsHostnames to true for the VPC.
choices.explanation: This supplies the VPC DNS attributes required for private DNS name resolution.

choices.text: Set only EnableDnsSupport to false so that all queries are sent to Internet DNS.
choices.explanation: This prevents private resolution of the standard endpoint name through the VPC Resolver.

learning.reason: Private DNS is enabled for the service's standard name, and the VPC DNS attributes required for private DNS resolution are enabled.
learning.concept: PrivateDnsEnabled on an interface endpoint and the VPC DNS attributes enable private resolution of the standard service name.

title: Who changes the return route and communication permissions in a shared subnet?
prompt: As a participant, an application team created an EC2 instance and its own security group in a shared subnet. Connectivity with on-premises infrastructure requires adding a destination to the shared subnet's route table and adding an allowed CIDR to the EC2 instance's security group. If the existing ownership relationships are maintained, which division of responsibilities is correct?

choices.text: The participant changes both the subnet's route table and its own security group.
choices.explanation: A participant may be able to view the shared subnet's route table, but cannot associate or manage it.

choices.text: The participant associates its own route table as the shared subnet's main table.
choices.explanation: Associating the shared subnet's route table is not an operation available to the participant.

choices.text: The VPC owner changes the subnet's route table, and the participant changes the rules of its own security group.
choices.explanation: The owner account changes shared-network resources, while the participant changes resources it owns.

choices.text: Because the VPC owner manages the shared subnet, it directly changes the participant's security group as well.
choices.explanation: Security-group ownership is separate from subnet ownership. A security group created by the participant is not a resource owned by the VPC owner.

learning.reason: The owner account changes the shared-network resource, while the participant changes the resource it owns.
learning.concept: In a shared VPC, the owner manages the route table, while a participant manages a security group that it owns.

title: Forward only a child domain to an authoritative DNS server at another site
prompt: The VPC Resolver has a forwarding rule for corp.example that specifies the resolver at the old site. You want only lab.corp.example at the acquired site to be sent to the authoritative DNS server at the new site, while keeping the existing forwarding destination for the other corp.example subdomains. Both sites are reachable from outbound endpoints. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Add the new site's destination IP address to the existing corp.example rule and have the Resolver try it only when there is no response.
choices.explanation: Adding a destination to the parent rule does not configure the child domain to consistently select the new site.

choices.text: Delete the existing parent-domain rule and associate only a rule for the child domain.
choices.explanation: Although the child domain could be forwarded, there would be no condition to send other internal queries under the parent domain to the old site.

choices.text: Add a forwarding rule for lab.corp.example that specifies the new site's DNS server, and associate it with the same VPC.
choices.explanation: The more specific rule is selected for queries to the child domain, while other queries continue to use the parent rule.

choices.text: Associate an empty private hosted zone for lab.corp.example and keep forwarding only to the existing parent rule.
choices.explanation: An empty zone does not configure forwarding to the new site's authoritative DNS server and does not provide the required records.

learning.reason: The specific rule is selected for queries to the child domain, while other queries continue to use the parent rule.
learning.concept: When multiple forwarding rules match a name, the rule for the more specific domain takes precedence.

title: Point the zone apex to an ALB with changing IP addresses
prompt: Point the apex of the public hosted zone example.com to an internet-facing ALB that uses IPv4. Users must keep the same URL even if the ALB node IP addresses change, and the existing SOA and NS records must be preserved. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Register the IPv4 address returned by the first lookup of the ALB DNS name in a standard A record for example.com.
choices.explanation: The current IP address may allow connections, but the record will not follow changes to the ALB node addresses.

choices.text: Create a CNAME record in example.com that references the ALB DNS name.
choices.explanation: The zone apex already has SOA and NS records, and a CNAME cannot be created at that name.

choices.text: Replace the NS record for example.com with the ALB DNS name and delegate the zone to it.
choices.explanation: An ALB is not an authoritative DNS server and cannot be the target of zone delegation.

choices.text: Create an alias A record in example.com that references the ALB.
choices.explanation: At the zone apex, an alias can coexist with the required existing records while AWS follows the ALB's addresses.

learning.reason: At the zone apex, an alias can coexist with the required records and AWS can follow the ALB's changing addresses.
learning.concept: A Route 53 alias can reference an ALB at the zone apex.

title: Delegating a child zone from an on-premises authoritative DNS server to AWS
prompt: The corporate authoritative DNS server manages example.internal. For the AWS private hosted zone cloud.example.internal, the company wants to handle resolution as a DNS delegation from the parent zone without introducing conditional forwarding for each site resolver. AWS and the sites are reachable over private IP addresses. What should be configured?

choices.text: Register the outbound endpoint IP addresses as glue records for the child domain in the parent zone.
choices.explanation: An outbound endpoint is used to send queries from the VPC to external destinations; it is not the receiving endpoint for delegated queries from the sites to AWS.

choices.text: Create a Default-type inbound endpoint and add conditional forwarding for the child name to every site resolver.
choices.explanation: This works as ordinary conditional forwarding, but it does not satisfy the requirement to use delegation from the corporate parent zone.

choices.text: Create a Delegation-type inbound endpoint and associate the parent zone's delegated NS records with the endpoint IP addresses by using glue records.
choices.explanation: The sites can follow the child-zone delegation and send queries to the private Delegation endpoint.

choices.text: Duplicate the private hosted zone as a public hosted zone and delegate the parent zone to authoritative DNS servers on the internet.
choices.explanation: This would expose DNS data for internal services and would not preserve the private delegation scope.

learning.reason: The sites can follow the child-zone delegation and send queries to the private Delegation endpoint.
learning.concept: A Delegation-type inbound Resolver endpoint can be referenced through the parent-zone delegation and glue records without exposing it publicly.

title: Using a custom name for a private API through an authorized endpoint
prompt: A custom domain has been assigned to an API Gateway private REST API. The resource policies for the API and domain allow the target VPC endpoint, and private DNS is already configured. The API's endpoint-specific name is reachable from the same endpoint. Which additional association is required to use the custom domain?

choices.text: Remove the endpoint ID from the REST API and duplicate the same mapping on a Regional public custom domain.
choices.explanation: This would not preserve the private name and access boundary.

choices.text: Set the endpoint's private IP address in an API stage variable.
choices.explanation: Stage variables can be used for integration settings and other purposes, but they do not create the network-side access association required for a custom domain.

choices.text: Duplicate only the custom domain's A record in another private hosted zone.
choices.explanation: Even if name resolution returns the same result, this does not create the domain-to-endpoint association required by API Gateway.

choices.text: Create a domain-name access association between the target execute-api interface endpoint and the private custom domain.
choices.explanation: This registers the consumer-side access path so that the custom domain can be used from that endpoint.

learning.reason: This registers the consumer-side access path so that the custom domain can be used from that endpoint.
learning.concept: Using a private custom domain requires a domain-name access association with the consumer VPC endpoint.

title: Adding UDP access for clients that include IPv6
prompt: In a supported Region, a new dual-stack NLB is created in a VPC with an IPv6 CIDR. The UDP listener's target group is of type IPv6, and the targets are registered with IPv6 addresses. Which setting must be specified on the NLB to support preserving source IP addresses for an IPv6 UDP listener?

choices.text: Replace UDP with a QUIC listener and omit the IPv6 source NAT setting.
choices.explanation: This replaces the existing application protocol with a different listener protocol and does not preserve the dual-stack premise.

choices.text: Specify an IPv6 source NAT prefix in each subnet mapping, or have AWS assign one.
choices.explanation: This allows the dual-stack NLB to use an IPv6 source NAT range for UDP traffic on a per-subnet basis.

choices.text: Switch to an IPv4-type UDP target group to protect client IPv6 addresses.
choices.explanation: A dual-stack NLB UDP configuration must satisfy the requirement for an IPv6 target group.

choices.text: Disable IPv6 source NAT and register only the NLB listener's DNS name in an AAAA record.
choices.explanation: Making name resolution IPv6-capable does not provision the internal prefix required by the dual-stack UDP configuration.

learning.reason: This allows the dual-stack NLB to use an IPv6 source NAT range for UDP traffic on a per-subnet basis.
learning.concept: To support source IP preservation for an IPv6 UDP listener, enable an IPv6 source NAT prefix.

title: Moving EKS Pod IP addresses to a CIDR separate from the nodes
prompt: The Linux EC2 nodes in an EKS cluster must remain in their current subnets, while regular Pod IP addresses must be assigned only from a new secondary CIDR. The VPC CNI is in use, and new Pod subnets and Pod security groups have already been prepared in each Availability Zone. Which action should be taken?

choices.text: Add the secondary CIDR to a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy and keep the existing VPC CNI configuration.
choices.explanation: NetworkPolicy controls communication permissions; it does not change the subnets used for Pod IP addresses.

choices.text: Specify a Kubernetes Service ClusterIP range and do not create secondary ENIs for the Pods.
choices.explanation: The virtual IP range for Services is different from the VPC IP addresses assigned to Pods.

choices.text: Enable custom networking and associate nodes with ENIConfig objects that specify the Pod subnet and security group for each Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: The VPC CNI can create secondary ENIs in subnets different from the node primary ENIs and assign their IP addresses to Pods.

choices.text: Enable only IPv4 prefix delegation in the VPC CNI and keep using the current node subnets.
choices.explanation: This can improve IP allocation efficiency, but it does not provide the configuration needed to select different subnets.

learning.reason: The VPC CNI can create secondary ENIs in subnets different from the node primary ENIs and assign their IP addresses to Pods.
learning.concept: VPC CNI custom networking uses ENIConfig to specify a separate subnet and security group.

title: Add an endpoint while retaining an existing same-name zone
prompt: A private hosted zone whose name matches the standard name of an AWS service is already associated with a VPC. Existing applications use records in that zone, so the zone cannot be disassociated. After an interface endpoint is added, private DNS for the service name cannot be enabled. New applications can change the destination name. Which option is correct?

choices.text: Replace the subnets of the endpoint ENIs so that the same-name zone is not visible.
choices.explanation: Private hosted zone associations apply at the VPC level, so moving the endpoint to different subnets in the same VPC does not remove the conflict.

choices.text: Create the endpoint with Private DNS disabled and have new applications use the endpoint-specific DNS name.
choices.explanation: The endpoint-specific name reaches the ENIs while allowing the existing same-name private hosted zone to remain in place.

choices.text: Delete the records in the same-name zone, keep the association, and enable private DNS again.
choices.explanation: The conflict is caused by the zone name associated with the same VPC. Deleting the records would also affect existing applications.

choices.text: Disable VPC DNS support and force Private DNS on the endpoint.
