choices.explanation: Disabling DNS support would remove the prerequisites for transparent private DNS.

learning.reason: The endpoint-specific name can reach the ENIs while the existing same-name private zone remains associated.
learning.concept: Using an endpoint-specific DNS name and transparently resolving the standard service name through Private DNS are separate connection paths.

title: Compare static and propagated routes with the same CIDR
prompt: A VPC route table contains a static route for 10.42.0.0/16 that sends traffic to a transit ENI. When propagation from a virtual private gateway is enabled, the same range is advertised dynamically. The ENI is operational, and the existing path must remain in use until the change window. How should the current forwarding for 10.42.1.20 be determined?

choices.text: Both routes have the same prefix length, so per-flow ECMP starts within the VPC.
choices.explanation: A static route and a propagated route are not treated as equal-cost routes in this situation.

choices.text: The route received through BGP is newer, so the virtual private gateway is selected.
choices.explanation: When the destination is the same and the route types differ, selection is based on route priority, not arrival time.

choices.text: Because the prefix lengths are the same, the existing static route targeting the transit ENI is selected.
choices.explanation: Enabling propagation does not displace a valid static route for the same destination; the static route takes priority.

choices.text: Neither route can be used in the route table unless the static destination is aggregated to 10.42.0.0/15.
choices.explanation: A valid static route can be used even when another route has the same destination. With /15, the propagated /16 would instead be the more specific match.

learning.reason: Enabling dynamic propagation does not displace a valid static route for the same destination.
learning.concept: When static and propagated routes with the same destination compete in a VPC route table, the applicable static route takes priority.

title: Express the prerequisite for creating a route in the same stack
prompt: A single CloudFormation stack creates a VPC, an IGW, a VPCGatewayAttachment, and a default route for a public subnet. The default route has Ref references to the IGW and the route table, but creation can fail the first time because the gateway has not yet been attached to the VPC. How should this be corrected in the template?

choices.text: Add the IGW logical ID to DependsOn and retain the existing Ref to the gateway.
choices.explanation: This can wait for the IGW itself to be created, but it does not represent completion of the attachment to the VPC, which is a separate resource.

choices.text: For AWS::EC2::Route, specify the logical ID of VPCGatewayAttachment in DependsOn.
choices.explanation: This waits for the attachment to complete before creating the default route, a dependency that a reference to the resource itself does not express.

choices.text: Set the default route as a DependsOn dependency of VPCGatewayAttachment.
choices.explanation: This reverses the dependency and makes the attachment occur after route creation, so it does not solve the creation-order problem.

choices.text: Set DeletionPolicy Retain on AWS::EC2::Route.
choices.explanation: This attribute controls deletion behavior and does not specify creation order.

learning.reason: The default route must be created only after the attachment is complete, because a reference to the resource itself does not express that prerequisite.
learning.concept: A public route using an IGW requires both creation of the IGW resource and completion of its attachment to the VPC.

title: Restore reachability to an on-premises network based on the associated AZ
prompt: AWS Client VPN is associated with subnets in two AZs of the same VPC. The on-premises network is reachable from the VPC route tables for both subnets, and the Client VPN authorization rule allows the on-premises CIDR. However, the Client VPN endpoint has a route for the on-premises CIDR registered for only one of the associated subnets. How should this be corrected?

choices.text: Add the Client VPN route for the on-premises CIDR for the other associated subnet as well.
choices.explanation: Regardless of which association is used for the connection, Client VPN route selection can then reach the same destination.

choices.text: Re-create the Client VPN authorization rule for the same on-premises CIDR and keep the endpoint route for only one association.
choices.explanation: Authorization does not add a route, so the association without a route remains unable to reach the destination.

choices.text: Re-register the same CIDR in the VPC route tables for both AZs so that it is automatically copied to the Client VPN routes.
choices.explanation: Even when the VPC routes are correct, the independent Client VPN route is required for each association.

choices.text: Delete the association with one subnet.
choices.explanation: This can constrain connections to the usable association, but it removes the redundancy provided by associations in two AZs.

learning.reason: Each associated target network needs the Client VPN route so that the same destination is reachable regardless of which association the connection uses.
learning.concept: For a Client VPN endpoint with multiple associated subnets, align the routes for every destination that must be reachable through each association.

title: Decouple task IP changes from the service-name contract
prompt: An ECS client service in the same Region needs to connect to frequently replaced ECS backend tasks through a protocol-aware proxy. The client must not require additional AWS API calls, and the application code must use a fixed name and port. Which option uses an ECS managed mechanism?

choices.text: Manually register targets in an internal NLB and use only a shared DNS name without configuring Service Connect.
choices.explanation: This can provide a TCP entry point, but it is not service-to-service communication through the ECS Service Connect proxy.

choices.text: Disable private DNS in the VPC and assign the same fixed IP address to every task.
choices.explanation: Concurrent tasks and task replacement conflict with IP uniqueness, and this does not provide a management function that maintains the service name.

choices.text: Write the IP address immediately after an ECS task starts to a shared parameter, and have the client retrieve it only at startup.
choices.explanation: This provides an initial destination, but it does not track task replacement or provide an ECS-managed proxy.

choices.text: Use the same Service Connect namespace for the related ECS services and configure a client alias for the backend's named port.
choices.explanation: This maps a fixed logical name to a connection through the ECS proxy and lets the service configuration handle task replacement.

learning.reason: This maps a fixed logical name to a connection through the ECS proxy and lets the service configuration handle task replacement.
learning.concept: ECS Service Connect uses an ECS-managed proxy based on service-to-service name and port configuration.

title: Expose an inspection service only to approved partners
prompt: The inspection-side account has already created a Gateway Load Balancer endpoint service. The provider must allow only a specific IAM role from a partner to create an endpoint, and the inspection side must individually approve each connection. Which settings should be configured by the provider? Choose two.

choices.text: Configure the service to automatically accept connection requests.
choices.explanation: Connections created by an allowed principal would be established without individual approval by the provider.

choices.text: Require acceptance of connection requests in the endpoint service.
choices.explanation: Even for connections from an allowed principal, the provider must individually review and accept the connection.

choices.text: Allow the partner's CIDR in the inspection appliance's security group and do not configure the service's allowed principals.
choices.explanation: Packet-permission rules do not control which principals can issue PrivateLink connection requests.

choices.text: Add the partner role's ARN to the endpoint service's allowed principals.
choices.explanation: This limits the principals that can issue connection requests to the specified partner role.

choices.text: Register the entire partner account as an allowed principal.
choices.explanation: Requests from principals other than the specified partner role would also be included among the allowed requests.

learning.reason: The provider can limit the principals that may issue connection requests to the specified partner role and can separately require individual acceptance even for allowed principals.
learning.concept: PrivateLink allowed principals and whether endpoint connections require acceptance are independent settings.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Reduce new TCP connection failures by distributing backend placement
prompt: Client IP preservation is disabled for an NLB TCP target group. PortAllocationErrorCount increases only during peak periods, while existing connections and backend health remain normal. Without reducing the request rate, which option improves per-connection translation-port allocation while continuing to use the same NLB?

choices.text: Add targets with different IP addresses or ports to the same target group.
choices.explanation: Because the NLB allocates translated connections for each target IP-and-port combination, this can distribute the connection concentration.

choices.text: Add only an IPv6 AAAA record to the NLB while leaving the TCP target resources unchanged.
choices.explanation: This does not add more of the constrained targets. Changing only the DNS record type cannot improve the allocation capacity of the path experiencing the errors.

choices.text: Shorten the target group's health check interval so that all targets are identified as healthy sooner.
choices.explanation: The targets are already healthy, and health checks cannot increase the capacity of connection translation ports.

choices.text: Only shorten the cache time for the DNS alias.
choices.explanation: Changing name-resolution refresh frequency does not increase the connection-allocation capacity of the same NLB and targets.

learning.reason: Because the NLB allocates translated connections for each target IP-and-port combination, adding different combinations distributes the connection concentration.
learning.concept: When port-allocation errors increase in a configuration with client IP preservation disabled, an NLB can expand the available combinations by adding targets.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Feed dedicated-circuit maintenance notices into work tickets
prompt: In the AWS account that owns the connection, you want to send scheduled Direct Connect maintenance to an existing operations ticket system before an outage occurs. Use a provider event that includes the affected connection and scheduled time, and do not create a ticket for optical-level or BGP state changes. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Create a ConnectionState CloudWatch alarm and create a ticket when DOWN is observed.
choices.explanation: This is notification after a failure and cannot obtain AWS-scheduled maintenance or the affected resource in advance.

choices.text: Subscribe to Direct Connect maintenance events from AWS Health through EventBridge and forward them to the existing ticket system.
choices.explanation: These service notifications include the scheduled time and affected resources, so the event can be received before the physical connection is disconnected.

choices.text: Record the time when the VIF traffic falls below a certain level as the scheduled maintenance time.
choices.explanation: This infers maintenance from an observed traffic change and cannot receive the confirmed time of planned maintenance.

choices.text: Monitor ModifyConnection in CloudTrail and assume that all AWS maintenance changes use the same event name.
choices.explanation: Account API activity records cannot replace scheduled-maintenance notifications from the service.

learning.reason: A service notification containing the scheduled time and affected resources can be received before the physical connection is disconnected.
learning.concept: Scheduled Direct Connect maintenance is notified through AWS Health in the owning account and can be forwarded to an operations system through EventBridge.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Distinguishing why traffic was lost in a TGW flow log
prompt: Transit Gateway flow logs are being collected. During an incident, packets failed to reach several destinations, and you need to classify, for each attachment, drops caused by missing routes separately from intentional blackhole drops. Which fields should you correlate?

choices.text: Aggregate only TGW bytes and always treat destinations with fewer bytes as having no route.
choices.explanation: Traffic volume does not record the reason, so it cannot distinguish the two causes of the drop.

choices.text: Look only at srcaddr and dstaddr in the TGW flow logs and infer the drop reason from the destination IP range.
choices.explanation: The addresses identify the destination, but they do not show the routing result applied by the TGW.

choices.text: Count every row with a REJECT action in the included VPC Flow Logs as a TGW blackhole.
choices.explanation: A rejection by a VPC filter is not equivalent to a TGW routing drop and cannot be distinguished from a missing route.

choices.text: Aggregate packets-lost-no-route and packets-lost-blackhole by attachment identifier and destination.
choices.explanation: These cause-specific counts can be associated with the relevant flows and attachments.

learning.reason: These cause-specific counts can be associated with the relevant flows and attachments.
learning.concept: TGW flow logs count packet loss caused by no route and by a blackhole separately.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Monitoring subnet exhaustion before automatic deployments fail
prompt: An incident occurred in some IPv4 subnets monitored by IPAM: new ENIs could not be created during scale-out. The VPC as a whole has sufficient capacity. You want to notify separately for each affected subnet when the percentage of consumed IPv4 addresses within that subnet exceeds 75%. Which option should you use?

choices.text: In CloudWatch, select IPAM's SubnetIPUsage and set an alarm on the utilization of the target subnet.
choices.explanation: This monitors the percentage of active IPs relative to the subnet's total number of IPv4 addresses.

choices.text: Monitor the packet count for each Transit Gateway connection.
choices.explanation: Routing usage cannot be used to calculate the remaining ENI address capacity of each subnet.

choices.text: Use IPAM's VpcIPUsage to monitor only the percentage of the VPC's allocated addresses occupied by subnet ranges.
choices.explanation: This can help with VPC CIDR planning, but it does not show the proportion of addresses consumed within a specific subnet.

choices.text: Aggregate EC2 NetworkIn for each ENI and convert traffic volume into the IPv4 allocation rate.
choices.explanation: An ENI can be using an IP even when it has little traffic, so this cannot measure address allocation.

learning.reason: This monitors the percentage of active IPs relative to the subnet's total number of IPv4 addresses.
learning.concept: AWS/IPAM SubnetIPUsage shows the active IPv4 utilization of a subnet.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Mapping flow-log collection status to audit findings
prompt: VPC Flow Logs produced different log-status values for multiple aggregation intervals for a target ENI. Match the single most appropriate log-status to each observation. Each candidate is used once.

choices.text: SKIPDATA
choices.explanation: Some records may have been omitted during the aggregation interval because of internal constraints or errors, so the absence of traffic cannot be proved.

choices.text: OK
choices.explanation: The flow logs recorded data normally.

choices.text: NODATA
choices.explanation: There was no network traffic for the target ENI that was eligible for recording during the aggregation interval.

learning.reason: The flow logs recorded data normally. There was no network traffic for the target ENI that was eligible for recording during the aggregation interval. Some records may have been omitted during the aggregation interval because of internal constraints or errors, so the absence of traffic cannot be proved.
learning.concept: The VPC Flow Logs log-status indicates collection status, while action indicates whether traffic was accepted or rejected.

prompts.text: The target traffic flow was observed, and records for the aggregation interval were received normally.
No traffic eligible for recording was observed, and there were no flows to record throughout the aggregation interval.
Flow records were omitted during part of the aggregation interval, so collection was incomplete.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Restoring connections from backends that use the same NLB
prompt: The TCP targets of an internal NLB sometimes connect from a separate job to the same NLB on which they are registered. The connection fails only when it is routed back to the originating target. Client IP preservation is enabled for the target group, but the application does not need to reference the source IP. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Only increase the deregistration delay for the targets.
choices.explanation: This is a hairpin problem involving an active target; the connection-termination grace period during deregistration does not resolve it.

choices.text: Enable cross-zone load balancing while keeping client IP preservation enabled.
choices.explanation: Broadening the range of possible targets does not change the restriction on a path that routes the connection back to itself.

choices.text: Disable client IP preservation for the target TCP target group.
choices.explanation: The connection uses an address translated by the NLB, avoiding the hairpin problem in which the source and selected target are the same.

choices.text: Keep client IP preservation enabled and enable only Proxy Protocol v2.
choices.explanation: Adding source-connection information in a header does not change the hairpin restriction of a configuration that preserves the original IP.

learning.reason: The connection uses an address translated by the NLB, avoiding the hairpin problem in which the source and selected target are the same.
learning.concept: NAT loopback for an internal NLB is not supported when client IP preservation is enabled.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Resolving an EC2 Public DNS Name to a Private IP Across VPCs
prompt: When an EC2 instance in peering-connected VPC A looks up the public IPv4 DNS name assigned to an EC2 instance in VPC B, the public IPv4 address is returned. DNS support and hostnames are enabled in both VPCs, and connectivity using the private IP has been confirmed. Which option allows A to obtain B's private IPv4 address while using the same name?

choices.text: Add a prefix for B's public IPv4 address to the VPC peering route.
choices.explanation: Configuring the traffic path does not change the result of name resolution and does not satisfy the requirement to resolve to the private IP.

choices.text: Specify only a public DNS server in VPC A's DHCP options.
choices.explanation: Using an external DNS server does not enable private DNS translation on the peering side.

choices.text: Use the same network ACL for A and B so that the DNS response is also a private IP address.
choices.explanation: Allowing or denying packets does not control which address DNS returns.

choices.text: Enable the peering DNS resolution setting that resolves B's public hostname to B's private IP from A.
choices.explanation: This returns a private name-resolution result for the peering target while allowing the existing name to be used.

learning.reason: This returns a private name-resolution result for the peering target while allowing the existing name to be used.
learning.concept: With the VPC peering DNS resolution option, an EC2 instance's public IPv4 DNS name can resolve to its private IPv4 address when queried from the peer.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Accepting a VPN Tunnel Update Ahead of Schedule
prompt: For a redundant Site-to-Site VPN, you want to record a pending AWS endpoint update and update only the affected tunnel first during a low-usage period. This period is before the automatic-application time specified by AWS. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Shorten the IKE key lifetime on the affected tunnel and wait for the AWS endpoint update to start at the same time.
choices.explanation: Key renegotiation and a service endpoint replacement are separate operations; this does not accept a pending update.

choices.text: Wait until the deadline passes with lifecycle control enabled and schedule the maintenance window assuming that AWS will not update the tunnel.
choices.explanation: After the deadline, AWS automatically updates the tunnel as part of scheduled maintenance, so this does not provide reliable control over the timing.

choices.text: Enable lifecycle control on the affected tunnel, review the pending maintenance, and accept the update during a window before the automatic-application deadline.
choices.explanation: You can review the pending state and deadline, confirm that the standby tunnel is operating, and start the update on the affected side.

choices.text: Temporarily withdraw BGP advertisements from the affected tunnel and treat the maintenance as completed.
choices.explanation: Changing the route does not change whether the AWS update is pending or complete.

learning.reason: You can review the pending state and deadline, confirm that the standby tunnel is operating, and start the update on the affected side.
learning.concept: Tunnel endpoint lifecycle control provides visibility into maintenance and allows acceptance at a chosen time before the deadline.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Identifying Why an Old Record Is Returned After an Authoritative DNS Update
prompt: You changed a Route 53 record to a new destination. The change status is INSYNC, and a direct query to the authoritative name servers returns the new address. Only the recursive resolvers at some offices return the old response with a TTL of 3,600 seconds that they obtained just before the change. How should you interpret this first?

choices.text: The authoritative distribution is updated, and the recursive resolvers are responding according to the remaining TTL of the old response.
choices.explanation: Recursive caches follow the TTL obtained before the update. Updating the authoritative side does not immediately clear old cached responses everywhere.

choices.text: Because the status is INSYNC, the recursive resolvers must also be updated, so the Route 53 DNS change should be considered failed.
choices.explanation: INSYNC indicates that the specified change has propagated to the authoritative DNS service; it does not describe the state of downstream recursive caches.

choices.text: Immediately set the new record's TTL to 0 so that already-stored old responses are also removed at the same time.
choices.explanation: Changing the TTL of newly obtained responses does not change the expiration time already associated with previously cached responses.

choices.text: Enable Route 53 Resolver query logging to clear the caches of the internal resolvers.
choices.explanation: Enabling logging does not operate external recursive caches.

learning.reason: Recursive caches follow the TTL obtained before the update. Updating the authoritative side does not immediately clear old cached responses everywhere.
learning.concept: The authoritative update status and the expiration time of recursive caches on the client side are managed separately.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Maintaining Connections While Stopping New Routing During a Deployment
prompt: The old-version target behind an ALB can take up to 120 seconds to process an export request. During an update, new routing to the old version must end, and the old version must stop only after in-progress requests complete. You can keep the old version waiting for up to 180 seconds. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Set the ALB idle timeout to 180 seconds and immediately stop the old-version process.
choices.explanation: Extending the ALB connection timeout does not allow a stopped process to complete requests that are already in progress.

choices.text: Immediately make the old version fail the AWS health check and stop the production process at the same time.
choices.explanation: New requests may still be sent to the old version while it is being marked unhealthy, and in-progress requests cannot be maintained once the process stops.

choices.text: Set Slow start to 180 seconds and terminate the process while leaving the old version registered.
choices.explanation: Slow start gradually distributes load to a target that has become healthy; it does not give a stopping old version time to complete in-progress requests.

choices.text: Set the deregistration delay to 180 seconds, deregister the old version from the target group, and do not stop it until processing finishes.
choices.explanation: This removes new requests from the old version while allowing existing requests time to complete before the deadline.

learning.reason: This removes new requests from the old version while allowing existing requests time to complete before the deadline.
learning.concept: An ALB stops routing new requests to a deregistered target and uses the deregistration delay to give in-progress requests time to finish.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Shortening the period that a temporary 404 persists after origin recovery
prompt: Documents published dynamically through CloudFront briefly return 404 while synchronization is in progress at the origin. Even after the origin starts returning 200, some users continue to receive 404 responses for a while. The 404 response has no header that changes the caching time. Which option shortens only the retention period for this type of error without requiring a manual invalidation for every publication?

choices.text: Shorten the TTL of the record in Route 53 that points to CloudFront.
choices.explanation: Changing how frequently DNS results are refreshed does not change the amount of time CloudFront caches an HTTP error.

choices.text: Shorten the Error Caching Minimum TTL in the custom error configuration for 404 responses.
choices.explanation: Because the origin response does not override the caching time, CloudFront attempts to retrieve the object again sooner.

choices.text: Convert 404 responses to 200 for viewers while keeping the error caching time unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing only the response code does not resolve the problem of retaining the content from the stale error response.

choices.text: Shorten only the Default TTL for normal CloudFront objects.
choices.explanation: This broadly changes the caching policy for successful normal responses but does not directly configure the error caching time dedicated to 404 responses.

learning.reason: Because the origin response does not override the caching time, CloudFront attempts to retrieve the object again sooner.
learning.concept: CloudFront's Error Caching Minimum TTL controls the minimum time that a specified HTTP error response is cached before CloudFront retrieves it again.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Preventing mirror truncation caused by VXLAN overhead
prompt: In IPv4 VPC Traffic Mirroring, the source ENI has an MTU of 1,500, and the target ENI and the mirroring path can also handle an MTU of only 1,500. On the analysis side, only the end of large mirrored packets is missing. You must receive the mirrored packets in full without changing the MTU used by the workload. The MTU of the mirroring path can be changed. Which option is correct?

choices.text: Select only TCP in the source mirror filter and leave packet-size handling unchanged.
choices.explanation: Limiting the traffic to TCP does not eliminate the need to encapsulate the selected large packets.

choices.text: Ensure that the target ENI and the entire mirroring path can handle at least 1,554 bytes.
choices.explanation: This provides room to carry the original packet together with the IPv4 mirroring encapsulation.

choices.text: Switch only the mirroring source to jumbo frames and leave the target and path unchanged.
choices.explanation: Allowing even larger original packets leaves insufficient MTU capacity on the receiving side.

choices.text: Add UDP ports that support VXLAN and keep the target MTU at 1,500.
choices.explanation: The permitted UDP ports and frame size are independent, so this does not eliminate truncation at the end of the packet.

learning.reason: This provides room to carry the original packet together with the IPv4 mirroring encapsulation.
learning.concept: For IPv4 Traffic Mirroring, the target side needs 54 additional bytes of MTU capacity for the encapsulation.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Distinguishing probe loss from observations of the AWS network
prompt: Packet loss increased on probes from a VPC to an on-premises site using CloudWatch Network Synthetic Monitor. The Network Health Indicator was Healthy during the same period. The on-premises network and the dedicated connection are also monitored separately. How should this observation be handled?

choices.text: Because Healthy confirms a failure of the on-premises router, replace all equipment without investigating the dedicated connection.
choices.explanation: A single metric cannot identify the failure location outside AWS; the result must be correlated with other monitoring evidence.

choices.text: Treat the absence of a detected problem in the AWS-side observation separately from the loss actually observed across the probes, and correlate both with evidence from the dedicated connection and the on-premises site.
choices.explanation: Healthy is an observation about the AWS network and does not disprove loss measured by the probes or an end-to-end problem.

choices.text: Discard the probe result because Healthy guarantees that there is no loss anywhere along the path.
choices.explanation: The NHI is limited to the AWS network and does not have the same meaning as end-to-end packet loss.

choices.text: Investigate only a display delay because NHI must always become Degraded when loss is observed.
choices.explanation: The AWS-side investigation result and the probe result are separate sources of information and do not always agree.

learning.reason: Healthy is an observation about the AWS network and does not disprove loss measured by the probes or an end-to-end problem.
learning.concept: The Network Health Indicator reports observations about the AWS network; it does not indicate the health of the entire path measured by the probes.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Preventing a fallback to unencrypted transmission over a dedicated connection
prompt: A supported-location dedicated Direct Connect connection uses MACsec. Compatible devices at both ends are configured with the same MACsec key, and key registration is maintained. An audit requirement prohibits unencrypted frames from being transmitted if MACsec establishment fails. Which Direct Connect encryption mode should be used?

choices.text: Set the encryption mode to should_encrypt so that the connection remains active even if negotiation fails.
choices.explanation: This attempts to use MACsec but allows the connection to continue in plaintext when encryption cannot be established, which does not meet the requirement.

choices.text: Require TLS only for applications that use HTTPS and leave the Direct Connect encryption mode unchanged.
choices.explanation: Application-level TLS does not satisfy the requirement to prohibit plaintext frames across the dedicated connection.

choices.text: Configure BGP authentication on the virtual interface and allow plaintext transmission with MACsec.
choices.explanation: BGP authentication protects the routing-exchange adjacency; it does not enforce encryption of data frames on the connection.

choices.text: Set the Direct Connect encryption mode to must_encrypt.
choices.explanation: If MACsec cannot protect the connection, transmission does not continue in plaintext, satisfying the requirement that encryption be mandatory.

learning.reason: If MACsec cannot protect the connection, transmission does not continue in plaintext, satisfying the requirement that encryption be mandatory.
learning.concept: The must_encrypt MACsec mode does not fall back to plaintext transmission when link encryption cannot be established.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Accept Only Trusted Partner Certificates at the ALB
prompt: An external partner presents a client certificate to the ALB HTTPS listener. Configure the ALB to validate only certificates signed by the specified CA and prevent traffic that fails validation from reaching the backend. Do not add certificate-validation code to the application. What should you configure?

choices.text: Set the listener to mutual TLS verify mode and associate a trust store that contains the partner's CA.
choices.explanation: The ALB verifies the client's certificate trust and forwards only validated requests to the application.

choices.text: Add the ALB server certificate to the listener and only switch to HTTPS.
choices.explanation: This identifies the server and encrypts the connection, but it does not configure validation of the partner's certificate.

choices.text: Set the ALB health check to HTTPS and connect it to the business application's CA.
choices.explanation: This configures a connection used to monitor targets; it does not configure mutual authentication between the client and listener.

choices.text: Set the listener to mutual TLS passthrough mode without adding validation on the application side.
choices.explanation: Although the ALB can pass certificate information through, it does not perform the same client trust validation as verify mode.

learning.reason: The ALB verifies the client's certificate trust and forwards validated requests to the application.
learning.concept: ALB mutual TLS verify mode validates client certificates using the associated trust store.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Map Authorization Settings to Their Roles for Video Delivery
prompt: Deliver an HLS manifest and segments from CloudFront only to subscribed users. The player can send cookies, and the delivery URLs should not be changed individually. Match one component to each purpose. Use each candidate once.

choices.text: Signed cookies
choices.explanation: The player sends shared authorization information, allowing access to be controlled without changing the URLs of individual videos.

choices.text: A custom policy containing a resource pattern and an expiration time
choices.explanation: It expresses permission for multiple files under the same path as time-limited conditions.

choices.text: A trusted key group
choices.explanation: CloudFront uses it to group the public keys used to validate signatures accepted by the behavior.

learning.reason: The player sends shared authorization information, so access can be controlled without changing individual video URLs. CloudFront uses a trusted key group to validate accepted signatures. A custom policy defines the path range and expiration conditions for multiple files.
learning.concept: CloudFront signed cookies use key-based signatures and a custom policy to authorize multiple files without rewriting URLs.

prompts.text: For multiple video segments, the player sends common authorization information with each request.
For the target behavior, determine the public keys that CloudFront can trust for signature validation.
Specify the path range to which the signed authorization applies and the final time until which it can be used.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Have AWS Contact Operations Staff When a DDoS Event with Service Disruption Is Detected
prompt: There is a public ALB protected by Shield Advanced. A 24-hour contact is already available, and the organization wants the Shield Response Team to proactively contact operations staff when a covered event causes reduced service availability. Which monitoring configuration is required? Select two.

choices.text: Set all AWS Managed Rules managed rules for the ALB's WAF to Count.
choices.explanation: Although WAF detection can be observed, this does not enable automatic SRT contact or configure the required contacts.

choices.text: Deliver the ALB's VPC Flow Logs to S3 and make creation of those logs alone the condition for contacting SRT.
choices.explanation: Network observation logs alone do not satisfy the Shield Advanced health-check and proactive-response requirements.

choices.text: Enable proactive engagement and register the contacts and contact methods that SRT should use.
choices.explanation: This provides a way for SRT to contact the appropriate staff when a covered event is detected.

choices.text: Create a Route 53 health check that accurately represents the application's health and associate it with the ALB protection in Shield Advanced.
choices.explanation: SRT can evaluate the application's state during an alert and determine whether the event qualifies for proactive engagement.

choices.text: Change to AWS Shield Standard and retain the same proactive settings.
choices.explanation: SRT proactive engagement applies to resources protected by Shield Advanced.

learning.reason: SRT needs a way to evaluate the application's state during an alert and a way to contact the appropriate staff when a covered event is detected.
learning.concept: Shield Advanced proactive engagement uses a Route 53 health check associated with the protected resource together with contact settings.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Switch Only the False-Positive Managed Rule to Monitoring
prompt: A Web ACL uses an AWS Managed Rules rule group. One known subrule falsely matches valid API requests, so temporarily record matches for only that rule. Keep the current Block action for the other subrules. Which option should be used?

choices.text: Configure an Allow rule for the path that generated the false positive before the rule group.
choices.explanation: Requests for that path would no longer be evaluated by the group, so this would not preserve recording of the subrule's matches and protection by the other rules.

choices.text: Set the rule group's OverrideAction to Count.
choices.explanation: The evaluation result would be overridden to Count for the entire group, so blocking by the other subrules would not be preserved.

choices.text: Change the Web ACL default action to Allow without changing the subrules.
choices.explanation: If a valid request matches a subrule's Block action, evaluation ends there, so changing the default action to Allow does not avoid the block.

choices.text: Use RuleActionOverrides to specify the target subrule name and change its action to Count.
choices.explanation: Only the target rule becomes a measurement rule, while the actions of the other rules in the same rule group remain unchanged.

learning.reason: Only the target rule becomes a measurement rule, while the actions of the other rules in the same rule group remain unchanged.
learning.concept: RuleActionOverrides can change the action of each rule individually within a rule group.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Align Stateful Rule Action Order with the Operating Policy
prompt: In AWS Network Firewall Suricata-compatible rules, a rule with multiple actions can match the same inspection target as other rules. The administrator wants rules to be evaluated in the order of the audited rule group and in the order specified within the group, rather than in the default action-type order. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Use the default action order and set only the Suricata priority value for each rule.
choices.explanation: Rules with the same action can be prioritized, but the default order for different action types remains in effect.

choices.text: Configure the firewall policy and its associated stateful rule group with Strict order, specifying the group priority and the order within the group.
choices.explanation: This switches from the fixed action-type order and expresses the evaluation order specified for the rules.

choices.text: Assign integer sid values to each rule so that they appear in the desired order, while retaining the default action order.
choices.explanation: sid identifies a signature and does not override the default evaluation order for different actions.

choices.text: Allow all packets through stateless default processing and retain the stateful configuration.
choices.explanation: This does not replace the setting that forwards traffic for stateful inspection and does not define the rule-group evaluation order.

learning.reason: This switches from the fixed action-type order and expresses the evaluation order specified for the rules.
learning.concept: With Strict order, the rule-group priority in the policy and the order in which rules are written within the group are used.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Do Not Allow Uninspected UDP-Based Traffic
prompt: Outbound HTTPS from internal devices is subject to AWS Network Firewall TLS inspection. When a browser uses HTTP/3, it may switch to UDP-based QUIC. Company policy does not allow HTTPS traffic that cannot be inspected. Which design should be used?

choices.text: Add UDP 443 to the TLS inspection scope and inspect QUIC.
choices.explanation: Listing a port in the scope does not make TLS inspection possible for data using an unsupported transport.

choices.text: Do not allow QUIC in the application and network policies, and limit TLS inspection to supported HTTPS over TCP.
choices.explanation: This restricts traffic to a supported transport and prevents uninspected methods from passing.

choices.text: Enable Network Firewall flow logs and allow QUIC's encrypted data as is.
choices.explanation: Logs can preserve connection information, but this does not satisfy the requirement not to allow uninspected traffic.

choices.text: Allow UDP 443 in the network ACL and use Route 53 DNS logs as a substitute for decrypted results.
choices.explanation: DNS logs record queries; they do not inspect application content sent over QUIC.

learning.reason: This restricts traffic to a supported transport and prevents uninspected methods from passing.
learning.concept: AWS Network Firewall TLS inspection cannot inspect UDP-based QUIC.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Restrict Delivery to a Dedicated Organizational Logging Bucket
prompt: VPC Flow Logs from a workload account must be delivered to an S3 bucket in an audit account. The bucket must not be public, and log delivery must be limited to the specified account that owns the VPC. The workload must not be granted direct write permission to the bucket. Which bucket-side configuration should be used?

choices.text: Allow the log delivery service s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:PutObject for the specified prefix, and restrict access by the log-owning account and the log service's source ARN.
choices.explanation: This permits service-to-service delivery while reducing the risk that the same permissions can be used by an unauthorized source resource.

choices.text: Make the Amazon VPC service itself the principal in the bucket and allow any source account unconditionally.
choices.explanation: This incorrectly grants permission to the actual log-delivery actor and does not restrict the source.

choices.text: Attach PutObject permission for the destination bucket to the instance roles of all workload EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: This does not grant bucket-side permission to the service that delivers flow logs and instead gives direct write access to workload roles.

choices.text: Add the destination bucket to an S3 gateway endpoint and make the bucket policy unnecessary.
choices.explanation: Defining a service path for the workload VPC does not grant write permission to a cross-account delivery service.

learning.reason: This permits service-to-service delivery while reducing the risk that the same permissions can be used by an unauthorized source resource.
learning.concept: For S3 flow-log delivery, grant permission to the log delivery service and restrict the source with aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Apply a Common Regional Boundary Only to the Target OU
prompt: An organization managed by AWS Control Tower has a regulated OU and a general-business OU. In the regulated OU, users in member accounts with administrator permissions must be restricted from performing in-scope operations outside approved Regions, while Regions must remain unrestricted for the general-business OU. Exceptions for required global services must be manageable. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Enable Region deny for the entire landing zone and apply the same control to the general-business OU.
choices.explanation: This applies the restriction too broadly and does not match the objective of leaving the general-business OU unrestricted.

choices.text: Use an AWS Config aggregator to read resources by Region and deny operations that have already been detected as created.
choices.explanation: Aggregating state provides after-the-fact monitoring and cannot deny AWS API calls before they occur.

choices.text: Apply an OU-level Region deny control to the regulated OU and define the allowed Regions and exceptions for required global services.
choices.explanation: This applies a preventive organization-level restriction to the target OU without imposing the same restriction on the out-of-scope business OU.

choices.text: Change only the permissions of one IAM administrator role in the regulated accounts and retain all other permission paths.
choices.explanation: Changing one role does not create a common boundary that includes other principals in the same accounts.

learning.reason: This applies a preventive organization-level restriction to the target OU without imposing the same restriction on the out-of-scope business OU.
learning.concept: Control Tower's OU-level Region deny control can define a regional boundary for the target OU.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Use inbound rules independent of CIDR between connected VPCs
prompt: Two VPCs in the same Region are directly connected to the same Transit Gateway. The security group (SG) of the application that initiates the API call already allows outbound traffic. You want to restrict inbound traffic to the database by referencing the application SG instead of using a fixed CIDR. Select TWO actions that are required.

choices.text: Enable SG referencing on the database-side attachment while leaving the Transit Gateway itself disabled.
choices.explanation: The Transit Gateway setting is also required; enabling the feature only on the attachment is not sufficient.

choices.text: Create SGs with the same name in both VPCs and reference the SG with that name in the database VPC.
choices.explanation: SGs with the same name are different SGs, so the reference does not point to the SG used by the application.

choices.text: In the database SG's inbound rules, reference the application SG for the port that should be allowed.
choices.explanation: This allows the required inbound traffic based on the SG to which the application belongs, without specifying a fixed CIDR.

choices.text: Reference the database SG in the application SG's outbound rules and do not allow inbound traffic on the database side.
choices.explanation: SG referencing through a Transit Gateway is not supported in outbound rules, and an inbound rule is also required.

choices.text: Enable SG referencing on the Transit Gateway and on the applicable VPC attachments.
choices.explanation: This enables VPC-to-VPC SG referencing at both ends of the Transit Gateway path.

learning.reason: VPC-to-VPC SG referencing through the Transit Gateway requires the feature to be enabled on the Transit Gateway and the related VPC attachments, and it is used in inbound rules instead of fixed CIDRs.
learning.concept: Enable SG referencing on the Transit Gateway and its related VPC attachments, then use the application SG in the database SG's inbound rule.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Restore session establishment for a managed EC2 instance without opening inbound ports
prompt: An EC2 instance in a VPC without NAT uses the current SSM Agent. The instance appears as a managed node in Systems Manager, and the IAM permissions of the session initiator have been verified. A Regional endpoint for ssm exists, but there is no endpoint for session data. Which action enables management without opening inbound ports on the EC2 instance?

choices.text: Create an ssmmessages interface endpoint, enable private DNS, and allow HTTPS connections from the EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: This allows SSM Agent to connect from inside the VPC to the Session Manager messaging endpoint.

choices.text: Allow TCP 22 to the EC2 instance in the security group of the existing ssm endpoint.
choices.explanation: This does not add the HTTPS communication with ssmmessages required for the Session Manager channel.

choices.text: Create only a CloudWatch Logs VPC endpoint.
choices.explanation: The instance may reach the log destination, but this does not establish the control and data channels for an interactive session.

choices.text: Create an ec2 VPC endpoint and route session data through the EC2 API as well.
choices.explanation: The EC2 API endpoint and the Session Manager communication channel opened by SSM Agent are different.

learning.reason: SSM Agent must be able to connect from inside the VPC to the Session Manager messaging endpoint.
learning.concept: SSM Agent uses ssmmessages for the Session Manager communication channel.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Explicitly allow two groups to access the same host
prompt: In Client VPN authorization rules, the operations group is allowed to access 10.71.16.0/20, and the audit group is allowed to access 10.71.18.34/32, which is within that range. The operations group is not a member of the audit group and can no longer connect to that host. The routes are working normally, and the audit group's access must be preserved. Which rule should be changed?

choices.text: Re-create the /20 rule for the operations group and make it appear first in the authorization-rule list.
choices.explanation: Destination-prefix specificity takes precedence over the order in which rules are created.

choices.text: Delete the audit group's /32 rule and keep only the operations group's /20 rule.
choices.explanation: Although the broad permission could then apply to the operations group, the required audit-group access would not be preserved.

choices.text: Add an authorization rule that allows the operations group to access 10.71.18.34/32.
choices.explanation: Both groups can then be allowed by rules with the same longest prefix, while the operations group can continue using the rest of the /20 range.

choices.text: Allow all users to access 10.71.18.34/32 and omit the additional group configuration.
choices.explanation: This grants access to a broader set of users than the two groups intended to access the host.

learning.reason: Rules with the same longest prefix can allow both groups to access the host, while the operations group continues to use the rest of the /20 range.
learning.concept: Client VPN evaluates which groups are allowed using the most specific destination rule.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Evaluate overlapping private CIDRs together with a VPC identifier
prompt: Requests to Amazon S3 pass through a VPC endpoint. You want to allow only the IP range of a specific subnet in an approved VPC by using a bucket policy. Another VPC uses the same private CIDR, so the policy must check both the subnet address range and the VPC. Which condition should be used?

choices.text: Specify the allowed CIDR with aws:VpcSourceIp and also require the approved VPC ID with aws:SourceVpc.
choices.explanation: Requiring both conditions distinguishes requests from the same IP range reused in another VPC.

choices.text: Specify only the allowed CIDR with aws:VpcSourceIp.
choices.explanation: The same private IP range reused in another VPC could also match this condition.

choices.text: Specify the approved VPC with aws:SourceVpc and omit the source-IP condition.
choices.explanation: This cannot distinguish requests from other subnets in the VPC and does not restrict access to the CIDR.

choices.text: Evaluate the private CIDR with aws:SourceIp and identify the source VPC using only aws:PrincipalAccount.
choices.explanation: VPC endpoint traffic requires aws:VpcSourceIp for the source IP, and the caller's account does not identify the VPC through which the traffic passes.

learning.reason: Requiring both conditions distinguishes requests from another VPC that uses the same IP range.
learning.concept: aws:VpcSourceIp evaluates the source IP from a VPC. When ranges overlap, combine it with a VPC identity condition.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Validate public DNS signatures during recursive resolution in a VPC
prompt: An application in a VPC resolves signed public domains through AmazonProvidedDNS. You want DNSSEC validation to be performed by the Resolver for the target VPC without operating an external custom resolver. There is no requirement to change the signing configuration of your public hosted zones. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Include the authoritative DNS key in the CloudFront server certificate.
choices.explanation: A certificate that verifies a website's identity over HTTPS is not used to validate signatures during recursive DNS resolution.

choices.text: Configure DNSSEC signing for your public hosted zone.
choices.explanation: You can sign zone data that your organization publishes, but this does not configure the VPC resolver to validate domains queried externally.

choices.text: Enable DNSSEC validation in Route 53 Resolver for the target VPC.
choices.explanation: This enables validation of signed public DNS records during recursive resolution in the target VPC.

choices.text: Enable Route 53 Resolver query logging and have signatures validated when queries are recorded in the logs.
choices.explanation: Query logs store observational data. They do not validate the DNS chain of trust before returning an answer.

learning.reason: This enables validation of signed public DNS records during recursive resolution in the target VPC.
learning.concept: Route 53 VPC Resolver supports enabling DNSSEC validation at the VPC level.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Query network audit results across accounts from a central location
prompt: AWS Config recording and evaluation are already enabled in the organization's target accounts and Regions. From an audit account registered as the delegated administrator for Config, the audit team needs to query SG and VPN configurations and noncompliance results across accounts. Existing recorders and rules must continue running in their current locations, and central access must not modify individual resources. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Create a Config aggregator in the audit account using AWS Organizations as the source and aggregate information from the target Regions.
choices.explanation: Each account can continue recording and evaluating resources while the current configuration and evaluation results are queried centrally.

choices.text: Stop the Config recorders in all member accounts and use only the recorder in the audit account.
choices.explanation: The recorder in the audit account alone cannot preserve the resources and evaluation results recorded in each source account.

choices.text: Create an organization trail for CloudTrail in all target Regions and do not retrieve Config evaluation results.
choices.explanation: Although API events can be recorded, this does not meet the requirement to query configuration snapshots and Config noncompliance results.

choices.text: Add SG Describe actions to an Organizations SCP and store each account's evaluation results in the SCP itself.
choices.explanation: An SCP defines permission boundaries; it does not store resource state or Config evaluations.

learning.reason: Each account can continue recording and evaluating resources while the current configuration and evaluation results are queried centrally.
learning.concept: A Config organization aggregator collects configuration and evaluation information from multiple accounts and Regions for read-only access.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Protect the plaintext of selected form fields after TLS termination
prompt: CloudFront receives an HTTPS form and routes it to multiple origin services. Of the URL-encoded POST fields, only the payment identifier must be readable by the specified downstream service, while the existing services must continue processing the other fields. The specified service can store a private key. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Use server-side encryption for the entire form in the origin's log storage location.
choices.explanation: This protects the data after it is stored and does not hide the selected field from services before storage.

choices.text: Use HTTPS between CloudFront and the origin, then process every field in plaintext after TLS termination.
choices.explanation: The data is protected in transit, but the selected field can still be read by intermediate origin processing.

choices.text: Issue a signed cookie and pass all form field values in the existing plaintext format.
choices.explanation: Controlling viewer permissions does not change the condition that downstream services can read the selected form value.

choices.text: Apply field-level encryption with the selected fields and public key configured to the behavior, and use the private key only in the specified service.
choices.explanation: The selected fields remain encrypted after TLS terminates, while the other form values can continue to be processed as before.

learning.reason: The selected fields remain encrypted after TLS terminates, while the other form values can continue to be processed as before.
learning.concept: CloudFront field-level encryption encrypts selected POST fields with a public key and limits decryption to the party holding the corresponding private key.

title: Route only partners in the same geographic area to a dedicated endpoint
prompt: For a public API, route only DNS queries from contracted partners to a partner-only endpoint. Authentication and authorization are already implemented in each API. The IPv4 ranges of the query sources that Route 53 recognizes as partner networks can be identified in advance, and general users in the same city must continue receiving the existing public endpoint. The partner ranges must be reusable across multiple records. Choose TWO.

choices.text: Create IP-based records with the same name and type, and use different destinations for the partner location and the default side that handles other queries.
choices.explanation: This returns different destinations for queries matching the registered CIDR and queries that do not match that range.

choices.text: Group the partner ranges into CIDR locations and create a Route 53 CIDR collection.
choices.explanation: This stores the network ranges as named locations so the same classification can be used across records.

choices.text: Configure failover with the partner record as primary and the public record as secondary.
choices.explanation: Health can be evaluated for the primary, but this cannot express response conditions based on the network of the querying client.

choices.text: Give partners the same URL as before and return both destinations evenly with weighted DNS.
choices.explanation: Selection by ratio cannot associate the partners' CIDRs with a particular response.

choices.text: Route all queries from the city where the partners are located using geolocation routing.
choices.explanation: This would treat general users in the same geographic location as partners and cannot select the known corporate networks.

learning.reason: This stores the network ranges as named locations so the same classification can be used across records. It also returns different destinations for queries matching the registered CIDR and queries that do not match that range.
learning.concept: Route 53 IP-based routing selects a response using locations in a reusable CIDR collection.

title: Return Multiple Healthy IPv4 Addresses Without Adding an Intermediate Load Balancer
prompt: Four public UDP collectors have fixed public IPv4 addresses, and each collector already has an HTTPS health-check endpoint that indicates whether it can receive traffic. The application can retrieve multiple healthy addresses from DNS and choose among them. As long as at least two collectors are healthy, you want the addresses of all healthy collectors to be included in multiple answers under the same name, while individually unhealthy addresses are excluded. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Create a weighted-routing record for each IPv4 address and assign the same weight to all of them.
choices.explanation: Although this can specify the proportions among healthy choices, it is not intended to return multiple healthy values in the same response.

choices.text: Combine the four IP addresses into one simple-routing A record and monitor only one representative collector.
choices.explanation: A single health result cannot individually exclude other addresses in the same set.

choices.text: Register fixed primary and secondary collectors with failover routing and exclude the others from DNS.
choices.explanation: This does not return multiple collectors during normal operation and does not evaluate all four collectors as candidates.

choices.text: Create a multivalue A record for each IPv4 address under the same name and associate the health check for that collector with its record.
choices.explanation: Health can be evaluated at the record level, allowing multiple healthy addresses to be returned to clients.

learning.reason: Health can be evaluated at the record level, allowing multiple healthy addresses to be returned to clients.
learning.concept: Multivalue answers consider the health of each record and return up to eight values.

title: Retrieve Only the Required File Range on the First Request
prompt: Large map data is delivered through CloudFront, and clients request only the byte ranges they need by specifying Range. Because the custom origin ignores Range and returns 200 with the entire file, the transfer is large on a cache miss. Which option returns a partial response from the initial request without pre-populating the cache?

choices.text: In CloudFront, leave only HEAD enabled among the allowed HTTP methods to reduce file transfer.
choices.explanation: This changes the response to metadata only and cannot provide the partial data requested by the client.

choices.text: Increase the normal edge-cache TTL so that the entire object continues to be retrieved from the origin as before.
choices.explanation: This may increase subsequent cache hits, but the first response for a range that is not yet stored remains the full object.

choices.text: Forward the origin's full 200 response unchanged and add only Accept-Ranges through a response headers policy.
choices.explanation: Changing a capability-announcement header does not make the actual HTTP response the requested byte range.

choices.text: Implement the origin so that it accepts byte ranges and returns a 206 partial response with Content-Range.
choices.explanation: CloudFront can receive the requested range from the origin and deliver a partial response even for the initial request.

learning.reason: CloudFront can receive the requested range from the origin and deliver a partial response even for the initial request.
learning.concept: For a range cache miss, CloudFront uses the origin's Range support to deliver a partial response.

title: Maintain Different VIFs on One Physical Connection
prompt: A single 10 Gbps Direct Connect circuit simultaneously uses a public VIF for the public S3 endpoint and a transit VIF for Transit Gateway. You want to avoid adding circuits for each purpose and configure an independent VLAN and BGP session for each VIF. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Create one 10 Gbps hosted connection and place both VIFs on it because the bandwidth is sufficient.
choices.explanation: Regardless of the connection bandwidth, a hosted connection limits the number of VIFs that can be created.

choices.text: Register the hosted connection in a LAG to increase the hosted-connection VIF limit.
choices.explanation: A LAG bundles dedicated connections; it does not change the VIF constraint for a single hosted connection.

choices.text: Create only a public VIF on the hosted connection and exchange the related Transit Gateway private routes through the same VIF.
choices.explanation: A public VIF is for AWS public services and cannot replace a Transit Gateway connectivity use case.

choices.text: Use a dedicated connection and create two VIFs for different purposes on the same port.
choices.explanation: Multiple VIFs can operate over one physical connection, with tagging and peering configured separately for each VIF.

learning.reason: Multiple VIFs can operate over one physical connection, with tagging and peering configured separately for each VIF.
learning.concept: A Direct Connect hosted connection supports one VIF. Use a dedicated connection to place multiple VIFs on the same connection.

title: Provide a Single Resource to a Partner Without Adding a Load Balancer
prompt: A service-provider account has an existing TCP database that must be accessed privately from a consumer VPC through AWS PrivateLink. The consumer must not receive reachability to the entire VPC, and no load balancer may be added in front of the existing database. Both sides are in the corresponding same Region, and common Availability Zones can be secured on the consumer and provider sides. Which options should you choose? Select two.

choices.text: On the provider side, prepare a resource gateway and a resource configuration for the database, then share that configuration with the consumer.
choices.explanation: The resource configuration explicitly identifies what is provided and allows access to be granted to authorized accounts through AWS RAM.

choices.text: On the consumer side, create a resource VPC endpoint for the shared resource configuration.
choices.explanation: The consumer's endpoint ENIs provide the path for establishing a connection to the database.

choices.text: Peer the consumer and provider VPCs and propagate the provider VPC's CIDR to the route table.
choices.explanation: This creates VPC-to-VPC routing and does not provide the boundary of a resource endpoint for a single target.

choices.text: Place an NLB in the provider VPC and route database traffic through a traditional endpoint service.
choices.explanation: This can provide private access to the resource, but the scenario explicitly prohibits adding a load balancer.

choices.text: Register the database with an S3 gateway endpoint and reference it from the consumer VPC route table.
choices.explanation: Gateway endpoints support specified AWS services; an arbitrary TCP database cannot be registered with one.

learning.reason: The provider explicitly identifies the resource in a resource configuration and can grant access to an authorized account through AWS RAM. The consumer then establishes the database connection through the endpoint ENIs.
learning.concept: A PrivateLink resource endpoint connects to a shared resource through a resource gateway.

title: Manage API Delivery Settings with an Existing CloudFront Distribution
prompt: A company uses a single CloudFront distribution to deliver static pages and an API, and the team manages the behaviors, certificates, and header settings themselves. A new public REST API must be reachable from the internet as an origin for the existing distribution, and no additional managed global distribution should be added on the API Gateway side. Which API type should be used?

choices.text: Expose an Edge-optimized REST API in front of the existing CloudFront distribution.
choices.explanation: An Edge-optimized API adds an edge distribution managed by API Gateway, which does not meet the requirement to manage delivery through only the existing distribution.

choices.text: Create a public Regional REST API and configure it as the origin for the API behavior of the existing CloudFront distribution.
choices.explanation: The public Regional API can be called through the existing CloudFront distribution, allowing the distribution to manage the edge-delivery settings.

choices.text: Instead of an API, configure a CloudFront custom error page to process the received REST methods.
choices.explanation: A custom error page can change how an error response is displayed, but it does not execute a REST API or process integrations.

choices.text: Create a Private REST API and specify its standard public hostname as the internet-facing origin for CloudFront.
choices.explanation: A Private API is accessed through a corresponding VPC endpoint and does not satisfy the requirement to reference it directly as a public origin.

learning.reason: The public Regional API can be called through the existing CloudFront distribution, allowing the distribution to manage the edge-delivery settings.
learning.concept: A Regional REST API can be used as an origin for a CloudFront distribution that you manage yourself.

title: Distribute Common DNS Settings from Multiple Private Zones to a Fleet of VPCs
prompt: In a single Region, the same two private hosted zones and common Resolver settings must be applied to many VPCs. The operations team wants to manage one Route 53 Profile containing these settings and apply the same set to new VPCs in one operation. The Profile is available in the target account. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Disable private DNS support in each VPC before associating it.
choices.explanation: This removes the prerequisite for using the settings through the VPC Resolver and prevents common private name resolution from being maintained.

choices.text: Only share the common Resolver forwarding rules through AWS RAM.
choices.explanation: This provides access to the forwarding rules, but it does not apply the complete set of settings in the Profile, such as the private hosted zones.

choices.text: Do not use a Profile; duplicate the private hosted zones for each new VPC and manage them independently.
choices.explanation: The settings become duplicated and independently managed, so updates to the common Profile cannot be propagated to every VPC.

choices.text: Associate the target VPCs with the common Route 53 Profile.
choices.explanation: Associating each VPC applies the Profile's DNS settings and allows the same set to be reused for new VPCs.

learning.reason: Associating each VPC applies the Profile's DNS settings and allows the same set to be reused for new VPCs.
learning.concept: Associating a Route 53 Profile with a VPC applies the DNS resource settings stored in the Profile.

title: Separate Shared-Destination Updates from Per-Account Route Editing
prompt: Across VPCs in multiple accounts in the same Region, a central network team specifies many IPv4 networks that must be registered as destinations in routes used for reachability. The next hop differs by account. Only the network team should add or remove destination CIDRs, and those changes should be reflected without having each account rewrite the target of its existing routes. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Register all destination CIDRs statically in each account and standardize only the tag name.
choices.explanation: Tags cannot be referenced as route destinations, so each route would still need to be modified whenever the CIDRs change.

choices.text: Create an IPv4 customer-managed prefix list, share it through AWS RAM, and reference it as the destination of routes in each VPC.
choices.explanation: The owner can modify the common set of CIDRs, while each consumer continues to use the same set with its own next hop configured.

choices.text: Duplicate a prefix list with the same name in each account and assume that lists with the same name synchronize their contents.
choices.explanation: Lists with the same name are separate resources, so updates by the owner are not automatically synchronized to the independent lists.

choices.text: Add the network team's custom destination CIDRs to an AWS-managed prefix list.
choices.explanation: Users cannot add custom entries to a list managed by AWS for a service.

learning.reason: The owner can modify the common set of CIDRs, while each consumer continues to use the same set with its own next hop configured.
learning.concept: Routes that reference a shared customer-managed prefix list receive destination updates made to that same list.

title: Share One Endpoint Between IPv4 and IPv6 Applications
prompt: IPv4-only and IPv6-only applications coexist and connect to the same service. The service supports both address families for interface endpoints. One endpoint ENI should be placed in each Availability Zone, and both types of clients must connect using addresses within the VPC. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Set the endpoint IP address type to dual-stack and select subnets that have both IPv4 and IPv6 CIDRs.
choices.explanation: One ENI in each Availability Zone supports both address families, allowing both clients to use the required destination.

choices.text: Create an IPv6 endpoint and translate the IPv4 service destination to the endpoint's public IP address.
choices.explanation: Interface endpoint ENIs provide private access and do not provide an alternative entry point through a public IP address.

choices.text: Select the dual-stack type and specify IPv6-only subnets in each Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: IPv6-only subnets do not satisfy the requirement that the same ENI have both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses assigned.

choices.text: Create an IPv4 endpoint and set only the endpoint's DNS record type to dual-stack.
choices.explanation: This does not assign IPv6 addresses to the IPv4 endpoint ENIs to provide IPv6 destinations.

learning.reason: One ENI in each Availability Zone supports both address families, allowing both clients to use the required destination.
learning.concept: A dual-stack interface endpoint requires a service that supports both address families and subnets with IPv4 and IPv6 addressing.

title: Reach IPv6 resources while keeping the existing IPv4 tunnel entry point
prompt: Devices connecting to AWS Client VPN from a travel network must use an IPv4-only entry point for the new VPN. The VPN clients and applications in the VPC support both IPv4 and IPv6, and both legacy IPv4 services and new IPv6 services must be available through the tunnel. Which address settings should be used for the new endpoint?

choices.text: Set the endpoint to IPv6-only and traffic to dual-stack.
choices.explanation: Although the tunnel can handle both address families, devices that initiate the outer connection over IPv4 cannot connect.

choices.text: Set the endpoint IP address type to IPv4 and the traffic IP address type to dual-stack.
choices.explanation: This uses an IPv4 outer connection while allowing routes inside the tunnel to reach both IPv4 and IPv6 destinations.

choices.text: Set both the endpoint and traffic to IPv4-only.
choices.explanation: Devices can connect from the travel network, but the configuration does not provide the routes required for IPv6 services inside the tunnel.

choices.text: Set the endpoint to dual-stack and traffic to IPv6-only.
choices.explanation: The entry point can accept IPv4, but routes to existing IPv4 services cannot be established inside the tunnel.

learning.reason: Use an IPv4 outer connection while allowing routes inside the tunnel to reach both IPv4 and IPv6 destinations.
learning.concept: The address family used for Client VPN endpoint connections is configured separately from the address families for which the tunnel provides routes.

title: Place separate certificates on the viewer and origin sides
prompt: The CloudFront alternate domain name is www.example.com, and a public ALB in the Tokyo Region accepts connections for origin.example.com. Use HTTPS both from viewers to CloudFront and from CloudFront to the ALB, with the name matching on each connection. CloudFront connects using the origin domain name. Select two certificate-placement operations.

choices.text: Use a certificate only with CloudFront and use HTTP for the ALB connection.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement to protect the origin connection with HTTPS.

choices.text: Configure a certificate for only www.example.com on the ALB HTTPS listener and have CloudFront connect using origin.example.com.
choices.explanation: The certificate returned by the ALB does not match the origin name used by CloudFront.

choices.text: Obtain a certificate for origin.example.com in ACM in the Tokyo Region and associate it with the ALB HTTPS listener.
choices.explanation: The ALB can present a server certificate whose name matches the name used for CloudFront's origin connection.

choices.text: Obtain a certificate for www.example.com in ACM in us-east-1 and associate it with CloudFront.
choices.explanation: This satisfies both the Region requirement for a CloudFront viewer certificate in ACM and the name used by viewers.

choices.text: Use a www.example.com certificate in ACM in the Tokyo Region directly for CloudFront viewers from that same Region.
choices.explanation: An ACM certificate selected for viewers must be prepared in us-east-1.
