learning.reason: The CloudFront viewer certificate must satisfy the us-east-1 ACM requirement and use the viewer-facing name. The ALB must present a server certificate matching the name used for the CloudFront origin connection.
learning.concept: Use ACM in us-east-1 for the CloudFront viewer certificate, while an ELB origin can use a certificate in the Region where that origin resides.

title: Keep the client-side port while using the existing backend port
prompt: With a standard Global Accelerator, client devices already use TCP port 443 as the entry point. An NLB in one Region is shared with an existing system and listens on port 1443 for its backend. Other Regions continue to use port 443, and neither the NLB listeners nor the external clients can be changed. What should be changed?

choices.text: Change the accelerator listener to port 1443 in all Regions.
choices.explanation: This would also change the port used by clients and would not preserve the client configuration.

choices.text: Return the NLB's port 1443 appended to its IPv4 address in a Route 53 A record.
choices.explanation: A Route 53 A record carries an IPv4 address and does not rewrite a TCP port.

choices.text: In the endpoint group for the affected Region, override listener port 443 with destination port 1443.
choices.explanation: Clients continue to use the same public port, while traffic forwarded to the affected Region reaches the existing port.

choices.text: Only lower the endpoint group's traffic dial and do not specify a destination port.
choices.explanation: The amount of traffic sent to the group can be adjusted, but the TCP destination port does not change.

learning.reason: Clients continue to use the same public port, while traffic forwarded to the affected Region reaches the existing port.
learning.concept: An endpoint group in a standard accelerator can specify an override from the listener port to the destination port.

title: Move only a short API from an existing ALB to Lambda
prompt: An upload service using an existing ALB is being migrated incrementally. /meta receives JSON of 100 KB or less and responds quickly, while /upload receives 5 MB of data. Keep the ALB path routing and switch only the path whose synchronous processing fits the Lambda target path. Which option is correct?

choices.text: Extend the ALB idle timeout and receive the 5 MB body through a Lambda target.
choices.explanation: The connection-time setting does not change the request-body size limit for forwarding to a Lambda target.

choices.text: Forward both paths to Lambda and have the ALB split the 5 MB into multiple invocations.
choices.explanation: The ALB Lambda integration does not automatically split a body into multiple function invocations.

choices.text: Forward only /meta to a Lambda-type target group and keep /upload on the existing target group.
choices.explanation: Only the processing that fits within the Lambda limit is migrated, while the existing service continues to handle the large-payload path.

choices.text: Change the /meta target group to type ip and register the Lambda function's execution-environment IP address.
choices.explanation: To invoke Lambda from an ALB, configure Lambda as the target; do not register the function's execution environment as an IP target.

learning.reason: Only the processing that fits within the Lambda limit is migrated, while the existing service continues to handle the large-payload path.
learning.concept: Requests sent to an ALB Lambda target and the Lambda response JSON each have a 1 MB limit.

title: Send only selected inbound traffic arriving at a VPC to an existing inspection target
prompt: In a VPC with an internet gateway, send only IPv4 inbound traffic destined for a payment subnet among the public subnets through an existing firewall in the same VPC. A public IP required by the inspection ENI is assigned, and the symmetric return path is configured. Without changing inbound paths for other subnets, how should the direction arriving from the IGW be configured?

choices.text: Create a NAT gateway in each subnet and make it the forwarding target for the payment subnet in the IGW gateway route table.
choices.explanation: A NAT gateway is not one of the inspection-path targets that can be specified in a gateway route table.

choices.text: Replace the VPC-wide local route in the IGW gateway route table with the inspection ENI.
choices.explanation: This would send inbound traffic to other subnets through the inspection path as well.

choices.text: Associate a gateway route table with the IGW and route the payment subnet CIDR to the inspection ENI.
choices.explanation: Only inbound traffic destined for the specified subnet matches the more specific route; other destinations can continue using the existing local route.

choices.text: Change only the payment subnet's outbound route table and assume that the same table applies to inbound traffic from the IGW.
choices.explanation: Changing only the subnet's outbound configuration does not change the first forwarding target for packets received by the IGW.

learning.reason: Only traffic destined for the specified subnet matches the more specific route, while other destinations use the existing local route.
learning.concept: A gateway route table associated with an IGW can forward inbound traffic destined for a specified subnet to an inspection ENI in the same VPC.

title: Design the network for tightly communicating compute nodes
prompt: In EC2 scientific computing, an MPI job that supports Libfabric frequently exchanges short messages among many nodes. The compute nodes can be placed in the same AZ, so low-latency transfer that bypasses the OS network stack should be used. Which option meets the requirement?

choices.text: Use an internal ALB to distribute converted HTTP requests to the compute nodes.
choices.explanation: HTTP load balancing does not provide the low-latency Libfabric path required for MPI transfers between compute nodes.

choices.text: Enable EFA on each node and use EFA's OS-bypass communication between different AZs.
choices.explanation: EFA traffic has AZ restrictions, so nodes in multiple AZs cannot be connected through the same EFA path.

choices.text: Enable EFA on supported instance types and place the MPI job's nodes in the same AZ.
choices.explanation: This enables node-to-node communication over an OS-bypass path using EFA through Libfabric.

choices.text: Use only ENA and assume that ordinary TCP/IP communication automatically becomes the Libfabric EFA path.
choices.explanation: Improving the ordinary IP network is separate from EFA OS bypass; an EFA interface must be provided.

learning.reason: The nodes can communicate through an OS-bypass path using EFA through Libfabric.
learning.concept: Elastic Fabric Adapter provides supported applications with low-latency OS bypass, and its traffic cannot cross AZ boundaries.

title: Forward between dedicated-line sites without entering a cloud VPC
prompt: Two on-premises sites use separate Direct Connect locations and have private VIFs associated with a Direct Connect gateway in the same AWS partition. The advertised ranges for the sites do not overlap. Which option enables the sites to communicate with each other over the AWS backbone without relaying through a VPC in an AWS Region?

choices.text: Register the physical connections in the same LAG spanning both locations.
choices.explanation: A LAG bundles physical connections terminating on the same device; it does not provide a path between distant PoPs.

choices.text: Replace each VIF with a public VIF and connect to the other site's private range through routes for AWS public services.
choices.explanation: A VIF for AWS public services does not provide private route exchange between the two sites.

choices.text: Enable SiteLink on the relevant VIF at both sites and verify that each site's prefixes are learned by the other.
choices.explanation: SiteLink can connect the sites through available AWS network paths between Direct Connect PoPs.

choices.text: Create a transit VPC in an AWS Region and forward traffic between the sites through Transit Gateway.
choices.explanation: This can be designed, but it does not satisfy the condition of avoiding a transit VPC in a Region.

learning.reason: The sites can be connected between Direct Connect PoPs using available AWS network paths.
learning.concept: SiteLink can provide a site-to-site path between supported VIFs without traversing a VPC in an AWS Region.

title: Authenticate and retrieve container layers without using NAT
prompt: Launch an ECS Fargate task on the Linux platform version 1.4.0 in a private subnet. The task retrieves an existing image from a private ECR repository in the same Region. The task execution role is properly configured, and neither internet connectivity nor NAT is used. Select two routes required to retrieve the image.

choices.text: Allow HTTPS egress to public IP addresses in the task security group; no route to the internet is needed.
choices.explanation: Allowing egress in a security group does not create a route from an isolated subnet to the required services.

choices.text: Configure an S3 gateway endpoint used to retrieve the image layers in the task's route table.
choices.explanation: This provides private access to S3, where the container image layers associated with ECR are stored.

choices.text: Attach a DynamoDB gateway endpoint instead of a route to S3.
choices.explanation: A DynamoDB endpoint cannot retrieve the S3 objects that store the ECR image layers.

choices.text: Create only an interface endpoint for the ECS control plane and omit the ECR interface endpoints.
choices.explanation: Access to services used to manage task startup does not provide reachability to the ECR authentication and image retrieval endpoints.

choices.text: Provide interface endpoints for both ecr.api and ecr.dkr.
choices.explanation: Authentication and Docker registry access can be performed through VPC endpoints.

learning.reason: Authentication and Docker registry access can use VPC endpoints, while the S3 image-layer objects can be reached privately.
learning.concept: For private ECR image retrieval on the current Fargate platform, routes to ECR API, the Docker registry, and S3 are required.

title: Consolidating access to replicated data behind one nearby entry point
prompt: S3 buckets exist in multiple Regions, and the data for distribution has already been replicated to each Region. You want clients everywhere to use the same S3 entry point and retrieve data from the nearest available Region without implementing client-side measurements or switching between Region-specific bucket names. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Recreate only the cross-Region replication rules and configure clients with the original single-Region bucket name.
choices.explanation: Replication makes the data available in each Region, but requests to the original bucket name are not automatically routed to the nearest Region.

choices.text: Create a single S3 Regional Access Point and specify all buckets in other Regions through that one Access Point.
choices.explanation: A standard Access Point provides an entry point to a specified bucket; it does not combine multiple Regions.

choices.text: Set up an S3 Multi-Region Access Point that includes multiple buckets, and have clients use its global endpoint.
choices.explanation: Clients connect to the same entry point, and S3 can direct access to a bucket in a nearby available Region.

choices.text: Have the application measure every Region at startup and connect directly to the bucket with the shortest latency.
choices.explanation: Although this can provide routing, it requires the client-side measurements and destination switching excluded by the requirements.

learning.reason: Clients connect to the same entry point, and S3 can direct access to a bucket in a nearby available Region.
learning.concept: An S3 Multi-Region Access Point can provide a common global endpoint for S3 buckets in multiple Regions.

title: Specifying which CAs may issue certificates for a public domain
prompt: The operations team manages a public zone in Route 53. api.example.com runs with an alias A record, and the team wants to indicate through DNS that only approved certificate authorities may issue standard TLS server certificates. Ownership validation and the existing address record must remain unchanged. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Create the ACM ownership-validation CNAME once and then delete it so that other certificate authorities can no longer issue certificates in the future.
choices.explanation: Ownership validation for a specific issuance procedure is a different mechanism from specifying which certificate authorities the domain generally permits to issue certificates.

choices.text: Create a CAA record for api.example.com that specifies the approved certificate authority identifiers with the issue tag.
choices.explanation: The address A record can remain unchanged, and the issuing party can determine the permitted CAs from DNS.

choices.text: Increase the TTL of the existing A record and preferentially deliver it to the DNS resolvers of the approved certificate authorities.
choices.explanation: The cache duration of an address record does not indicate which certificate authorities may issue certificates.

choices.text: Enable DNSSEC signing and do not create a DNS record that specifies certificate authorities.
choices.explanation: DNSSEC can verify the authenticity of DNS responses, but it does not provide a list of certificate authorities permitted to issue certificates.

learning.reason: The address A record can remain unchanged, and the issuing party can determine the permitted CAs from DNS.
learning.concept: The CAA issue tag specifies which certificate authorities are permitted to issue certificates for a domain.

title: Accepting DNS forwarding from on premises over both protocols
prompt: An on-premises recursive resolver conditionally forwards queries for a private hosted zone in a VPC to an inbound Resolver endpoint. The security group for the endpoint ENIs must follow least privilege. Which configuration accepts standard DNS queries and retries for large responses from the on-premises CIDR? Select two.

choices.text: Allow UDP 53 from the on-premises CIDR in the security group's inbound rules.
choices.explanation: UDP 53 is required to receive ordinary DNS queries.

choices.text: Set the on-premises CIDR as a local target in the VPC route table.
choices.explanation: A local route is used for traffic within the VPC CIDR and does not create a route to on-premises networks.

choices.text: Allow only TCP 443 from the on-premises CIDR in the security group's inbound rules.
choices.explanation: Port 443 is not the receiving port for DNS queries.

choices.text: Allow UDP 53 to the on-premises CIDR only in the security group's outbound rules.
choices.explanation: Reaching an inbound endpoint requires an inbound rule on its ENIs.

choices.text: Allow TCP 53 from the on-premises CIDR in the security group's inbound rules.
choices.explanation: DNS also uses TCP for large responses and retries, so TCP 53 must be allowed.

learning.reason: UDP 53 is required to receive ordinary DNS queries. DNS also uses TCP for large responses and retries, so TCP 53 must be allowed.
learning.concept: An inbound Resolver endpoint receives queries on TCP and UDP port 53.

title: Making the forwarding point to on-premises DNS resilient to an AZ failure
prompt: Applications in a VPC conditionally forward names in corp.example to on-premises DNS. The solution must keep name resolution running through a single-AZ failure and use an AWS-managed Resolver as the forwarding source. Which option creates the outbound Resolver endpoint?

choices.text: Configure the on-premises DNS server directly in /etc/resolv.conf on each application EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: This does not provide VPC-wide conditional forwarding or an AZ-redundant Resolver configuration.

choices.text: Specify the EIP of a NAT Gateway in one AZ as the source for the forwarding rule.
choices.explanation: A Resolver rule does not use a NAT Gateway as a DNS forwarding endpoint.

choices.text: Create an outbound Resolver endpoint with at least two IP addresses in subnets in different AZs, and use it as the source for the forwarding rule.
choices.explanation: Endpoint IP addresses across AZs improve the availability of conditional forwarding.

choices.text: Create only an inbound Resolver endpoint.
choices.explanation: An inbound endpoint receives queries from on premises into the VPC; it is not the forwarding source for queries from the VPC to external DNS.

learning.reason: Endpoint IP addresses across AZs improve the availability of conditional forwarding.
learning.concept: For high availability, assign IP addresses in multiple AZs to an outbound Resolver endpoint.

title: Make the endpoint service name transparent through an internal DNS name
prompt: A service provider account publishes an Endpoint service backed by an NLB. The provider configures a Private DNS name so consumers can connect to the interface endpoint using the provider's custom service DNS name. Which action is required to securely verify ownership of the domain?

choices.text: Create only an A record in the consumer VPC's private hosted zone.
choices.explanation: An A record on the consumer side does not verify the service provider's ownership of the domain.

choices.text: Create the verification TXT record provided by AWS in the domain's public DNS and wait for verification to complete.
choices.explanation: AWS verifies ownership of the domain used for the Private DNS name with a TXT record.

choices.text: Configure the NLB IP address as the DNS name for the Endpoint service.
choices.explanation: A Private DNS name must be a domain whose ownership can be verified; setting the NLB IP does not bypass verification.

choices.text: Require Endpoint connection acceptance so that DNS ownership verification is unnecessary.
choices.explanation: Connection acceptance and domain verification for the Private DNS name are independent settings.

learning.reason: AWS verifies ownership of the domain used for a Private DNS name with a TXT record.
learning.concept: An Endpoint service Private DNS name requires domain ownership verification using the TXT record provided by AWS.

title: Assign contiguous IP addresses when increasing Pod density
prompt: An Amazon EKS IPv4 cluster uses the Amazon VPC CNI on EC2 worker nodes. You want to increase the number of Pods on supported Nitro instances, but available IP addresses in the existing subnet are fragmented. There is no need to isolate Pods in a separate CIDR. Select two actions required to introduce prefix-based allocation.

choices.text: If the subnet has more than 16 free IP addresses in total, specify a noncontiguous range that spans used addresses as a /28.
choices.explanation: A prefix requires a contiguous address range; separate free IP addresses cannot be combined.

choices.text: Enable IPv4 prefix delegation in the VPC CNI.
choices.explanation: IPv4 prefixes can be assigned to network interfaces and used as Pod IP addresses.

choices.text: Keep IPv4 allocation unchanged and add only VPC IPv6 addresses to the nodes.
choices.explanation: This does not configure VPC CNI IPv4 prefix delegation for Pods, so it does not resolve the IPv4 constraint.

choices.text: Use a subnet for the nodes where a contiguous /28 can be reserved and, if necessary, reserve the prefix range with a subnet CIDR reservation.
choices.explanation: Even with many individually free IP addresses, fragmented space cannot be assigned as a contiguous prefix.

choices.text: Expand the Kubernetes Service CIDR so that /28 prefixes are automatically assigned to the VPC ENIs.
choices.explanation: The virtual address range for Services is different from the IPv4 prefixes that the VPC CNI assigns to ENIs.

learning.reason: IPv4 prefixes can be assigned to network interfaces and used as Pod IP addresses, but fragmented free addresses cannot form a contiguous prefix.
learning.concept: VPC CNI IPv4 prefix allocation uses a contiguous /28, so the total number of free IP addresses alone is insufficient.

title: Add a new Availability Zone to a PrivateLink service
prompt: You want to add low-latency connectivity for a partner in another Availability Zone to an existing Endpoint service. The NLB does not yet have a subnet enabled in that Availability Zone. What is the first change required before the Availability Zone can be added to the Endpoint service?

choices.text: Register one IP address from the other Availability Zone in the NLB target group without adding an NLB subnet.
choices.explanation: Target placement does not enable an NLB node or an Endpoint service in that Availability Zone.

choices.text: Add the NLB IP address as a static entry in the consumer VPC route table.
choices.explanation: PrivateLink Availability Zone availability is not enabled through the consumer's route table.

choices.text: First add a subnet from that Availability Zone to the NLB to enable the Availability Zone, and then make it available in the Endpoint service.
choices.explanation: An Endpoint service adds Availability Zones based on the Availability Zones provided by its NLB.

choices.text: Change the Endpoint service's Private DNS name to the new Availability Zone name.
choices.explanation: A Private DNS name is a domain name and does not add an Availability Zone enabled on the NLB.

learning.reason: An Endpoint service adds available Availability Zones based on the Availability Zones provided by its NLB.
learning.concept: The Availability Zones available through an Endpoint service are provided by the Availability Zones enabled on the backing NLB.

title: Restrict sources reaching an NLB from the time of creation
prompt: You are creating a new internet-facing NLB. You want to manage the source CIDRs with a Security Group and be able to change the rules later. Which two actions are correct for NLB creation and inbound control? Select two.

choices.text: Create the NLB without a Security Group and associate one only after it is running.
choices.explanation: A Security Group cannot be associated later with an NLB that was created without one.

choices.text: Leave the inbound NACL rules empty and automatically associate a Security Group with the NLB.
choices.explanation: NACLs and associating a Security Group with an NLB are separate features.

choices.text: Associate at least one Security Group when creating the NLB.
choices.explanation: An NLB created with a Security Group can continue to have its Security Groups and rules managed.

choices.text: Use only the target's Security Group to restrict client ingress to the NLB.
choices.explanation: The target Security Group protects the backend but does not add source control to the NLB itself.

choices.text: In the inbound rules of the associated Security Group, allow only the required client CIDRs and listener ports.
choices.explanation: The Security Group can minimize the sources and ports that can reach the NLB.

learning.reason: An NLB created with a Security Group can continue to have its Security Groups and rules managed, and its inbound sources and ports can be minimized with those rules.
learning.concept: To use Security Groups with an NLB, you must associate at least one Security Group when creating the NLB.

title: Terminate TLS and centrally manage certificates with an NLB
prompt: A partner connects to the fixed IP address of an NLB over TLS. The backend TCP services must remain plain TCP, and certificate updates should not have to be distributed to each backend. Which NLB listener configuration meets these requirements?

choices.text: Associate an ACM certificate with a UDP listener.
choices.explanation: A UDP listener is not used to terminate TLS.

choices.text: Have an HTTP listener on an ALB serve as the NLB's certificate store.
choices.explanation: A listener on a different load balancer does not configure TLS termination on the NLB.

choices.text: Configure a TLS listener on the NLB with an ACM certificate and a TCP target group.
choices.explanation: The NLB can terminate TLS and communicate with the backends over TCP.

choices.text: Configure a TCP listener and a TLS target group, expecting the NLB to renew the certificate automatically.
choices.explanation: A TCP listener does not terminate TLS or use a certificate.

learning.reason: The NLB can terminate TLS while the backends communicate over TCP.
learning.concept: An NLB TLS listener uses a certificate to terminate TLS and can forward traffic to TCP targets.

title: Authenticate unauthenticated users before they reach the application with an ALB
prompt: An internal web application is behind an ALB. The organization wants to authenticate users with an OIDC provider without modifying the application. Which ALB implementation prevents requests that fail authentication from being forwarded to the application target?

choices.text: Configure the authenticate-oidc action before the forward action in an HTTPS listener rule.
choices.explanation: The listener rule can forward requests to the target only after authentication succeeds.

choices.text: Set the OIDC issuer URL in the target group's health check.
choices.explanation: A health check verifies backend health; it does not authenticate clients.

choices.text: Configure the OIDC client secret on an NLB TLS listener.
choices.explanation: An NLB listener does not provide the ALB OIDC authentication action.

choices.text: Enable ALB access logs so unauthenticated requests are rejected automatically.
choices.explanation: Access logs provide observability; they do not enforce authentication or rejection policies.

learning.reason: Only successfully authenticated requests are forwarded to the target.
learning.concept: The authenticate-oidc action in an ALB listener rule can perform OIDC authentication before forwarding.

title: Protect a production ALB from accidental deletion through IaC
prompt: An operations team is organizing the CloudFormation stack that manages a production ALB. They want to reduce the risk that an operator accidentally deletes the ALB or that a stack update replaces it. The requirement is deletion protection that rejects deletion APIs, not a feature that stops load balancing during a temporary outage. Which option meets the requirement?

choices.text: Set the ALB attribute deletion_protection.enabled to true, requiring explicit disabling before deletion.
choices.explanation: This protects the ALB from deletion through a deletion API or stack deletion.

choices.text: Extend the target group's deregistration delay.
choices.explanation: Connection draining during deregistration does not reject the deletion operation itself.

choices.text: Set the listener's default action to return a fixed response.
choices.explanation: This only changes responses temporarily; it does not prevent ALB deletion.

choices.text: Change the ALB to an internal scheme.
choices.explanation: Whether the ALB is public or internal is not a deletion-protection setting.

learning.reason: Deletion through a deletion API or stack deletion can be protected.
learning.concept: When ALB deletion protection is enabled, the ALB cannot be deleted until deletion protection is disabled.

title: Prevent overlapping inside CIDRs for multiple VPN connections
prompt: Multiple AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections from different site routers will be added to the same virtual private gateway. Static routing will be used for each tunnel. To avoid future problems, what policy should be used to assign the tunnel inside IPv4 CIDRs?

choices.text: Specify the CIDR only on the AWS-side tunnel and have the customer gateway automatically detect the same CIDR.
choices.explanation: Both ends must use matching inside-tunnel address settings, and overlaps must also be avoided.

choices.text: Set 0.0.0.0/0 as the inside CIDR for every tunnel.
choices.explanation: Inside-tunnel CIDRs must use an allowed /30 range; a default route is not specified here.

choices.text: Reuse the site's LAN CIDR as the inside CIDR for every tunnel.
choices.explanation: Inside-tunnel CIDRs are not reused LAN addresses; they must be nonoverlapping across VPN tunnels.

choices.text: Assign each tunnel a permitted /30 inside IPv4 CIDR that does not overlap with any other connection to the same VGW.
choices.explanation: This keeps tunnel inside CIDRs unique across multiple VPN connections using static routing.

learning.reason: Tunnel inside CIDRs can remain unique across multiple VPN connections using static routing.
learning.concept: When static routing is used for VPN connections to the same VGW, the tunnel inside IPv4 CIDRs must not overlap.

title: Obtain a configuration template for a customer gateway device
prompt: A network administrator wants to securely obtain the customer gateway device configuration for an existing AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection in the format recommended by AWS. Which task allows the administrator to select the device vendor, platform, and IKE version?

choices.text: Download the NLB health check configuration and apply it to the device.
choices.explanation: An NLB health check is not a configuration for a Site-to-Site VPN device.

choices.text: Register the customer gateway's public IP address in a Route 53 A record.
choices.explanation: DNS registration does not generate encryption, BGP, or tunnel settings for the VPN connection.

choices.text: In the Site-to-Site VPN connection configuration download, select the device vendor, platform, software, and IKE version, then obtain the configuration file.
choices.explanation: AWS generates device configuration corresponding to the connection ID.

choices.text: Recover the IPsec configuration from VPC Flow Logs and load it onto the device.
choices.explanation: Flow Logs do not provide an IPsec parameter configuration template.

learning.reason: AWS generates device configuration corresponding to the connection ID.
learning.concept: AWS provides configuration based on the vendor, platform, and software selected in the VPN connection configuration download.

title: Discard stale SAs from an unresponsive VPN peer quickly
prompt: After a branch router failure, the AWS-side VPN tunnel retains the Security Association with the unresponsive peer, delaying reestablishment. After detecting the failure, the administrator wants to clear the AWS-side tunnel state and proceed with renegotiation. Which tunnel option should be configured?

choices.text: Set the DPD timeout action for the affected tunnel to clear, and align the DPD settings on the customer gateway.
choices.explanation: After DPD detects an unresponsive peer, AWS can clear the stale tunnel state.

choices.text: Increase the CloudTrail trail retention period.
choices.explanation: Retaining audit records longer does not speed up tunnel reestablishment.

choices.text: Increase the number of BGP AS_PATH prepends.
choices.explanation: This can change route preference, but it does not clear the IPsec SA on a DPD timeout.

choices.text: Change the VPN tunnel's inside CIDR to 0.0.0.0/0.
choices.explanation: The inside CIDR does not configure failure detection by DPD or SA-clearing behavior.

learning.reason: After DPD detects an unresponsive peer, AWS can clear the stale tunnel state.
learning.concept: When the DPD timeout action is set to clear, the AWS-side tunnel is cleared after a DPD timeout.

title: Register the destination for a branch that cannot use BGP
prompt: A branch router before a hardware refresh supports IPsec but cannot use BGP. In AWS, a virtual private gateway terminates the Site-to-Site VPN for the VPC. The network used at the branch is the fixed 10.22.16.0/20, and the required route propagation on the VPC side is already configured. What should be specified for the VPN connection?

choices.text: Use dynamic routing for the VPN and assume that the customer gateway's IP address can be used as a route even without receiving BGP advertisements from the branch.
choices.explanation: The customer gateway's public IP is the IKE and IPsec peer address; it is not an advertised prefix for the branch network.

choices.text: Use static routing for the VPN and register the branch's 10.22.16.0/20 as a static route for the VPN connection.
choices.explanation: Because AWS does not learn the destination through BGP, specify the branch prefix to which traffic must be forwarded in the VPN connection.

choices.text: Use dynamic routing for the VPN and use the /30 of the tunnel inside IPv4 CIDR as the route to the entire branch.
choices.explanation: The link addresses inside the tunnel and the destination network within the branch are different.

choices.text: Select static routing for the VPN and register the VPC's own CIDR, rather than the branch network, as a static route.
choices.explanation: AWS needs the branch destination reachable through the VPN; the VPC's own CIDR does not represent the branch.

learning.reason: Because AWS does not learn the destination through BGP, specify the branch prefix to which traffic must be forwarded in the VPN connection.
learning.concept: Use static routing for a customer gateway that cannot use BGP, and explicitly specify the network destined for the branch.

title: Distribute Transit Gateway attachment permissions only to specified accounts in the organization
prompt: A network account centrally owns a Transit Gateway and wants only two application accounts in the organization to create VPC attachments. The administrator wants to avoid making the Transit Gateway available to all accounts or transferring ownership. Which mechanism should be used?

choices.text: Have each application account create a new Transit Gateway with the same TGW ASN.
choices.explanation: Separate Transit Gateways do not share the central Transit Gateway or provide shared connectivity.

choices.text: Automatically approve VPC peering across the organization.
choices.explanation: VPC peering does not distribute permission to create Transit Gateway attachments.

choices.text: Share only the Transit Gateway route table with RAM and do not share the Transit Gateway itself.
choices.explanation: The Transit Gateway resource itself must be shared to create a VPC attachment.

choices.text: Use an AWS RAM resource share to share the Transit Gateway with the two specified accounts.
choices.explanation: Ownership remains centralized, while only the shared accounts can create attachments.

learning.reason: Ownership remains centralized, while only the shared accounts can create attachments.
learning.concept: A Transit Gateway can be shared through AWS RAM with specified AWS accounts, organizational units, or the organization.

title: Safely Passing Network Stack Outputs to an Application Stack
prompt: A network foundation stack creates a VPC and subnets in the same account and Region. An application stack uses the subnet ID to create an interface endpoint. Which CloudFormation method avoids manually entering or duplicating the value and explicitly establishes the dependency between the stacks?

choices.text: Directly reference a CloudFormation Export from another Region by using Fn::ImportValue.
choices.explanation: Export/ImportValue cannot be referenced across Regions.

choices.text: Export the network stack's Output and reference the subnet ID in the application stack by using Fn::ImportValue.
choices.explanation: Output values can be reused between stacks in the same account and Region.

choices.text: Store the VPC ID in an AMI tag and have CloudFormation retrieve it automatically.
choices.explanation: An AMI tag is not a mechanism for referencing stack outputs.

choices.text: Have the application stack guess the network stack's physical ID and concatenate it into a string.
choices.explanation: Depending on logical IDs or generated names does not provide a stable contract between stacks.

learning.reason: Output values can be reused between stacks in the same account and Region.
learning.concept: CloudFormation can reference an exported Output from another stack in the same Region by using Fn::ImportValue.

title: Reviewing Network Changes Before Applying Them
prompt: An existing stack manages the route table association for a production subnet. You want to reduce the risk of associating the wrong subnet after a template update and present the changes to an approver before modifying the real resources. Which CloudFormation feature should you use?

choices.text: Execute the change directly and restore the differences from CloudTrail if the operation fails.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail provides post-event auditing and does not support approval of changes before they are applied.

choices.text: Create a Change set for the update, review the replacement or modification of the route table association, and then execute it.
choices.explanation: You can review the changes CloudFormation will make before executing them.

choices.text: Run only CloudFormation drift detection.
choices.explanation: drift detection checks differences between the current physical resources and the template; it is not a preview of a planned update.

choices.text: Delete the stack and recreate it with the new template.
choices.explanation: This could destroy the production network and does not provide a pre-change review.

learning.reason: You can review the changes CloudFormation will make before executing them.
learning.concept: A Change set previews the additions, modifications, and deletions that will occur during a stack update.

title: Safely Bringing an Existing Route Table Under CloudFormation Management
prompt: An existing route table in a production VPC was created manually, and you want to manage it with a CloudFormation stack without interrupting traffic. Which two actions bring the current physical resource into the template and stack instead of deleting and recreating it? Select two.

choices.text: Run only drift detection to make the existing route table a managed resource.
choices.explanation: drift detection checks differences from resources already under management; it does not import an unmanaged resource.

choices.text: Specify a DeletionPolicy for the logical resource being imported.
choices.explanation: The template for a resource import must include a DeletionPolicy for the resource being imported.

choices.text: Create a new route table and immediately replace it for all existing subnets.
choices.explanation: A misconfiguration during replacement could interrupt traffic, and this does not import the existing resource.

choices.text: Create a StackSet and wait for existing resources to be discovered automatically.
choices.explanation: StackSets deploy stacks across multiple accounts and Regions; they do not automatically import existing resources.

choices.text: Identify the current route table in the template and use a resource import operation to bring the existing physical resource into the stack.
choices.explanation: You can begin managing the existing resource with CloudFormation without deleting or recreating it.

learning.reason: You can begin managing the existing resource with CloudFormation without deleting or recreating it. The template for a resource import must include a DeletionPolicy for the resource being imported.
learning.concept: CloudFormation resource import brings an existing resource under stack management without deleting it, and the template must include a DeletionPolicy.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Identifying an Excessive Drop Rate on a NAT Gateway
prompt: Connection failures have been reported for traffic passing through a NAT gateway. New connection port allocation failures are zero, but packet drops are increasing. Using the 5-minute Sum values in CloudWatch, you need to determine whether the drop rate exceeds 0.01% of all received packets. Which formula should you use?

choices.text: PacketsDropCount / (PacketsInFromSource + PacketsInFromDestination) × 100
choices.explanation: This is the AWS-provided drop-rate formula and uses traffic received by the NAT gateway in both directions as the baseline.

choices.text: PacketsDropCount / BytesOutToDestination × 100
choices.explanation: It mixes packet counts with bytes, so it does not calculate a packet drop rate.

choices.text: PacketsInFromSource / PacketsInFromDestination × 100
choices.explanation: This is a traffic-volume ratio between directions, not the proportion of packets that were dropped.

choices.text: ErrorPortAllocation / ConnectionAttemptCount × 100
choices.explanation: This could represent the rate of port allocation exhaustion, but it does not show the proportion of packets actually dropped.

learning.reason: This is the AWS-provided drop-rate formula and uses traffic received by the NAT gateway in both directions as the baseline.
learning.concept: For a NAT gateway, PacketsDropCount can be used with the number of packets received from both directions as the denominator to calculate the drop rate.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Re-establishing connections after a NAT idle timeout
prompt: An application maintains connections to an external API. When the interval between requests is long, only the next request fails and a retry succeeds. NAT gateway IdleTimeoutCount increases at the same time, but ErrorPortAllocation and PacketsDropCount do not. Without unnecessarily increasing the number of connections, which action should be taken first?

choices.text: Have the application re-establish connections and, when necessary, send valid keepalives at intervals shorter than 350 seconds
choices.explanation: IdleTimeoutCount indicates connections that have entered the idle state, so the design should be changed to avoid reusing stale connections.

choices.text: Add NAT gateways and distribute each connection across a different gateway
choices.explanation: The cause is stale idle-connection reuse, not port-allocation exhaustion, so adding gateways does not address the root cause.

choices.text: Change the default route to an internet gateway
choices.explanation: This changes the requirements for outbound traffic from a private subnet and does not resolve the idle timeout.

choices.text: Change the CloudWatch aggregation period from 5 minutes to 1 minute
choices.explanation: This increases observation granularity but does not correct the application's reuse of stale connections.

learning.reason: IdleTimeoutCount indicates connections that have entered the idle state, so the design should be changed to avoid reusing stale connections.
learning.concept: A NAT gateway moves connections with no activity for 350 seconds and that have not been properly closed into the idle state. The application should implement reconnection or an appropriate keepalive.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Measuring packet-rate load separately from bandwidth for inspection appliances
prompt: An appliance behind a Gateway Load Balancer has nearly the same transferred byte volume as during normal operation, but its CPU utilization rises only during periods when small packets surge. Which CloudWatch metric shows the maximum packet-processing rate?

choices.text: Maximum of HealthyHostCount
choices.explanation: This is the number of healthy targets, not the packet rate delivered to the appliance.

choices.text: Maximum of PeakPacketsPerSecond
choices.explanation: This shows the peak number of packets processed over a short period rather than the byte volume.

choices.text: Sum of ProcessedBytes
choices.explanation: This is the total number of processed bytes and does not directly show the packet rate caused by a surge in small packets.

choices.text: Minimum of ActiveFlowCount
choices.explanation: This is the minimum number of concurrent flows, not the peak number of processed packets.

learning.reason: PeakPacketsPerSecond shows the peak number of packets processed over a short period rather than the byte volume.
learning.concept: Gateway Load Balancer's PeakPacketsPerSecond represents the maximum average packet rate calculated every 10 seconds.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Identifying an inconsistent flow cookie on packets returned to GWLB
prompt: After updating a custom appliance behind a Gateway Load Balancer, only certain bidirectional TCP flows are lost in the return direction. The target health check is normal, and the appliance uses GENEVE to return traffic to GWLB. Which metric should be checked to determine whether the original FlowCookie was changed or omitted during the return?

choices.text: TCP_Target_Reset_Count
choices.explanation: This counts TCP RSTs forwarded by the appliance and does not indicate a GWLB cookie-validation failure.

choices.text: RejectedFlowCount
choices.explanation: This is the number of flows rejected by the load balancer and does not identify a mismatch in the return TLV of an existing flow.

choices.text: PacketsDroppedCount_InvalidGeneveTunnel
choices.explanation: This metric applies when the source or destination IP address or destination port of the GENEVE packet is invalid, not when the FlowCookie itself is inconsistent.

choices.text: PacketsDroppedCount_InvalidGwlbFlowCookie
choices.explanation: This shows the number of return packets discarded by GWLB because of a flow-cookie mismatch.

learning.reason: This shows the number of return packets discarded by GWLB because of a flow-cookie mismatch.
learning.concept: GWLB increments PacketsDroppedCount_InvalidGwlbFlowCookie when the FlowCookie TLV in a returned packet does not match the original flow.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Detecting policy-table mismatches in a TGW operations alarm
prompt: In a Transit Gateway policy table, traffic from an attachment fails to reach only new destinations. The corresponding route exists in the standard TGW route table, but you need to continuously detect traffic that does not match a policy rule. Which CloudWatch alarm target is the most direct?

choices.text: The Sum of PacketDropCountNoPolicy remaining greater than 0
choices.explanation: This directly indicates packets dropped because they did not match a policy rule.

choices.text: The Sum of PacketDropCountTTLExpired remaining greater than 0
choices.explanation: This indicates drops caused by expired TTL values, not the result of policy-table evaluation.

choices.text: The Sum of PacketDropCountBlackhole remaining greater than 0
choices.explanation: This indicates drops that matched an explicit blackhole route and is different from a policy-rule mismatch.

choices.text: A decrease in the Average of BytesOut
choices.explanation: A change in outbound volume does not identify the cause and can also occur during low traffic.

learning.reason: PacketDropCountNoPolicy directly indicates packets dropped because they did not match a policy rule.
learning.concept: Traffic dropped because it did not match a policy rule can be observed with PacketDropCountNoPolicy. In a standard route table, this is equivalent to NoRoute.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Monitoring the measured delivery rate of an inter-Region TGW path
prompt: Multipath resilience using multiple AWS network paths is enabled between Transit Gateways in two Regions. You want to monitor, as availability using the minimum value, how many packets sent to the peer Region were delivered during each one-minute period. Which metric and statistic should you use?

choices.text: Minimum for MultipathResilienceAvailabilityToPeer
choices.explanation: It reports the delivery rate as a percentage for each one-minute period, and using the minimum makes it less likely that packet loss will be overlooked.

choices.text: Average for MultipathResilienceSLANonCompliantSecondsToPeer
choices.explanation: This counts the seconds below the SLA; it is not the delivery rate itself. The meaningful statistic is also Sum.

choices.text: Minimum for VirtualInterfaceBgpStatus
choices.explanation: This is the BGP status of a Direct Connect virtual interface, not the delivery rate provided by multipath resilience between TGW Regions.

choices.text: Average for PacketDropCountNoRoute
choices.explanation: This is the number of packets dropped because no route was available; it does not show the delivery rate across multiple paths.

learning.reason: It reports the delivery rate as a percentage for each one-minute period, and using the minimum makes it less likely that packet loss will be overlooked.
learning.concept: MultipathResilienceAvailabilityToPeer shows the proportion of packets sent to the peer Region that were delivered, and Minimum is meaningful for this metric.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Mapping monitoring metrics to the physical state of a dedicated connection and a VIF
prompt: A Direct Connect path switches intermittently. To investigate the connection state, the BGP state of the relevant VIF, and the optical signal received by the AWS-side device separately, choose one metric for each observation purpose. Use each candidate once.

choices.text: ConnectionLightLevelRx
choices.explanation: Monitors the optical signal level received by the AWS-side device for the Direct Connect connection.

choices.text: VirtualInterfaceBgpStatus
choices.explanation: Monitors whether BGP is established on the specified virtual interface.

choices.text: ConnectionState
choices.explanation: Monitors whether the entire physical connection is up or down, at the connection-ID level.

learning.reason: ConnectionState monitors whether the entire physical connection is up or down, at the connection-ID level. VirtualInterfaceBgpStatus monitors whether BGP is established on the specified virtual interface. ConnectionLightLevelRx monitors the optical signal level received by the AWS-side device for the Direct Connect connection.
learning.concept: Direct Connect CloudWatch metrics separate metrics for the physical connection, the VIF, and the optical signal.

prompts.text: Check per connection whether the link-up state is continuing.
Check whether the BGP session is established only on the VIF experiencing the problem.
Check whether the received optical level has decreased on the AWS side.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Aggregating and investigating Direct Connect MAC-layer errors
prompt: A Direct Connect dedicated connection remains up, but short bursts of retransmissions are increasing. You want an alarm for the total number of MAC-layer errors observed by the AWS-side device during each five-minute period. Which metric and statistic should you use?

choices.text: Sum for VirtualInterfaceBgpPrefixesAccepted
choices.explanation: This is the number of BGP prefixes received, not MAC-layer errors on the physical connection.

choices.text: Sum for ConnectionErrorCount
choices.explanation: It sums data points in which errors occurred to obtain the total number of errors for the selected period.

choices.text: Maximum for ConnectionBpsEgress
choices.explanation: This is the bit rate from the AWS side, not the number of MAC-layer errors.

choices.text: Average for ConnectionCRCErrorCount
choices.explanation: ConnectionCRCErrorCount has been retired and replaced by ConnectionErrorCount. Average also does not aggregate a period's total.

learning.reason: It sums data points in which errors occurred to obtain the total number of errors for the selected period.
learning.concept: ConnectionErrorCount represents MAC-layer errors recorded by the AWS-side device, and Sum gives the total for the selected period.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Confirming completion of a submitted CloudFront invalidation
prompt: After a release, you submitted a CloudFront invalidation for specific paths. A few seconds later, you realized that you had accidentally included a path, but you do not want to change another distribution setting. Choose two operationally correct statements.

choices.text: CloudFront rejects all requests until the invalidation status becomes completed.
choices.explanation: An invalidation processes cached objects; it does not stop the entire distribution.

choices.text: A submitted invalidation cannot be canceled, so prepare for a cache miss even for the path that was included accidentally.
choices.explanation: CloudFront propagates an invalidation request to the edge locations after submission. Because invalidated objects are removed from the cache, the next request may retrieve the object again.

choices.text: Check status and the paths included in the invalidation in the invalidation ID details.
choices.explanation: The invalidation details show the ID, status, creation time, and paths included in the invalidation.

choices.text: To stop the invalidation, submit an empty path list using the same ID.
choices.explanation: There is no mechanism to modify a request with the same ID to stop it, and a submitted invalidation cannot be canceled.

choices.text: Increasing the TTL automatically cancels an invalidation that is in progress.
choices.explanation: A TTL setting does not cancel a submitted invalidation.

learning.reason: CloudFront propagates an invalidation request to the edge locations after submission. Because invalidated objects are removed from the cache, the next request may retrieve the object again. The invalidation details show the ID, status, creation time, and paths included in the invalidation.
learning.concept: A CloudFront invalidation cannot be canceled after submission. You can check its status and included paths in the invalidation ID details.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Monitor the hit rate for cacheable requests in CloudFront
prompt: The origin load of a CloudFront distribution has increased. You want to continuously monitor cache usage for GET and HEAD requests, but you do not want POST, PUT, or error responses included in the denominator. After enabling additional metrics, which CloudWatch metric and statistic are most appropriate?

choices.text: Average of TotalErrorRate
choices.explanation: This is the percentage of 4xx and 5xx errors, not the cache hit rate.

choices.text: Sum of Requests
choices.explanation: This counts requests for all HTTP methods and does not represent the cache-hit ratio.

choices.text: Average of OriginLatency
choices.explanation: This shows the wait time for an origin response, not the percentage of cacheable requests served from the cache.

choices.text: Average of CacheHitRate
choices.explanation: This lets you verify the percentage served from the cache while excluding POST, PUT, and errors from cacheable requests.

learning.reason: This excludes POST, PUT, and errors from cacheable requests and lets you verify the percentage served from the cache.
learning.concept: CacheHitRate is the percentage of cacheable requests answered from the CloudFront cache; use Average.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Identify high-volume traffic by source-and-destination pair from VPC Flow Logs
prompt: Transfer costs have increased in a VPC. You do not need individual packet analysis, but you want to continuously identify the top source-IP and destination-IP pairs by total transferred bytes from VPC Flow Logs already delivered to CloudWatch Logs. Which method is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use a CloudWatch alarm to count only VPC Flow Logs records whose log-status is ACCEPT
choices.explanation: This shows the number of permitted communications, but not which IP pairs transferred the most data or the total bytes.

choices.text: Use Reachability Analyzer to list the most frequent communication pairs
choices.explanation: Reachability Analyzer analyzes configured reachability; it does not rank actual traffic by byte contribution.

choices.text: Create a CloudWatch Contributor Insights rule that uses srcaddr and dstaddr as keys and sums bytes as the value
choices.explanation: This aggregates total bytes by communication pair from the flow logs and continuously displays the top contributors.

choices.text: Monitor only the NAT gateway's BytesOutToDestination
choices.explanation: This shows the NAT gateway's overall byte volume but cannot break it down by source-and-destination IP pair inside and outside the VPC.

learning.reason: This aggregates total bytes by communication pair from the flow logs and continuously displays the top contributors.
learning.concept: CloudWatch Contributor Insights can use srcaddr and dstaddr from VPC Flow Logs as keys and bytes as the value to aggregate the top byte-transfer pairs.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Validate only TGW routes in both directions before traffic occurs
prompt: Two Transit Gateways registered in the global network are peered. For the route from a VPC attachment to the peer-side VPN attachment, you want to verify the round-trip path in the TGW route tables without generating traffic. You will verify the VPC route tables, security groups, and customer gateway device configuration separately. Which feature is most appropriate?

choices.text: Collect only Transit Gateway Flow Logs and wait for the results
choices.explanation: Flow logs observe actual traffic and do not satisfy the requirement to validate the route in advance without generating traffic.

choices.text: Use Route 53 Resolver Query Logging to verify the round trip of name resolution
choices.explanation: DNS query logs do not analyze IP routing through Transit Gateways.

choices.text: Analyze the path, including the return path, with AWS Network Manager Route Analyzer
choices.explanation: This can validate the round-trip path between the source and destination attachments in advance while limiting the analysis to TGW route tables.

choices.text: Use VPC Reachability Analyzer to analyze the entire path, including the TGW and VPN device
choices.explanation: Reachability Analyzer is a different configuration-analysis feature and is not the Route Analyzer-based return-path validation for multiple TGWs required here.

learning.reason: This validates the round-trip path between the source and destination attachments in advance while limiting the analysis to TGW route tables.
learning.concept: AWS Network Manager Route Analyzer analyzes only TGW route tables between attachments of registered TGWs and can also verify the return path.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Distinguish when Internet Monitor has stopped measuring
prompt: After adding an application resource to CloudWatch Internet Monitor, metrics are not arriving. In the console, monitor status is Inactive, not Error. Which interpretation and action are most appropriate?

choices.text: Only the Error state stops data, so continue using the previous measurements even when the monitor is Inactive
choices.explanation: Inactive also means that data is not being processed, so the current state cannot be determined from previous values alone.

choices.text: The monitor is inactive and is not processing data, so enable it and verify the conditions for transitioning to Active
choices.explanation: Internet Monitor does not process data while it remains Inactive. First verify activation and the monitored-resource configuration.

choices.text: Lowering the CloudWatch alarm threshold will automatically restart the Inactive monitor
choices.explanation: Alarm settings do not activate the monitor's lifecycle state.

choices.text: Because AWS network health has been confirmed, conclude that the users' internet experience is normal
choices.explanation: When the monitor is Inactive, Internet Monitor is not measuring at all, so the user experience cannot be concluded from it.

learning.reason: Internet Monitor does not process data while it remains Inactive. First verify activation and the monitored-resource configuration.
learning.concept: Inactive means that the Internet Monitor is inactive and not processing data; Error indicates an error state.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Determine access to a private application based on device posture
prompt: A company application must be provided without a public IP address, and access must be limited not only by user identity but also to connections from compliant devices. Which mechanism is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use AWS Verified Access to evaluate identity and device trust signals
choices.explanation: It can make context-based access decisions at the application level.

choices.text: Add the source CIDR to the internet gateway
choices.explanation: This cannot evaluate the device's trust state.

choices.text: Add a NAT Gateway
choices.explanation: This provides outbound address translation, not user authorization.

choices.text: Shorten the Route 53 TTL
choices.explanation: This is a DNS setting and does not make access decisions.

learning.reason: It can make context-based access decisions at the application level.
learning.concept: Zero-trust application connectivity

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Identify which policy lacks permission for an API action
prompt: A Secrets Manager interface endpoint in an isolated VPC allows the worker role to call DescribeSecret and GetSecretValue for the same secret. DescribeSecret succeeds, but the role has only the DescribeSecret IAM permission, so GetSecretValue is implicitly denied. There is no separate allow or deny on the secret, and no customer-managed KMS key is used. Which change allows reads while maintaining the network boundary?

choices.text: Broaden the TCP 443 allow range in the endpoint security group and leave the IAM policy unchanged.
choices.explanation: Because DescribeSecret succeeds, HTTPS connectivity is established. A security group cannot change the IAM permission for an individual API operation.

choices.text: Retrieve the secret from a different subnet while continuing to use the same worker IAM role.
choices.explanation: Changing the source connection does not add the IAM permission required for the worker to perform the read on the secret.

choices.text: Change the endpoint policy to allow all actions while keeping the worker's IAM permissions unchanged.
choices.explanation: Broadening the operations available through the endpoint does not remove the implicit deny in the worker role.

choices.text: Allow GetSecretValue for the target secret in the worker role's IAM policy.
choices.explanation: For the read operation, the endpoint's existing allow and the worker's IAM allow are then both present.

learning.reason: For the read operation, the endpoint's existing allow and the worker's IAM allow are then both present.
learning.concept: A Secrets Manager VPC endpoint policy is an additional restriction applied when the endpoint is used; it is evaluated separately from the caller's IAM permissions.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Restrict a Regional REST API to mTLS only
prompt: A partner-facing Regional REST API must require trusted client certificates, and bypass through the default execute-api endpoint without mTLS must also be prevented. Select two.

choices.text: Change the API to a private API
choices.explanation: This is not an mTLS configuration for the required Regional public API.

choices.text: Disable the REST API's default execute-api endpoint
choices.explanation: Disabling the default endpoint prevents access through an entry point other than the mTLS custom domain.

choices.text: Configure only a usage plan
choices.explanation: Usage management neither validates client certificates nor blocks the alternate entry point.

choices.text: Configure only a WAF IP set
choices.explanation: An IP restriction does not validate the certificate trust chain.

choices.text: Enable mTLS on a Regional custom domain and specify a truststore in Amazon S3
choices.explanation: REST API mTLS requires a Regional custom domain and a truststore.

learning.reason: REST API mTLS requires a Regional custom domain and a truststore. Disabling the default endpoint prevents access through an entry point other than the mTLS custom domain.
learning.concept: API Gateway mTLS and default endpoint

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Match ALB TLS policy meanings to different connection requirements
prompt: Audit the HTTPS settings of a public ALB and an isolated test ALB. Match each existing listener's TLS version requirement with one security policy to verify. Use each candidate once.

choices.text: ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-3-2021-06
choices.explanation: This configuration uses TLS 1.3 and does not allow TLS 1.2 or earlier versions.

choices.text: ELBSecurityPolicy-2016-08
choices.explanation: This provides compatibility with TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, and TLS 1.2. When validating current requirements for a public service, note this legacy permitted range.

choices.text: ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06
choices.explanation: This allows TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 but does not allow earlier TLS versions.

learning.reason: This allows TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 but does not allow earlier TLS versions. This configuration uses TLS 1.3 and does not allow TLS 1.2 or earlier versions. This provides compatibility with TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, and TLS 1.2. When validating current requirements for a public service, note this legacy permitted range.
learning.concept: An ALB HTTPS security policy specifies the TLS versions and cipher suites that clients can negotiate.

prompts.text: A public API must accept both partners using TLS 1.2 and general users using TLS 1.3, while rejecting older protocols.
An internal HTTPS listener whose clients all support TLS 1.3 must allow only TLS 1.3.
Identify the configuration of an existing listener in a compatibility test for isolated legacy devices that allows TLS 1.0 through TLS 1.2.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス

title: Decrypt HTTPS traffic for inspection and policy evaluation

choices.explanation: This evaluates DNS names but does not inspect HTTPS content.

choices.text: Export Flow Logs to S3

choices.text: Add more NAT Gateways
choices.explanation: NAT does not decrypt TLS traffic.

choices.explanation: This would block normal users as well.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
