title: Restricting Principals That Use an S3 Gateway Endpoint
prompt: Multiple roles in a VPC share an S3 Gateway endpoint. You want to allow only a specific application role to read from a specific bucket. Select TWO options.

choices.text: Delete the route for the Gateway endpoint.
choices.explanation: The target application would also lose connectivity to S3.

choices.text: Set Principal to * in the Gateway endpoint policy, and use an aws:PrincipalArn condition to restrict the application role, bucket, and operations.
choices.explanation: In an endpoint policy, Principal can be set to *, and the allowed roles can be narrowed with a PrincipalArn condition.

choices.text: Restrict the application role's IAM policy to read access for the target bucket.
choices.explanation: Least privilege is also required on the identity side.

choices.text: Enable only CloudTrail data events.
choices.explanation: Auditing alone does not restrict authorization.

choices.text: Specify S3 object operations in a security group.
choices.explanation: Security groups do not evaluate S3 API actions.

learning.reason: An endpoint policy can set Principal to * and narrow the allowed roles with a PrincipalArn condition. Least privilege is also required on the identity side.
learning.concept: Layered authorization with a Gateway endpoint and IAM

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Rejecting Requests Whose Entire Body Cannot Be Inspected
prompt: You use AWS WAF associated with an ALB to inspect the POST body of a form API. Normal request bodies are evaluated by existing rules. As a security requirement, requests whose body exceeds the limit that the ALB can pass to WAF must be rejected, even when the initial portion contains no match. Which setting should you use in the Block rule for the target path?

choices.text: Set Oversize handling to Continue and always evaluate only the initial portion that can be retrieved.
choices.explanation: Normal evaluation continues, but an oversized request is not rejected merely because no match is found in the initial portion.

choices.text: Set Oversize handling to Match in the statement that evaluates the body, and set the rule action to Block.
choices.explanation: When the body exceeds the limit, the rule matches, preventing the request from being allowed based only on the portion that could be inspected.

choices.text: Set the normal monitoring rule for the target path to Count and assume that only oversized requests are automatically blocked.
choices.explanation: Count measures matching requests; it does not become a Block that terminates processing because the body is oversized.

choices.text: Set Oversize handling to No match and stop the request with the same Block rule when it is oversized.
choices.explanation: Because the statement does not match when the body is oversized, that Block rule does not reject the request.

learning.reason: When the body exceeds the limit, the rule matches, preventing the request from being allowed based only on the portion that could be inspected.
learning.concept: With WAF Oversize handling set to Match, a statement can be treated as matching when the request body exceeds the inspection limit.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Blocking Name Resolution During a DNS Protection Failure
prompt: In a VPC where blocking malware connections has the highest priority, name resolution must not be allowed when DNS Firewall does not respond. Which setting is most appropriate?

choices.text: Leave the VPC DNS Firewall in fail-closed mode.
choices.explanation: The default fail-closed behavior blocks queries that cannot be evaluated by returning SERVFAIL, prioritizing security.

choices.text: Do not associate a DNS Firewall rule group.
choices.explanation: The protection provided by the fail mode would not apply.

choices.text: Enable FirewallFailOpen.
choices.explanation: This allows queries when they cannot be evaluated, which violates the requirement.

choices.text: Configure only Resolver query logging.
choices.explanation: Logging does not block name resolution when evaluation cannot be performed.

learning.reason: The default fail-closed behavior blocks queries that cannot be evaluated by returning SERVFAIL, prioritizing security.
learning.concept: DNS Firewall fail closed

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Preventing Imported Certificate Expiration
prompt: You use a third-party-issued certificate imported into an ALB. Who is responsible for ensuring that it is renewed before it expires?

choices.text: ACM automatically requests renewal from the external CA.
choices.explanation: Imported certificates are not eligible for automatic renewal.

choices.text: The ALB extends the certificate's expiration date.
choices.explanation: The load balancer does not renew certificates.

choices.text: Route 53 renews the certificate.
choices.explanation: DNS does not renew certificates issued by an external CA.

choices.text: The user who imported the certificate re-imports the renewed certificate.
choices.explanation: ACM does not automatically renew imported certificates.

learning.reason: ACM does not automatically renew imported certificates.
learning.concept: ACM imported certificate renewal

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Sending UDP fragments under inspection to stateful inspection
prompt: In AWS Network Firewall, you need to apply stateful inspection to specific authorized business UDP traffic. Normal packets flow correctly, but UDP fragments that do not match an individual stateless rule are being discarded by the default action. You must apply stateful rules to the fragments and avoid allowing them without inspection. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Enable both Flow logs and Alert logs while keeping the packet-processing action unchanged.
choices.explanation: Enabling logging does not forward packets discarded during stateless processing to the inspection layer.

choices.text: Select Pass directly as the default action for fragments.
choices.explanation: This processing does not forward the fragments for the required stateful inspection.

choices.text: Change the default action for normal packets and leave Drop for fragments.
choices.explanation: The individual default processing applied to UDP fragments remains discard.

choices.text: Configure the stateless default action for fragments to forward them to a stateful rule group.
choices.explanation: The applicable UDP fragments are evaluated by stateful rules instead of ending in discard.

learning.reason: The applicable UDP fragments are evaluated by stateful rules instead of ending in discard.
learning.concept: StatelessFragmentDefaultActions is used for UDP fragments that do not match an applicable stateless rule.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Restricting S3 Access Point use to a specified VPC
prompt: For an S3 Access Point used by a data lake, you want to accept requests only from a specified VPC and reject requests through the internet. Which setting is most appropriate?

choices.text: Enable only CloudTrail data events
choices.explanation: Auditing alone does not reject requests through the internet.

choices.text: Enable S3 Inventory
choices.explanation: Creating an inventory does not restrict access to the VPC.

choices.text: Keep the bucket name private
choices.explanation: Keeping the name private does not restrict the access path.

choices.text: Set the Access Point network origin to VPC and specify the target VPC
choices.explanation: An Access Point with a VPC origin rejects requests from outside the specified VPC.

learning.reason: An Access Point with a VPC origin rejects requests from outside the specified VPC.
learning.concept: S3 Access Point VPC network origin

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Disallowing HTTP at the edge
prompt: For a CloudFront distribution, you want to reject HTTP connections from viewers rather than redirecting them to HTTPS, allowing only TLS connections. Which behavior setting is most appropriate?

choices.text: Set the Viewer protocol policy to HTTPS Only.
choices.explanation: HTTP requests receive an error, and only HTTPS is allowed.

choices.text: Change the cache policy.
choices.explanation: The cache key does not control whether viewer TLS connections are allowed.

choices.text: Set the policy to Redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
choices.explanation: This redirects HTTP instead of rejecting it.

choices.text: Set the Origin protocol policy to HTTPS Only.
choices.explanation: This controls only the connection between CloudFront and the origin.

learning.reason: HTTP requests receive an error, and only HTTPS is allowed.
learning.concept: Viewer protocol policy HTTPS only

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Sending inspection decisions to a central logging platform
prompt: You want to deliver Network Firewall alert logs and flow logs to separate prefixes in an audit S3 bucket in the same account. Which setting is most appropriate?

choices.text: Write the decisions in the security group description field.
choices.explanation: This does not send runtime logs to a central destination.

choices.text: Record the NACL rule numbers.
choices.explanation: This does not output Firewall alert or flow logs.

choices.text: Use only NAT Gateway metrics.
choices.explanation: This does not provide rule-match information from the inspection engine.

choices.text: In the Firewall logging configuration, set the S3 destination and prefix separately for alert and flow logs.
choices.explanation: Network Firewall lets you configure an output destination for each log type.

learning.reason: Network Firewall lets you configure an output destination for each log type.
learning.concept: Network Firewall logging configuration

title: Preventing both regional entry points from being disabled during a Region switch
prompt: Two regional public entry points are switched by Amazon ARC routing controls. Configure the system so that the service rejects a change that would turn both controls off during an operation, rather than relying only on notifying the operator. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Shorten the DNS cache time so that, if both are off, clients perform DNS resolution again sooner.
choices.explanation: Faster re-resolution does not reject the update that turns both controls off.

choices.text: Use data plane endpoints from the same cluster for both routing controls.
choices.explanation: Using the same endpoints does not restrict which combinations of states are allowed.

choices.text: Create only a CloudWatch alarm that detects when both controls are off.
choices.explanation: This can notify you after an abnormal change, but it does not reject the change in advance.

choices.text: For the two routing controls, configure an assertion safety rule requiring at least one to be on.
choices.explanation: ARC can define a condition that rejects a state change in which both controls would be off.

learning.reason: ARC can define a condition that rejects a state change in which both controls would be off.
learning.concept: An assertion safety rule specifies the conditions that the states of routing controls must satisfy.

title: Connecting VPCs across Regions individually while sharing a dedicated connection
prompt: There is one Direct Connect connection to the on-premises environment. VPCs in multiple Regions each use an existing VGW and need communication with the site, but direct transit between VPCs is not required. Which option aggregates the connections without adding a TGW?

choices.text: Connect only one VPC to Direct Connect and peer that VPC with the other VPCs.
choices.explanation: Because of the edge-to-edge restriction on VPC peering, the other VPCs cannot share the first VPC's Direct Connect connection through it.

choices.text: Use a public VIF to advertise each VPC's private CIDR to the internet.
choices.explanation: A public VIF for public services does not provide the VPCs' private routes in this configuration.

choices.text: Connect the VIF directly to one VGW and add associations with the other Regions' VGWs to that VGW.
choices.explanation: A virtual private gateway is not an aggregation point that extends a connection to other VPCs' VGWs.

choices.text: Connect a private VIF to a Direct Connect gateway and associate each target VGW with it.
choices.explanation: A single VIF can reach the associated VPCs. The configuration does not provide a transit path between VGWs.

learning.reason: A single VIF can reach the associated VPCs. The configuration does not provide a transit path between VGWs.
learning.concept: A Direct Connect gateway can connect to multiple VGWs through a private VIF.

title: Moving a private IP address to a standby in the same subnet
prompt: Users reach a state-synchronized EC2 service through a fixed IPv4 address in a VPC. The primary and standby ENIs are in the same subnet, and DNS must not be changed during failover. How should the service IPv4 address be assigned?

choices.text: Assign the same private IPv4 address to both ENIs simultaneously and suppress responses from the standby.
choices.explanation: The same address cannot normally be assigned to two ENIs in the same subnet as overlapping addresses.

choices.text: Create another subnet with the same IPv4 range as the primary subnet and allow overlapping ranges in the same VPC.
choices.explanation: Overlapping subnet CIDRs cannot be used to move the same destination address.

choices.text: Reassign the primary IPv4 address of the primary ENI to the standby ENI while leaving the primary ENI in place.
choices.explanation: A primary IPv4 address cannot be moved using the same reassignment operation available for a secondary address.

choices.text: Use the service IP as a secondary IPv4 address on the primary ENI and reassign it to the standby ENI during failover.
choices.explanation: Moving the same private IP to the standby ENI preserves the destination used by clients.

learning.reason: Moving the same private IP to the standby ENI preserves the destination used by clients.
learning.concept: A secondary private IPv4 address can be reassigned to another network interface in the same subnet.

title: Preserving allowlisted IP addresses for a public TCP service
prompt: A public TCP service runs across two Availability Zones in a single Region and must use two Elastic IP addresses that are already on an allowlist. Map the specified IP to the entry point in each Availability Zone while preserving the existing client configuration. Which option does this?

choices.text: Specify private IP addresses in the subnet mappings of an internal NLB and advertise them directly to the internet.
choices.explanation: Private IP addresses of an internal NLB cannot serve as the public IP addresses already registered on the allowlist.

choices.text: Create an internet-facing NLB and specify the corresponding Elastic IP in the subnet mapping for each Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: This assigns the specified public IP to the NLB entry point in each Availability Zone.

choices.text: Attach the two Elastic IP addresses to the targets of an internet-facing ALB and assume that the ALB entry points will use the same addresses.
choices.explanation: Fixing the backend IP addresses does not satisfy the ALB's external-address and arbitrary TCP-listening requirements.

choices.text: Use the NLB's automatically assigned IP addresses and assign the registered Elastic IP addresses to the targets.
choices.explanation: Clients connect to the NLB entry point; an IP assigned to a target is not the entry point.

learning.reason: This assigns the specified public IP to the NLB entry point in each Availability Zone.
learning.concept: An internet-facing NLB can use a specified Elastic IP for each subnet mapping.

title: Send only requests matching both a specified host and path to a separate service
prompt: At the HTTPS entry point of the same ALB, send only requests for admin.example.com and paths under /manage to the administrative target group. Requests matching only one of these conditions must continue to use the existing default forwarding. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Add the administrative host name to the HTTPS certificate list and use only the default forwarding action.
choices.explanation: Certificate selection for the TLS connection and HTTP host and path conditions are separate processes.

choices.text: Set both host-header and path-pattern conditions in one listener rule and forward matching requests to the administrative target group.
choices.explanation: Only requests meeting both conditions match the administrative rule before the default rule.

choices.text: Create a DNS record in Route 53 that includes /manage, and select the target group there.
choices.explanation: DNS does not process HTTP request paths and cannot select a forwarding rule inside the ALB.

choices.text: Create separate rules for the host and path, and send requests to the administrative group in both rules.
choices.explanation: A request matching either condition alone would be forwarded to the administrative group by one of the separate rules.

learning.reason: Only requests meeting both conditions match the administrative rule before the default rule.
learning.concept: An ALB listener rule can contain both host-header and path-pattern conditions.

title: Audit multiple PrivateLink consumers by connection
prompt: For partners using the same PrivateLink service, the backend must include the originating VPC endpoint ID in its audit logs. The application can interpret Proxy Protocol v2, and communication authentication is performed separately. Which NLB design is appropriate?

choices.text: Use a different NLB DNS name for each consumer and identify the origin from the target connection logs.
choices.explanation: Adding aliases for names does not add the consumer's endpoint ID to the metadata of a TCP connection.

choices.text: Interpret only the X-Forwarded-For header inserted by the NLB's TCP listener.
choices.explanation: NLB TCP forwarding does not insert HTTP headers.

choices.text: Enable Proxy Protocol v2 for the TCP target group and record the endpoint ID in the backend.
choices.explanation: The endpoint ID can be read from AWS-specific information in the binary header attached to the connection.

choices.text: Enable only client IP preservation and record the socket's source IP as the VPC endpoint ID.
choices.explanation: An IP address and an endpoint ID are different types of information and are not the same identifier through PrivateLink.

learning.reason: The endpoint ID can be read from AWS-specific information in the binary header attached to the connection.
learning.concept: For traffic through PrivateLink, NLB Proxy Protocol v2 includes information identifying the VPC endpoint.

title: Interconnect a managed IPv6 range without advertising it to the internet
prompt: An enterprise allocates part of a GUA used on premises for private IPv6 use in AWS. VPCs in AWS must use a range under the same administrative control, and AWS must not advertise that range to the public internet. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Make the VPC IPv4-only and register only the on-premises IPv6 range in the VPC route table.
choices.explanation: This does not allow resources in the VPC to use IPv6 from the same administratively controlled range.

choices.text: Onboard IPv6 for public use, begin advertising it from AWS, and then use security groups to block inbound traffic.
choices.explanation: Inbound filtering does not stop the range from being advertised through a public route.

choices.text: Enable private GUA in IPAM and allocate the range to the target VPC from a pool for nonpublic use.
choices.explanation: This allocates the enterprise-managed IPv6 range for private use without relying on public advertising by AWS.

choices.text: Use an Amazon-provided public IPv6 CIDR in each VPC and represent the GUA range with a DNS alias.
choices.explanation: Changing a DNS name does not preserve the IPv6 prefix used by the workloads.

learning.reason: This allocates the enterprise-managed IPv6 range for private use without relying on public advertising by AWS.
learning.concept: IPAM can enable provisioning of private GUA ranges.

title: Send only QA requests to the configuration used for deployment validation
prompt: Using the existing CloudFront domain, you need to test a new cache behavior. Test devices can add a dedicated header, but the validation configuration must not be applied to requests from ordinary users. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Add a header to the production distribution's requests to the origin and keep only one CloudFront configuration.
choices.explanation: This provides more information to the origin, but it does not switch requests to a staging distribution with different cache behaviors.

choices.text: Give the production and validation distributions equal weights in DNS.
choices.explanation: DNS does not evaluate the user's dedicated request header, so ordinary users could also be sent to the validation distribution.

choices.text: Create a staging distribution and configure a continuous deployment policy that routes requests based on the dedicated aws-cf-cd- header.
choices.explanation: Only test requests that meet the policy condition use the staging configuration.

choices.text: Publish the new behavior to the production distribution immediately and disable it if a problem occurs.
choices.explanation: Users whose requests do not meet the validation condition would be affected from the beginning.

learning.reason: Only test requests that meet the policy condition use the staging configuration.
learning.concept: CloudFront continuous deployment can route requests to a staging distribution based on a header condition.

title: Matching delivery cost and regional requirements to price classes
prompt: Match the available CloudFront edge locations to the requirements for each delivery. Select one price class for each requirement. Use each candidate exactly once.

choices.text: Price Class 200
choices.explanation: It covers a wider range than Price Class 100, including Asia, while excluding certain high-cost regions.

choices.text: The price class that uses all edge locations
choices.explanation: It includes all CloudFront edge locations in the price class coverage.

choices.text: Price Class 100
choices.explanation: It provides the lower-cost coverage that includes the United States, Canada, and Europe.

learning.reason: It provides the lower-cost coverage that includes the United States, Canada, and Europe. It covers a wider range than Price Class 100, including Asia, while excluding certain high-cost regions. It includes all CloudFront edge locations in the price class coverage.
learning.concept: CloudFront price classes select the available edge-location coverage; they do not prohibit access from specific countries.

prompts.text: Users are concentrated mainly in the United States, Canada, and Europe, and the goal is to minimize cost by using the narrowest available edge-location coverage.
The available coverage must be extended to include edge locations in Asia, but it does not need to include edge locations in South America.
Using edge locations in every region is more important than cost.

title: Priority between wildcard and specific host-name registrations
prompt: One CloudFront distribution has *.example.com registered as an alternate domain name, and another distribution has shop.example.com registered as an alternate domain name. Each certificate appropriately covers its respective name. During a phased migration, DNS for shop.example.com points to the distribution domain name of the wildcard distribution. Which distribution processes existing requests for this host name?

choices.text: The requests are sent alternately to both distributions because both the wildcard and the specific name match.
choices.explanation: CloudFront selects the most specific registration; this is not a load-balancing condition.

choices.text: The wildcard distribution always processes the requests because DNS points to it.
choices.explanation: The DNS target alone does not change the priority of alternate domain names within CloudFront.

choices.text: CloudFront rejects all requests because the parent domain and specific host name overlap.
choices.explanation: An overlap between a wildcard name and a more specific registration is allowed, and the specific name is selected.

choices.text: The distribution with shop.example.com explicitly registered processes the requests.
choices.explanation: Separately from the distribution domain name used in DNS, CloudFront selects the most specific registration for the host name in the request.

learning.reason: Separately from the distribution domain name used in DNS, CloudFront selects the most specific registration for the host name in the request.
learning.concept: When a wildcard name and a specific alternate domain name exist on different distributions, the more specific name takes precedence.

title: Obtaining a public IP that can be associated with a Local Zone ENI
prompt: Place an EC2 instance with a stable public entry point in a Local Zone in the same AWS Region as an existing regional hub. The Local Zone's network border group differs from that of the regional hub. From which scope should the Elastic IP be allocated?

choices.text: Specify an Elastic IP previously used in another Region and change it to target the Local Zone in Route 53.
choices.explanation: DNS does not change the allocation scope or association constraints of an Elastic IP.

choices.text: Specify the Local Zone's network border group when allocating the Elastic IP.
choices.explanation: The Local Zone ENI and the border group match, so the Elastic IP can be associated and used.

choices.text: Place the existing private IPv4 address in a public subnet and obtain the same address as an Elastic IP.
choices.explanation: A private address and an Elastic IP for public Internet access are different allocations.

choices.text: Obtain the Elastic IP from the parent Region's default group and assume it can be associated with any Local Zone in the same Region.
choices.explanation: Even within the same Region, an Elastic IP cannot be associated when the network border groups differ.

learning.reason: The Local Zone ENI and the border group match, so the Elastic IP can be associated and used.
learning.concept: An Elastic IP must be in the same network border group as the resource to which it is associated.

title: Using an IPv6-only public entry point while retaining IPv4 backends
prompt: All public clients of an application can use IPv6, and the policy is to use no public IPv4. The existing backends remain on private IPv4, and HTTP forwarding through the ALB must be maintained. Authentication by an external IdP is not performed on the ALB listener. Which option should be used?

choices.text: Set the public ALB's address type to dualstack-without-public-ipv4 and use an IPv4 target group.
choices.explanation: This provides no public IPv4 to clients while maintaining IPv4 forwarding to the target group.

choices.text: Set the public ALB to dualstack, provide only its AAAA record to clients, and retain the public IPv4 allocation.
choices.explanation: Not advertising an address in DNS is different from preventing the ALB from being assigned a public IPv4 address.

choices.text: Use an internal dualstack ALB and provide its internal name to Internet clients.
choices.explanation: Providing the internal ALB name does not create a public entry point for Internet clients.

choices.text: Set the public ALB to ipv4 and use NAT in a private subnet to provide a public IPv6 entry point.
choices.explanation: NAT alone does not provide an ALB entry point over public IPv6 for clients.

learning.reason: This provides no public IPv4 to clients while maintaining IPv4 forwarding to the target group.
learning.concept: ALB address type dualstack-without-public-ipv4 provides public IPv6 while allowing private IPv4 to be used toward targets.

title: Reduce traffic sent to anomalous targets that pass health checks
prompt: An ALB target group always has at least four instances that are considered healthy. Some instances intermittently return connection errors, but they pass health checks. Without changing the application, you need the ALB to automatically reduce the traffic sent to anomalous targets compared with the other targets. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Create a CloudWatch alarm for HTTP 5xx errors and keep the ALB distribution attributes unchanged.
choices.explanation: An alarm can send notifications, but it does not automatically change the distribution to anomalous targets.

choices.text: Choose Weighted Random routing and enable anomalous mitigation for Automatic Target Weights.
choices.explanation: This identifies targets with higher error rates than the others and automatically reduces their traffic allocation.

choices.text: Extend target Slow Start and do not deregister and register again all instances that are already considered healthy.
choices.explanation: Slow Start primarily warms up newly added targets; it does not control allocation according to the error rate of existing targets.

choices.text: Keep Round Robin and enable only target group stickiness.
choices.explanation: Stickiness keeps existing sessions on their targets; it does not use error rates to control traffic volume.

learning.reason: Targets with higher error rates than the others can be identified and their traffic allocation can be reduced automatically.
learning.concept: ALB anomalous mitigation for Automatic Target Weights can reduce traffic to anomalous targets when combined with Weighted Random.

title: Place multiple mirror sources behind a swappable fleet of analysis appliances
prompt: You are collecting mirrored traffic from multiple VPC ENIs during migration validation. You need an entry point that lets you replace multiple corresponding analysis appliances without assigning a fixed analysis EC2 IP address for each new mirror source. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Use an ALB with an HTTP listener as the mirror target and select an appliance by URL.
choices.explanation: Mirrored traffic is VXLAN traffic, not HTTP requests, and an ALB is not a supported corresponding target.

choices.text: Route the mirror source subnet to an analysis NAT gateway.
choices.explanation: Routes affect the original traffic; they do not receive mirror copies or distribute them to an appliance fleet.

choices.text: Use an NLB with a UDP 4789 listener and a target group containing the analysis appliances as the mirror target.
choices.explanation: This provides a common entry point for the mirrored VXLAN traffic while allowing the appliance fleet to be managed independently.

choices.text: Directly specify the ENI of one analysis EC2 instance in each mirror session.
choices.explanation: Direct specification is possible, but it does not provide a common appliance fleet that is independent of appliance replacement.

learning.reason: A common entry point can receive the mirrored VXLAN traffic while the analysis appliance configuration is managed independently.
learning.concept: Traffic Mirroring can use an NLB configured with UDP 4789 to receive VXLAN traffic.

title: Account for finer-grained records even with a 10-minute aggregation setting
prompt: You are estimating the storage and analysis costs of VPC Flow Logs. The only monitored interfaces are the ENIs of EC2 instances on Nitro systems. The maximum aggregation interval for the flow logs is set to 10 minutes. Which assumption is appropriate when designing for the number of records ingested?

choices.text: Flows for the target ENIs can be aggregated within one minute, so do not assume that they are always combined every 10 minutes.
choices.explanation: For ENIs on Nitro systems, records can be generated with finer-grained aggregation even when 10 minutes is specified.

choices.text: Even for ENIs on Nitro systems, exactly one flow is always recorded at 10-minute intervals.
choices.explanation: The setting represents the general maximum interval; Nitro systems apply a shorter upper limit.

choices.text: If the CloudWatch Logs retention period is set to 10 minutes, Nitro aggregation will also be 10 minutes.
choices.explanation: The retention period and the aggregation interval used by the source to group records are different concepts.

choices.text: Sending the logs to S3 always changes the records into 10-minute units at the destination service.
choices.explanation: Changing the destination does not change the source flow aggregation interval in that way.

learning.reason: For ENIs on Nitro systems, records can be generated with finer-grained aggregation even when 10 minutes is specified.
learning.concept: For ENIs of Nitro instances, the aggregation interval can be within one minute regardless of the configured maximum aggregation interval.

title: Validate the backend certificate for a private integration
prompt: An API Gateway HTTP API calls an internal ALB through a VPC Link. The ALB uses a certificate for service.internal. The client side already uses HTTPS. You must also use HTTPS on the integration side and configure validation of the expected name in the certificate used for the connection. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Match the VPC Link subnet to the certificate's issuing Region and assume that HTTPS configuration is added automatically.
choices.explanation: The VPC Link placement does not automatically configure backend TLS or the verification name.

choices.text: Set service.internal as ServerNameToVerify in the integration's TlsConfig.
choices.explanation: This uses HTTPS for the connection to the origin and validates the server certificate against the expected name.

choices.text: Set a certificate only on the public API's custom domain and leave the integration configuration unchanged.
choices.explanation: This manages HTTPS between users and the API; it does not specify name verification for forwarding through the VPC Link.

choices.text: Keep the integration target as HTTP and override only the outgoing Host header to service.internal.
choices.explanation: Changing an HTTP header does not establish TLS for the integration request.

learning.reason: The origin connection uses HTTPS and the server certificate is validated against the expected authentication name.
learning.concept: A private HTTP API integration can specify TlsConfig to connect using HTTPS.

title: Delegate reverse lookups for an internal address range to the site’s authoritative DNS
prompt: An AWS auditing application retrieves PTR records for the on-premises 10.8.16.0/24 range. The site DNS manages the reverse lookup zone for that range and is reachable through the existing outbound Resolver. Normal forward lookups and other reverse lookups must remain unchanged. Which rule should be added?

choices.text: Create a forwarding rule for 16.8.10.in-addr.arpa and associate it with the VPC of the application on AWS.
choices.explanation: Only reverse lookup names for the target IPv4 range can be sent to the site DNS through the existing outbound path.

choices.text: Create a forwarding rule only for the site’s normal forward-lookup domain and have PTR records for the same IPs selected automatically.
choices.explanation: A PTR query name is in in-addr.arpa and does not match the normal forward-lookup domain.

choices.text: Forward all of 8.10.in-addr.arpa to the site DNS.
choices.explanation: This would also change reverse lookups outside the target /24 within 10.8.0.0/16, affecting other existing ranges.

choices.text: Use 10.8.16.0/24 as the DNS rule name and route PTR queries by longest CIDR match.
choices.explanation: Resolver forwarding rules are evaluated against DNS domain names.

learning.reason: Only reverse lookup names for the target IPv4 range can be sent to the site DNS through the existing outbound path.
learning.concept: Reverse queries can be controlled with a forwarding rule that specifies the target in-addr.arpa zone.

title: Configure an internal VPN with per-user client certificates
prompt: The company has no directory or SAML IdP and issues a certificate for each managed device. In addition to validating the VPN server name, the connection must require the presentation of a client certificate issued by an approved CA. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Distribute a Site-to-Site VPN pre-shared key to the devices and register everyone as the same customer gateway.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the mutual-authentication requirements of Client VPN for individual devices.

choices.text: Distribute only the VPN server certificate and perform client authentication through subnet routes.
choices.explanation: Routes cannot verify whether a connecting device has an approved certificate.

choices.text: Select mutual authentication in Client VPN and configure the trust information required to validate the server and client certificates.
choices.explanation: This requires connecting devices to present approved client certificates without using an IdP.

choices.text: Do not use certificates; register the usernames of approved device users as sources in the VPC security group.
choices.explanation: Security groups do not provide VPN authentication based on individual usernames or client certificates.

learning.reason: This requires connecting devices to present approved client certificates without using an IdP.
learning.concept: AWS Client VPN mutual authentication uses client and server certificates when a connection is established.

title: Map public VIF advertisement scope to BGP communities
prompt: A company advertises its publicly owned IPv4 addresses to AWS through a Direct Connect public VIF. For each prefix, select one community corresponding to the desired propagation scope within AWS. Use each candidate once.

choices.explanation: Represents global propagation to public AWS Regions.
Represents propagation to AWS Regions within the same continent.
Represents propagation to the local AWS Region.

learning.reason: Represents propagation to the local AWS Region. Represents propagation to AWS Regions within the same continent. Represents global propagation to public AWS Regions.
learning.concept: AWS determines the propagation scope within AWS from the BGP community specified on routes received through a public VIF.

prompts.text: Use only in the local AWS Region for Direct Connect.
Use in AWS Regions on the same continent, without propagation to other continents.
Use in public AWS Regions globally, without limiting the scope to a continent.

title: Protect a production route from replacement during updates
prompt: The route table in a production stack should allow normal tag updates, but replacement caused by an incorrect update must be rejected until it is approved. Which two actions provide protection during normal operation and support planned changes? Select two.

choices.text: Enable only termination protection.
choices.explanation: It protects against stack deletion but does not reject changes made by an update.

choices.text: Run drift detection every hour.
choices.explanation: Drift detection identifies differences; it does not prevent an update from running.

choices.text: Set a stack policy that denies updates to the route table’s logical ID.
choices.explanation: This protects the critical resource from normal updates.

choices.text: Only during a planned update, specify a temporary stack policy that includes the permitted changes.
choices.explanation: This allows only the explicitly approved changes required for the planned update.

choices.text: Export the resource to another Region.
choices.explanation: An export does not protect a resource from updates.

learning.reason: A stack policy can protect a critical resource from normal updates and allow only explicitly approved changes during a planned update.
learning.concept: A stack policy can deny updates to specified logical resources during stack updates.

title: Fixing Network Change Permissions with CloudFormation
prompt: A network infrastructure stack must update VPCs and route tables only through an approved IAM role. Which method applies consistent least privilege to stack operations without directly using the individual operator's permissions?

choices.text: Reuse the VPC Flow Logs IAM role as the CloudFormation service role.
choices.explanation: The Flow Logs delivery role is not an execution role with permissions to create network resources.

choices.text: Configure only a stack policy.
choices.explanation: A stack policy restricts which resources can be updated, but it does not specify the IAM role that executes AWS API calls.

choices.text: Associate a CloudFormation service role that permits only network operations with the stack.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation performs resource operations using the specified role, reducing differences between operators.

choices.text: Grant AdministratorAccess to every operator.
choices.explanation: This violates least privilege and does not fix a single stack execution role.

learning.reason: CloudFormation performs resource operations using the specified role, reducing differences between operators.
learning.concept: A CloudFormation service role specifies the execution role that CloudFormation assumes when performing stack operations.

title: Rejecting Malformed HTTP at the ALB Entry Point
prompt: For a public ALB, do not pass ambiguous HTTP messages to the backend, and prioritize strict validation over compatibility. Which attribute should be used?

choices.text: Enable target group stickiness.
choices.explanation: This controls how the same client is routed.

choices.text: Only send WAF logs to S3.
choices.explanation: Logging alone does not reject requests at the entry point.

choices.text: Enable the NLB proxy protocol.
choices.explanation: This transfers connection information for a different load balancer.

choices.text: Set routing.http.desync_mitigation_mode to strictest.
choices.explanation: This handles malformed or ambiguous requests strictly.

learning.reason: This handles malformed or ambiguous requests strictly.
learning.concept: The ALB desync mitigation mode controls how HTTP desync is handled.

title: Forwarding the Original Host Header to the Backend
prompt: A legacy application behind an ALB identifies tenants using the Host header it receives. Which setting preserves the client's Host header instead of rewriting it to the hostname generated by the ALB?

choices.text: Disable X-Forwarded-For.
choices.explanation: This contains source information and does not preserve the Host header.

choices.text: Change the listener from HTTP to TCP.
choices.explanation: An ALB does not have TCP listeners.

choices.text: Set routing.http.preserve_host_header.enabled to true.
choices.explanation: This allows the client's Host header to be forwarded to the backend.

choices.text: Increase the target deregistration delay.
choices.explanation: This is a connection-draining setting.

learning.reason: This allows the client's Host header to be forwarded to the backend.
learning.concept: Enabling preserve_host_header causes the ALB to preserve the Host header.

title: Applying a DNS Migration with an Atomic UPSERT
prompt: During a DNS migration, multiple A and CNAME records must be replaced at the same time. Which Route 53 API operation avoids a state in which only some changes are applied and updates existing records in the same change request?

choices.text: Create a Route 53 health check so that the records are replaced automatically.
choices.explanation: A health check is not a DNS record update API.

choices.text: Use ChangeResourceRecordSets to put multiple changes in one batch and specify UPSERT for each record.
choices.explanation: The entire batch is validated and applied atomically, and existing records can also be updated.

choices.text: Delete each record in a separate request and then create it.
choices.explanation: The intermediate state becomes visible externally, and a failure can leave the migration incomplete.

choices.text: Delete the hosted zone and recreate a zone with the same name.
choices.explanation: This destroys delegation and existing records and is not an atomic migration.

learning.reason: The entire batch is validated and applied atomically, and existing records can also be updated.
learning.concept: A ChangeResourceRecordSets change batch is applied as a transaction, while UPSERT creates or updates a record depending on whether it already exists.

title: NLB Isolating Unhealthy Targets Quickly
prompt: An NLB TCP target responds to health checks but returns failures for actual client connections. Without any additional explicit configuration, which mechanism allows the NLB to reflect failures in real traffic in its health determination?

choices.text: Configure only Route 53 failover.
choices.explanation: This does not isolate targets inside the NLB.

choices.text: Use NLB passive health checks to detect unhealthy targets based on actual connection failures.
choices.explanation: They use observations from real traffic in health determinations.

choices.text: Allow all outbound traffic in the security group.
choices.explanation: This does not detect application failures.

choices.text: Set the DNS TTL to 1 second.
choices.explanation: Updating name resolution does not evaluate target health.

learning.reason: The mechanism uses observations from real traffic in health determinations.
learning.concept: In addition to active health checks, an NLB performs passive health checks.

title: Applying Security Groups per ECS Task
prompt: You want to isolate the destinations of two ECS services on the same EC2 container instance using different Security Group rules. You cannot use an approach that applies the same Security Group to the entire host. Which network mode should you use?

choices.text: Use awsvpc network mode and configure a service-specific Security Group on each task ENI.
choices.explanation: This creates a network boundary at the task level.

choices.text: Use bridge mode with only the host Security Group.
choices.explanation: This does not provide a separate ENI and Security Group for each task.

choices.text: Change the DHCP settings of the default VPC.
choices.explanation: This does not separate communication permissions at the task level.

choices.text: Use host mode and fix the container ports.
choices.explanation: This shares the host network.

learning.reason: This creates a network boundary at the task level.
learning.concept: With awsvpc, you can associate an ENI and Security Group with each task.

title: Relieving ENI Shortages for ECS on EC2
prompt: In an EC2 launch type ECS cluster, you cannot add more awsvpc tasks because the instance has reached its ENI limit. You must retain a Security Group for each task, and you can launch Linux instances that meet the ENI trunking requirements. Which action increases the number of tasks that can run per instance?

choices.text: Add a NAT Gateway in each Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: This does not increase the ENI limit.

choices.text: Create a Cloud Map namespace.
choices.explanation: Service discovery does not increase the number of ENIs.

choices.text: Switch the tasks to host mode while retaining Security Group isolation.
choices.explanation: Host mode loses task-level ENI isolation.

choices.text: Enable awsvpcTrunking, then launch new compatible EC2 instances and gradually replace the existing instances.
choices.explanation: Compatible instances launched after it is enabled receive a trunk ENI, increasing the limit for task ENIs.

learning.reason: ECS assigns a trunk ENI to new instances launched after the feature is enabled. Re-registering existing instances does not increase the task ENI limit.
learning.concept: Launch compatible instances after enabling awsvpcTrunking.

title: Assigning an Independent Security Group to an EKS Pod
prompt: In EKS, you want to allow only payment Pods to access a database Security Group and prevent general Pods on the same node from accessing it. Which two actions enable Security Groups for Pods at the Pod level when using the VPC CNI? Select two.

choices.text: Enable Security groups for Pods.
choices.explanation: This is the prerequisite for applying an independent Security Group to a Pod's branch ENI.

choices.text: Use SecurityGroupPolicy to assign the payment Security Group to the target Pods.
choices.explanation: This grants database access only to the selected Pods.

choices.text: Add database access to the node Security Group.
choices.explanation: This broadens access to all Pods on the same node.

choices.text: Change the CoreDNS ConfigMap.
choices.explanation: DNS configuration does not assign Security Groups.

choices.text: Set the Kubernetes Service type to LoadBalancer.
choices.explanation: External exposure does not create Pod-level Security Group isolation.

learning.reason: This is the prerequisite for applying an independent Security Group to a Pod's branch ENI. It then grants database access only to the selected Pods.
learning.concept: Security groups for Pods applies Security Groups to Pods through branch ENIs provided by the VPC CNI.

title: Register an HTTP Service Name with the Cloud Map API
prompt: Multiple non-ECS workloads need to register and discover endpoints for an HTTP service. You want to use a Cloud Map API that can discover instances by attributes rather than relying only on DNS. Which namespace should you use?

choices.text: Require ECS Service Connect.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the Cloud Map API requirement for non-ECS workloads.

choices.text: Create a Route 53 public hosted zone.
choices.explanation: This provides publicly accessible DNS.

choices.text: Create an HTTP namespace and register and discover service instances through the Cloud Map API.
choices.explanation: This enables attribute-based discovery without requiring DNS records.

choices.text: Create only a private DNS namespace.
choices.explanation: This is intended for DNS name resolution and does not meet the API-based discovery requirement of an HTTP namespace.

learning.reason: Attribute-based discovery is available without relying on DNS records.
learning.concept: An HTTP namespace provides service discovery through Cloud Map APIs such as DiscoverInstances.

title: Validate CloudFormation CIDR Input Before Creation
prompt: A network stack receives an IPv4 CIDR parameter from the user. You want the template to reject an invalid string or an address format that is not allowed before the VPC creation API is called. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Set AllowedPattern and ConstraintDescription on the CIDR parameter.
choices.explanation: This validates the format before creation and communicates the constraint violation to the user.

choices.text: Define the CIDR only as an Output.
choices.explanation: An Output does not validate input.

choices.text: Set the Parameter to NoEcho.
choices.explanation: NoEcho suppresses value display; it does not validate the CIDR format.

choices.text: Reject the CIDR with a network ACL after the VPC is created.
choices.explanation: This is not input validation before resource creation.

learning.reason: The format can be validated before creation and constraint violations can be communicated to the user.
learning.concept: CloudFormation parameter AllowedPattern can validate input values with a regular expression.

title: Distribute an Internal DNS Suffix to Instances in a VPC
prompt: You want to consistently distribute the corp.example search suffix and on-premises DNS servers to EC2 instances in a new VPC from startup. Avoid configuring each instance individually. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Create a DHCP option set containing domain-name and domain-name-servers, and associate it with the VPC.
choices.explanation: This centrally distributes DNS settings to instances in the VPC.

choices.text: Allow all UDP 53 traffic in the security group.
choices.explanation: Allowing the traffic does not distribute DNS settings.

choices.text: Change the NS records in the private hosted zone.
choices.explanation: This does not distribute the DNS server settings through DHCP.

choices.text: Add the DNS server IP addresses to the route table for each subnet.
choices.explanation: Routes do not distribute a DHCP search suffix.

learning.reason: DNS settings can be centrally distributed to instances in the VPC.
learning.concept: A DHCP option set distributes domain-name and domain-name-servers settings to instances in the VPC.

title: Automatically Assign IPv6 Addresses Only at New Instance Launch
prompt: In a subnet with an IPv6 CIDR, you want to leave existing EC2 instances unchanged and automatically assign IPv6 addresses only to EC2 instances launched in this subnet in the future. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Re-create the ENIs of the existing EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement not to change existing EC2 instances.

choices.text: Register the IPv6 CIDR in the DHCP option set.
choices.explanation: A DHCP option set does not configure automatic IPv6 assignment for a subnet.

choices.text: Enable the subnet attribute AssignIpv6AddressOnCreation.
choices.explanation: This automatically assigns IPv6 addresses to instances launched in the subnet.

choices.text: Associate an Internet Gateway with the subnet.
choices.explanation: An Internet Gateway is attached to the VPC and does not control address assignment at launch.

learning.reason: IPv6 addresses can be automatically assigned to newly launched instances.
learning.concept: The subnet's auto-assign IPv6 setting controls IPv6 address assignment at launch.

title: Estimating Reserved IP Addresses in a Subnet
prompt: Before creating a small IPv4 subnet, you want to calculate the number of addresses that can actually be assigned to EC2 and other resources rather than relying on the total CIDR count. How many IP addresses does AWS reserve in a VPC subnet?

choices.text: Exactly five addresses are always reserved for both IPv4 and IPv6.
choices.explanation: The reservation rules for IPv6 subnets are not the same as those for IPv4.

choices.text: Plan for five reserved IP addresses in each IPv4 subnet.
choices.explanation: The first four addresses and the last address are reserved for VPC operations.

choices.text: Assume that only one address is reserved in each subnet.
choices.explanation: This underestimates the number of reserved addresses.

choices.text: Reserve only five addresses per Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: Addresses are reserved per subnet, not per Availability Zone.

learning.reason: The first four addresses and the last address are reserved for VPC operations.
learning.concept: In each IPv4 subnet, AWS reserves the first four addresses and the last address, for a total of five reserved addresses.

title: Adding a Subnet for EKS Control Plane ENIs
prompt: You want the control plane ENIs of an existing EKS cluster to be placeable in a newly created private subnet in addition to the two existing subnets. You do not want to change the Pod VPC CNI configuration; you only want to add availability to the communication path between the control plane and kubelets. Which action should you take?

choices.text: Use UpdateClusterConfig to add the new private subnet to subnetIds in the cluster VPC config.
choices.explanation: This updates the subnets that the control plane's cross-account ENIs can use.

choices.text: Change the ClusterIP CIDR of the EKS Service.
choices.explanation: Changing the Service CIDR of an existing cluster does not add a subnet for ENI placement.

choices.text: Add an Internet Gateway to the new subnet's route table.
choices.explanation: This is not the operation for registering a subnet for control plane ENIs.

choices.text: Configure the new subnet CIDR only in the aws-node DaemonSet.
choices.explanation: This changes Pod network configuration and does not change control plane ENI placement.

learning.reason: This updates the subnets that the control plane's cross-account ENIs can use.
learning.concept: You can specify the subnets used by EKS control plane ENIs by updating the cluster VPC config.

title: Applying an S3 Gateway Endpoint Only to Required Subnets
prompt: Of two private subnets in the same VPC, you want only the batch subnet to reach S3 without using NAT. You want to leave the S3 route for the application subnet unchanged. What should you specify when creating the gateway endpoint?

choices.text: Associate an Internet Gateway with the batch subnet.
choices.explanation: A subnet cannot be associated with an Internet Gateway, and this would not provide a private S3 path.

choices.text: Associate only the batch subnet's security group with the endpoint.
choices.explanation: A gateway endpoint cannot be associated with a security group.

choices.text: Associate only the route tables associated with the batch subnet with the gateway endpoint.
choices.explanation: Only subnets that use the specified route tables will use the endpoint.

choices.text: Create an endpoint ENI in the batch subnet.
choices.explanation: A gateway endpoint does not create an ENI.

learning.reason: Only subnets that use the specified route tables will use the endpoint.
learning.concept: A gateway endpoint adds a route for the service prefix list to the selected route tables.

title: Switching DNS Based on the Logical Result of Multiple Health Checks
prompt: You want a Route 53 failover record to be returned as primary only when two independent health checks are both healthy. You do not want to combine the monitored targets into a single HTTP check. Which action should you take?

choices.text: Increase the TTL.
choices.explanation: The cache duration does not change the health-check logic.

choices.text: Enable multivalue answer.
choices.explanation: This feature returns multiple healthy values; it does not evaluate a condition across child health checks.

choices.text: Create a calculated health check that references the two child health checks and set the required number of healthy checks to two.
choices.explanation: The calculated health check is healthy only when both child checks are healthy.

choices.text: Configure a weighted record with a 50/50 split.
choices.explanation: Weighting does not create a logical AND between health checks.

learning.reason: The calculated health check is healthy only when both child checks are healthy.
learning.concept: A calculated health check can determine its status based on the number of healthy child health checks.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Distinguishing Network Access Analyzer static analysis from real-traffic failures
prompt: You are investigating connection failures that occur only briefly after changes to route tables and security groups. You also want to verify configuration-based reachability without generating traffic, but you must not mistake this for a determination of actual packet loss or temporary service disruptions. Which operational approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use Network Access Analyzer to validate configuration-based paths, and investigate real-traffic failures separately with Flow Logs or application monitoring
choices.explanation: Correct. Static reachability and communication success during actual operations must be verified using separate evidence.

choices.text: Conclude solely from the absence of Network Access Analyzer findings that no temporary packet loss has occurred
choices.explanation: Static analysis does not account for temporary network interruptions or service disruptions.

choices.text: Stop VPC Flow Logs after enabling Network Access Analyzer
choices.explanation: Configuration analysis and real-traffic observation are complementary; enabling the analyzer is not a reason to stop the logs.

choices.text: Wait for Network Access Analyzer to send real packets for the investigation
choices.explanation: This analysis does not send packets, so waiting will not test real communications.

learning.reason: Correct. Static reachability and communication success during actual operations must be verified using separate evidence.
learning.concept: Network Access Analyzer performs static analysis of configuration without sending packets, so it does not account for loss caused by temporary interruptions or service disruptions.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Identifying ENI skew in a Resolver inbound endpoint
prompt: A Resolver inbound endpoint with multiple ENIs continues to show a capacity warning. You want to verify, per ENI, whether the on-premises DNS forwarder is using only the same IP address by checking the query count. Which combination of metrics is most appropriate?

choices.text: Sum InboundQueryVolume by EndpointId and RniId
choices.explanation: Correct. This separates inbound DNS query volume by ENI, allowing you to identify concentration on a particular IP address.

choices.text: Sum P90ResponseTime by TargetNameServerIP only
choices.explanation: Response time is not query volume, and Sum is not a valid statistic for this metric.

choices.text: Sum EndpointUnhealthyENICount by EndpointId and RniId
choices.explanation: This metric represents the number of ENIs in AUTO_RECOVERING, not the query volume for each ENI.

choices.text: Average OutboundQueryAggregateVolume by EndpointId only
choices.explanation: This is the aggregate query volume for outbound traffic and cannot identify per-IP concentration for an inbound endpoint.

learning.reason: Correct. This separates inbound DNS query volume by ENI, allowing you to identify concentration on a particular IP address.
learning.concept: Using the RniId dimension with InboundQueryVolume lets you examine each IP address of an inbound endpoint separately.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Distinguishing timeouts for a forwarding DNS target
prompt: On an outbound Resolver endpoint, name-resolution failures continue even after adding ENIs. Detailed metrics are enabled, and you want to verify that a specific on-premises DNS server is not responding. Which metric is the most direct indicator?

choices.text: Sum TimeoutQueries by EndpointId and TargetNameServerIP
choices.explanation: Correct. This directly shows timeouts occurring for a specific forwarding DNS server.

choices.text: Sum InboundQueryVolume by RniId
choices.explanation: This is inbound query volume, not timeouts to a specific outbound target.

choices.text: Maximum NxDomainQueries by EndpointId and RniId
choices.explanation: NXDOMAIN is a response indicating that a name does not exist; it does not indicate that the target server failed to respond.

choices.text: Minimum EndpointHealthyENICount by EndpointId
choices.explanation: This represents the operating state of Resolver ENIs and does not indicate timeouts at a forwarding DNS server.

learning.reason: Correct. This directly shows timeouts occurring for a specific forwarding DNS server.
learning.concept: TimeoutQueries indicates the number of timeouts for queries sent to a specific target name server through a Resolver endpoint.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Observing TLS failures from an ALB to its targets
prompt: For an ALB with an HTTPS listener, TLS between the client and the ALB succeeds, but some requests fail only when the ALB connects to HTTPS targets. Which CloudWatch metric should you check first for a mismatch in the target certificate or TLS protocol or cipher suite?

choices.text: Sum HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count
choices.explanation: This counts 5xx responses returned by targets as HTTP responses. It does not identify failures in the segment that occurs before TLS is established.

choices.text: Sum TargetTLSNegotiationErrorCount
choices.explanation: Correct. This directly counts TLS negotiation failures between the ALB and its targets.

choices.text: Sum ClientTLSNegotiationErrorCount
choices.explanation: This represents TLS failures between the client and the ALB, which is a different segment from the one in question.

choices.text: Maximum HealthyHostCount
choices.explanation: This is the number of healthy targets and does not indicate the number of failed TLS sessions with targets.

learning.reason: Correct. This directly counts TLS negotiation failures between the ALB and its targets.
learning.concept: TargetTLSNegotiationErrorCount indicates how many times the ALB could not establish a TLS session with a target.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Detecting ALB Fail-Open Routing Within a Zone
prompt: The number of healthy targets in an ALB target group in one Availability Zone fell below the threshold. In addition to checking whether the Availability Zone is excluded from DNS, you want to determine whether the ALB is sending requests to unhealthy targets within that same Availability Zone. Which metric is the most direct indicator?

choices.text: Check the Maximum of UnhealthyStateDNS
choices.explanation: This shows the state of a zone excluded from DNS, but not the number of requests routed to unhealthy targets.

choices.text: Check the Sum of ActiveZonalShiftHostCount
choices.explanation: This is the number of targets disabled by an ARC zonal shift and differs from normal routing failover.

choices.text: Check only the Sum of HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count
choices.explanation: This shows target 5xx responses, but cannot determine whether the ALB routed requests in fail-open mode.

choices.text: Check the Sum of UnhealthyRoutingRequestCount by the AvailabilityZone dimension
choices.explanation: Correct. It shows requests routed to unhealthy targets through routing failover for each Availability Zone.

learning.reason: Correct. It shows requests routed to unhealthy targets through routing failover for each Availability Zone.
learning.concept: UnhealthyRoutingRequestCount indicates the number of requests sent to unhealthy targets through routing failover.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Safely Enabling Unhealthy Draining for an NLB
prompt: An NLB target with long-lived TCP sessions is disconnected immediately after failing a health check. You want new connections to stop being sent to that target while allowing existing connections a grace period. Which settings are required in the NLB target group? Select two.

choices.text: Enable cross-zone load balancing for the NLB
choices.explanation: This controls how targets in other Availability Zones are handled; it does not define unhealthy connection draining.

choices.text: Configure the deregistration delay for unhealthy NLB targets
choices.explanation: A deregistration grace period is different from the unhealthy draining setting used after a health check failure.

choices.text: Enable client IP preservation
choices.explanation: This controls source IP handling and does not control how connections to unhealthy targets are terminated.

choices.text: Disable unhealthy connection termination
choices.explanation: Correct. Unhealthy draining cannot be enabled while connection termination remains enabled.

choices.text: Configure the unhealthy draining interval
choices.explanation: Correct. This gives existing connections to a target that became unhealthy a grace period.

learning.reason: Correct. Unhealthy draining requires disabling connection termination and configuring an interval that gives existing connections to unhealthy targets time to drain. Correct. The interval provides a grace period for those existing connections.
learning.concept: To use the NLB unhealthy draining interval, disable connection termination first, then configure the draining interval.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Monitoring NLB Zonal Health Independently of DNS Caching
prompt: Problems with registered targets persist in one Availability Zone of an NLB. Some clients continue using IP addresses previously obtained from their DNS cache, so DNS responses and connection counts alone cannot confirm the load balancer's zonal assessment. Which CloudWatch metric is most appropriate for monitoring the NLB's zonal health itself for each Availability Zone?

choices.text: Monitor the Maximum of HealthyHostCount
choices.explanation: The maximum can miss a decline in zonal health when some targets remain healthy.

choices.text: Monitor the Sum of TCP_ELB_Reset_Count
choices.explanation: This shows the number of resets, but not zonal health independently of DNS caching.
