learning.concept: For a supported ALB endpoint, Global Accelerator Standard can use client IP preservation.

title: Add Headers Based on the Retrieved Origin Response
prompt: With CloudFront, you need to inspect the status returned by the origin on a cache miss and adjust the response headers before the response is stored in the cache according to business requirements. The origin application cannot be modified. Which processing location should you use?

choices.text: Configure Lambda@Edge only for the Origin request event and process the origin response that is received.
choices.explanation: The event sent before the request reaches the origin does not contain the response to that request.

choices.text: Use DNS failover records to choose between two origins and evaluate the response-header conditions there.
choices.explanation: DNS selects a destination; it does not process CloudFront HTTP response headers.

choices.text: Configure CloudFront Functions for the Viewer request event and inspect the origin response status.
choices.explanation: When the request is received, the origin response is not yet available.

choices.text: Associate Lambda@Edge with the Origin response event and process the response returned by the origin.
choices.explanation: This lets you inspect the origin result and rewrite the response before it is stored in the cache.

learning.reason: The origin result can be inspected and the response rewritten before it is stored in the cache.
learning.concept: Lambda@Edge supports the Origin response event.

title: Update Static Assets Without Invalidating All Cached Objects at the Same Path
prompt: JavaScript is cached for a long time in CloudFront. At release time, both the new and old pages must be able to retrieve the assets they reference, and rolling back to the previous version must not require repeated invalidation at the edge. The client retrieves the HTML and selects the referenced assets. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Overwrite the objects at the current paths each time and leave the long cache duration unchanged.
choices.explanation: Users may receive an old cached object, and the new and old contents cannot be selected concurrently.

choices.text: Use the same paths and invalidate all paths on every deployment.
choices.explanation: Although this can reflect changes, it does not meet the requirements to avoid repeated invalidations and keep references to both versions in parallel.

choices.text: Update Route 53 records each time to convert the same asset paths into cache keys for the new version.
choices.explanation: Changing the DNS destination does not change the object paths handled by CloudFront.

choices.text: Include a build identifier in each asset name and switch the filenames referenced by the HTML for each version.
choices.explanation: Each version uses a different path as its cache key, and the assets referenced by older HTML can remain available.

learning.reason: Each version uses a different path as its cache key, so assets referenced by older HTML can remain available.
learning.concept: Versioned filenames allow changed and old assets to be served in parallel under different names.

title: Reflect Internal Processing That Cannot Be Judged by Connectivity Alone in DNS Failover
prompt: Services in two Regions respond to HTTP requests, but the service is considered unavailable when the processing queue within a Region exceeds a certain delay. A custom metric has already been published to CloudWatch at standard resolution, and a corresponding alarm will be used for Route 53 failover decisions. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Create a Route 53 health check that monitors the target CloudWatch alarm and associate it with the failover record.
choices.explanation: This incorporates data representing business-level delay into the DNS health decision instead of checking only port responsiveness.

choices.text: Create only a notification for the CloudWatch alarm and leave the Route 53 record fixed independently of health.
choices.explanation: The notification is generated, but its signal is not reflected in DNS failover.

choices.text: Use a TCP health check and consider the queue to have no delay whenever a connection succeeds.
choices.explanation: TCP connectivity cannot measure the application's delay threshold.

choices.text: Have each client set a short Route 53 TTL and infer queue delay from the DNS cache.
choices.explanation: DNS cache expiration is not a measurement of application processing delay.

learning.reason: Data representing business-level delay can be reflected in DNS health evaluation instead of relying only on port responsiveness.
learning.concept: Route 53 can create a health check based on the data monitored by a CloudWatch alarm.

title: Aligning the MTU for Large Transfers Through a Transit VIF
prompt: A site uses a TGW through a Direct Connect transit VIF. It wants to send IP packets as large as the entire connection path supports. An example configuration for an existing private VIF shows 9,001. What assumption should be used when designing the transit VIF?

choices.text: Because 9,001 is common to all Direct Connect VIFs, set the transit VIF to the same value.
choices.explanation: A transit VIF cannot be assumed to support the same maximum setting as a private VIF.

choices.text: Shorten the BGP Hold Timer so that 9,001 can be used end to end.
choices.explanation: Route-failure detection time does not change the packet size accepted by the VIF.

choices.text: Set only the site-side MTU to 9,001 and always leave the Direct Connect setting at 1,500.
choices.explanation: A smaller MTU remains somewhere on the path, so large IP packets cannot be sent unconditionally.

choices.text: Set the transit VIF to no more than 8,500 and use a smaller limit if another path component has one.
choices.explanation: This stays within the transit VIF jumbo-frame limit and selects a size that the entire path can carry.

learning.reason: This stays within the transit VIF jumbo-frame limit and selects a size that the entire path can carry.
learning.concept: In Direct Connect, the maximum jumbo-frame MTU differs between private VIFs and transit VIFs.

title: Using Multiple Services Through One Connection Point
prompt: Multiple application services and resources have been consolidated into an existing VPC Lattice service network and shared with the consumer. The consumer VPC should use the shared destinations in the network through one private connection point, without managing an individual endpoint for each service. Which option meets this requirement?

choices.text: Create a service network VPC endpoint in the consumer VPC that references the shared service network.
choices.explanation: The service network provides the entry point, so the services can be accessed without creating a new connection point for each one.

choices.text: Add the service names to the route for an S3 Gateway endpoint.
choices.explanation: An S3 gateway endpoint cannot target a VPC Lattice service network.

choices.text: Create a separate interface endpoint for each service.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid increasing the number of individual connection points.

choices.text: Choose one resource in the network and configure all service names on a VPC endpoint for a single resource.
choices.explanation: An endpoint for a specific resource cannot serve as an entry point for the entire network.

learning.reason: The service network provides the entry point, so the services can be accessed without creating a new connection point for each one.
learning.concept: A service network VPC endpoint provides private connectivity to multiple services and resources in the network.

title: Separating the Impact of AZ Loss with Zonal NAT Gateways
prompt: Applications in three AZs use a single zonal public NAT gateway to access external destinations. They must retain external access even if only the AZ containing an application remains available. Keep zonal NAT gateways and reduce cross-AZ forwarding. Which option meets this requirement?

choices.text: Keep the existing NAT gateway and add the same default route to all subnets in the other AZs.
choices.explanation: Subnets in the other AZs would still depend on the same NAT gateway and would not tolerate the loss of its AZ.

choices.text: Use an internet gateway directly from all subnets without assigning IP addresses to the applications.
choices.explanation: There is no translation to send private IPv4 traffic directly to external destinations.

choices.text: Attach additional Elastic IP addresses to the existing NAT gateway without changing the zonal NAT placement.
choices.explanation: Adding public IP addresses does not remove the dependency on the NAT gateway in the same AZ.

choices.text: Place a zonal NAT gateway in each AZ and point each private subnet's default route to the NAT gateway in the same AZ.
choices.explanation: The dependencies are separated by AZ, preserving outbound connectivity for a remaining AZ even if NAT in another AZ is unavailable.

learning.reason: The dependencies are separated by AZ, preserving outbound connectivity for a remaining AZ even if NAT in another AZ is unavailable.
learning.concept: A zonal NAT gateway is an AZ-level resource. Pointing each AZ's subnets to a NAT gateway in the same AZ isolates the impact of a failure.

title: Recognizing That a Small Number of Registered Entries Can Consume a Larger Route Quota
prompt: A customer-managed prefix list with a maximum of 30 entries is added as a destination to a VPC route table. The list currently contains only 12 CIDRs. When estimating the route-table quota before adding it, how should this reference be counted?

choices.text: It is a separate resource from route-table entries, so the prefix-list reference consumes no quota.
choices.explanation: In addition to the list's own management limit, the referencing side also consumes quota.

choices.text: Because the console shows only one route row, estimate that the quota will always consume one entry.
choices.explanation: A prefix-list reference does not necessarily have the same weight as the number of rows displayed.

choices.text: Calculate it as consuming 30 entries in the route-table quota.
choices.explanation: The quota used by the reference is based on the configured maximum, not the list's current number of entries.

choices.text: Estimate that only the 12 CIDRs consume quota and do not count the remaining 18.
choices.explanation: The maximum number is counted for the referenced quota even if the number of registered entries does not increase.

learning.reason: The quota used by the reference is based on the configured maximum, not the list's current number of entries.
learning.concept: A reference to a customer-managed prefix list counts its configured maximum number of entries toward the referencing side's quota.

title: Planning for the shared limit on DNS and other link-local traffic from the same ENI
prompt: A single EC2 instance generates a large number of AmazonProvidedDNS queries. The instance also uses link-local services such as time synchronization. Network bandwidth is sufficient, but the design must limit the peak number of queries from the same ENI. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Change the default route in the VPC public subnet and load-balance AmazonProvidedDNS destinations through an NLB.
choices.explanation: AmazonProvidedDNS is a local VPC capability; it is not something that can be arbitrarily distributed across the entry point of a standard NLB.

choices.text: Assume that each link-local service has a completely independent bandwidth allocation, and treat DNS load as having no effect on other traffic.
choices.explanation: A shared limit applies to the aggregate link-local packets from the same ENI.

choices.text: Increase the number of outbound NAT gateways to increase the limit on link-local packets generated from the same ENI.
choices.explanation: Link-local traffic is not controlled by the capacity of outbound NAT gateways.

choices.text: Estimate the combined link-local usage from the same ENI and reduce queries through DNS caching and similar measures.
choices.explanation: This accounts for a shared packet-rate limit that cannot be avoided merely by having sufficient bandwidth.

learning.reason: This accounts for a shared packet-rate limit that cannot be avoided merely by having sufficient bandwidth.
learning.concept: Packets sent to Route 53 Resolver and other link-local services count toward a shared per-network-interface limit.

title: Reducing latency variation between compatible EC2 instances without changing existing sockets
prompt: The application uses regular TCP sockets between compatible EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone. The application code cannot be changed, and the solution will not migrate to EFA and Libfabric. Which AWS-managed capability should be used to reduce high-percentile latency caused by congestion?

choices.text: Enable ENA Express on the network interfaces at both compatible ends.
choices.explanation: This can improve latency variation between compatible senders and receivers while retaining the regular TCP application.

choices.text: Increase the MTU on each instance so that ENA Express automatically uses SRD transmission.
choices.explanation: The MTU setting and the setting that enables ENA Express on an interface are separate.

choices.text: Switch the application to an EFA-only interface and use Libfabric directly through the existing TCP sockets.
choices.explanation: Using EFA-only transmission requires a compatible application path and is different from using the existing regular TCP connection unchanged.

choices.text: Enable ENA Express only on the sender and use an unsupported interface on the receiver.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the conditions at both ends of a connection that uses ENA Express.

learning.reason: This can improve latency variation between compatible senders and receivers while retaining the regular TCP application.
learning.concept: ENA Express is used through compatible sender and receiver interfaces and can provide the benefits of SRD transmission for existing TCP traffic.

title: Matching protection-group aggregation methods to their purposes
prompt: For multiple groups of entry points protected by Shield Advanced, select one aggregation method for each design intention. Use each candidate once.

choices.text: Mean
choices.explanation: Evaluate the average traffic across multiple entry points.

choices.text: Max
choices.explanation: Evaluate the entry point with the greatest amount of traffic.

choices.text: Sum
choices.explanation: Evaluate the total traffic observed across all target entry points.

learning.reason: Evaluate the total traffic observed across all target entry points. Evaluate the average traffic across multiple entry points. Evaluate the entry point with the greatest amount of traffic.
learning.concept: Shield Advanced protection groups evaluate member traffic using one of three aggregation methods: Sum, Mean, or Max.

prompts.text: Evaluate multiple entry points that receive distributed traffic for one application using the combined amount for the entire application.
Even when members are added, the signal to evaluate is the average per entry point, calculated by dividing by the number of members.
To reflect an anomaly concentrated at one entry point, use the amount received by the member receiving the most traffic.

title: Match CloudFront origin wait times to their purposes
prompt: For a CloudFront custom origin, configure constraints with different waiting-time purposes. Select one setting for each constraint. Use each candidate exactly once.

choices.text: Connection timeout
choices.explanation: Limits how long CloudFront waits to establish a connection with the origin.

choices.text: Response timeout
choices.explanation: Limits how long CloudFront can wait to receive the initial response and the time allowed between subsequent packets.

choices.text: Response completion timeout
choices.explanation: Limits the total time until the origin response is complete, even if packets arrive in small increments.

learning.reason: Connection timeout limits the time CloudFront waits to establish a connection with the origin. Response timeout limits the wait for the initial response and between subsequent packets. Response completion timeout limits the total time until the origin response is complete, even when packets arrive gradually.
learning.concept: CloudFront has separate settings for connection establishment, the start and continuation of the origin response, and the total time until the response is complete.

prompts.text: Set a maximum wait time for the stage in which a connection to the origin is established.
Limit the wait for the first response after connection and for a subsequent response packet while receiving data.
Set a maximum total retrieval time, even for an origin that sends its response gradually.

title: Choose where to configure the setting that evaluates ALB health through an accelerator
prompt: A standard Global Accelerator has an ALB endpoint. When the target application’s readiness path is changed to /ready, you want the health determination for the entry point that uses the ALB to follow that change. The accelerator listener ports and traffic destinations remain unchanged. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Shorten the Route 53 cache time and assume that the health evaluation path will be updated.
choices.explanation: DNS cache duration and the load balancer’s monitoring path are separate settings.

choices.text: Increase the dial for the target Region in Global Accelerator and assume that the health determination path will also change to /ready.
choices.explanation: The dial controls the amount of traffic; it does not change the path used to measure health.

choices.text: Change the target group health check on the ALB to /ready.
choices.explanation: This change is reflected in the load balancer health evaluation used by the accelerator.

choices.text: Specify /ready only in the Global Accelerator endpoint group and keep the old health check on the ALB.
choices.explanation: For an ELB endpoint, the ALB health check configuration is used; changing only the endpoint group does not override it.

learning.reason: The change is reflected in the load balancer health evaluation used by the accelerator.
learning.concept: Global Accelerator determines the health of an ELB endpoint based on the Elastic Load Balancing configuration.

title: Forward traffic to dynamically replaced internal services without a load balancer
prompt: The HTTP API backend consists of internal application instances using different ports, and AWS Cloud Map registers each instance’s private IP address and port. Integrate the backend from API Gateway using a VPC Link without operating fixed IP addresses or an additional load balancer. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Register Cloud Map as a public custom origin for CloudFront and bypass API Gateway.
choices.explanation: This does not create a private integration using a VPC Link that specifies the Cloud Map service ARN.

choices.text: Create a VPC Link, but distribute the address of the first EC2 instance to users as the backend list.
choices.explanation: This does not propagate Cloud Map registration updates to the integration’s destinations and requires static destination management on the client side.

choices.text: Specify the current private IP address of one instance in API Gateway’s public HTTP integration and do not update it after instances change.
choices.explanation: A fixed destination does not follow instance replacement, and a public integration does not use the VPC Link path.

choices.text: Configure a private integration using a VPC Link and the Cloud Map service ARN.
choices.explanation: API Gateway can forward traffic to the IP addresses and ports of applications discovered through Cloud Map, eliminating the need for a fixed backend list.

learning.reason: API Gateway can forward traffic to the IP addresses and ports of applications discovered through Cloud Map, eliminating the need for a fixed backend list.
learning.concept: An HTTP API can reference a Cloud Map service in a private integration and retrieve registered IP addresses and ports with DiscoverInstances.

title: Keep uploads from around the world in a bucket in the same Region
prompt: Users send large measurement files from remote locations to an S3 bucket in the same Region. Without replicating the data to another Region, use an upload entry point that routes traffic through AWS edge locations. The bucket name and target Region are compatible with the feature. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Set a short TTL in Route 53 for the current S3 DNS name.
choices.explanation: Changing the frequency of DNS resolution does not turn S3 transfer into an accelerated edge-routed path.

choices.text: Create new buckets in multiple Regions and store the data separately with a Multi-Region Access Point.
choices.explanation: This distributes uploads across multiple buckets and does not meet the requirement to keep uploads in a single bucket in the same Region.

choices.text: Enable Transfer Acceleration on the bucket and use the acceleration endpoint for client uploads.
choices.explanation: Remote clients connect to an edge location and can transfer data to the same target bucket.

choices.text: Enable cross-Region replication and keep using the normal Region-specific upload entry point.
choices.explanation: This replicates data after upload but does not accelerate the transfer entry path.

learning.reason: Remote clients connect to an edge location and can transfer data to the same target bucket.
learning.concept: S3 Transfer Acceleration uses edge locations for transfers to the same bucket.

title: Version a multi-condition DNS routing policy and test it before production
prompt: A public DNS configuration combines geographic and health-based conditions. You want to reuse the same basic policy under multiple names and apply the next routing change to the production name only after validating it with a test name. Do not change the existing production response first. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Point the test name and production name to the same CNAME and assume that shortening the DNS TTL will also separate policy versions.
choices.explanation: Pointing both names to the same target does not allow an independent test policy to be selected for the test name.

choices.text: Create a new version of the same traffic policy, adopt it with a test policy record, and then update the production record.
choices.explanation: During testing, the production record continues to use the previous version, while only the new version of the same policy is tested.

choices.text: Disable the production health check only during testing and alternate between the old and new routes with the same record.
choices.explanation: This affects production evaluation and does not provide separate policy versions for each name.

choices.text: Update every name with a policy record to the new destinations first and fix problems found during testing by clearing the DNS cache.
choices.explanation: This changes the production route before testing and violates the requirement.

learning.reason: During testing, the production record continues to use the previous version, while only the new version of the same policy is tested.
learning.concept: Route 53 Traffic Flow separates reusable traffic policies and their versions from policy records that use a specific version.

title: Isolate New Attachments Before Connecting Them
prompt: When a new VPC attachment is created for the central TGW, you do not want it to be automatically associated with the default route table until review is complete. Which two actions ensure that it is connected to the production route table only after review? Select two.

choices.text: Disable Default route table association.
choices.explanation: This allows the routes for new attachments to be managed explicitly.

choices.text: Disable only Default route table propagation.
choices.explanation: The association itself remains with the default table.

choices.text: Change the TGW ASN.
choices.explanation: The ASN does not control which route table an attachment is associated with.

choices.text: Explicitly associate the reviewed attachment with the intended TGW route table.
choices.explanation: The attachment uses the required route table's routes only after approval.

choices.text: Delete the VPC's main route table.
choices.explanation: This does not control TGW associations.

learning.reason: This allows the routes for new attachments to be managed explicitly. The attachment uses the required route table's routes only after approval.
learning.concept: When Default route table association is disabled, attachments must be associated explicitly.

title: Distinguish the VPC ID and Default Security Group ID with CloudFormation
prompt: In the same template, create a VPC, pass its VPC ID to one resource, and pass the VPC's default security group ID to a different rule. Which approach correctly uses CloudFormation return values without constructing strings?

choices.text: Reference the Outputs Description.
choices.explanation: The description does not return a resource identifier.

choices.text: Use Ref for the VPC ID and the Fn::GetAtt DefaultSecurityGroup attribute for the default security group ID.
choices.explanation: This uses the return values defined for each resource type.

choices.text: Use Ref for both values.
choices.explanation: Ref returns the VPC ID, not the Security Group ID.

choices.text: Use GetAtt CidrBlock for both values.
choices.explanation: The CIDR is neither the VPC ID nor the Security Group ID.

learning.reason: This uses the return values defined for each resource type.
learning.concept: For AWS::EC2::VPC, Ref returns the VPC ID and GetAtt DefaultSecurityGroup returns the default Security Group ID.

title: Update the Client VPN Server Certificate with Minimal Disruption
prompt: You are updating the ACM server certificate used by an AWS Client VPN endpoint. You will modify the endpoint configuration by specifying the ARN of the new certificate and want to minimize the impact on existing clients. What operational decision is required after changing the configuration?

choices.text: Change only the clients' DNS servers.
choices.explanation: A DNS change does not update the endpoint's certificate.

choices.text: Re-create only the Client VPN route table.
choices.explanation: Routing configuration does not update the TLS server certificate.

choices.text: Change the server certificate ARN to the new ACM certificate and instruct users to reconnect.
choices.explanation: The new certificate can be applied to the endpoint configuration, and existing sessions establish new connections after reconnecting.

choices.text: Replace the ACM certificate while keeping the same ARN and do not change the Client VPN configuration.
choices.explanation: The new certificate has a different ARN, so the endpoint's certificate ARN must be updated.

learning.reason: The new certificate can be applied to the endpoint configuration, and existing sessions establish new connections after reconnecting.
learning.concept: After changing the Client VPN endpoint's server certificate ARN, existing connections must reconnect.

title: Reuse Network Components from a Parent Stack
prompt: Multiple environments use the same VPC, subnet, and route template components. You want the parent stack to pass environment-specific values and manage updates to the child template as stacks. Which CloudFormation configuration should you use?

choices.text: Make the shared network template a nested stack and pass parameters from the parent's AWS::CloudFormation::Stack resource.
choices.explanation: This allows the shared components to be reused and updated as an independent template.

choices.text: Import an exported value with ImportValue from another Region.
choices.explanation: ImportValue cannot cross Regions.

choices.text: Build the template using only CloudTrail events.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail does not provide template composition functionality.

choices.text: Manually create resources with the same names in each environment.
choices.explanation: This does not provide reusable components or consistent management.

learning.reason: This allows the shared components to be reused and updated as an independent template.
learning.concept: A nested stack can be referenced from the parent template as AWS::CloudFormation::Stack.

title: Stopping a Network Update with a Monitoring Alarm
prompt: When a CloudWatch alarm for the connection failure rate enters ALARM during a stack update, you want CloudFormation to roll back the update. Which configuration avoids relying only on manual monitoring?

choices.text: Specify the target CloudWatch alarm as a rollback trigger in the stack update's rollback configuration.
choices.explanation: The alarm can cause an automatic rollback during the update monitoring period.

choices.text: Set all resources to Allow in the stack policy.
choices.explanation: This does not monitor the update or roll it back.

choices.text: Enable termination protection.
choices.explanation: This protects the stack from deletion; it does not link an alarm to an update.

choices.text: Configure the alarm action to send only an SNS notification.
choices.explanation: A notification alone does not roll back the CloudFormation update.

learning.reason: The alarm can cause an automatic rollback during the update monitoring period.
learning.concept: When a CloudWatch alarm is specified as a rollback trigger, an alarm during the update can cause a rollback.

title: Detecting Manual Changes as Drift from a Managed Stack
prompt: An inbound rule was manually added to a Security Group managed by CloudFormation as an emergency response. You want to list the current differences between the template and the actual resource without executing an update. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Execute a change set.
choices.explanation: A change set shows proposed update differences, not existing manual changes.

choices.text: Extend the CloudTrail retention period.
choices.explanation: API auditing does not calculate differences from the template.

choices.text: Delete and recreate the stack.
choices.explanation: This is destructive and goes beyond checking the differences.

choices.text: Start drift detection on the target stack and check the drift status of the Security Group resource.
choices.explanation: This can identify differences between the running resource and the template.

learning.reason: This can identify differences between the running resource and the template.
learning.concept: Drift detection identifies differences between a stack template and the actual resources.

title: Managing Organization-Owned Public IPv4 Addresses with IPAM
prompt: A company has obtained a public IPv4 CIDR from an RIR and wants to use it for EC2 in an AWS account while tracking its AWS allocations and utilization with IPAM. Which IPAM scope should it use?

choices.text: Add the public CIDR to the IPAM public scope and manage its allocations.
choices.explanation: This tracks public addresses used in AWS.

choices.text: Register the CIDR in a Route 53 hosted zone.
choices.explanation: A DNS zone does not manage IP allocations.

choices.text: Associate the CIDR with a NAT Gateway.
choices.explanation: A NAT Gateway is not an IPAM address-management boundary.

choices.text: Put the public CIDR only in the private scope.
choices.explanation: The private scope is for managing private addresses.

learning.reason: This tracks public addresses used in AWS.
learning.concept: The IPAM public scope manages public IP addresses used in AWS.

title: Having IPAM Discover CIDR Usage Across the Organization
prompt: You want a central IPAM to discover VPC CIDRs created in multiple accounts under AWS Organizations and use them for capacity planning. You want to avoid having each account enter CIDRs manually. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Share a Route 53 Resolver rule with each account.
choices.explanation: Sharing a DNS rule does not discover CIDRs.

choices.text: Integrate IPAM with AWS Organizations and enable resource discovery through the management account or a delegated administrator.
choices.explanation: This centrally discovers address usage by VPCs in the organization.

choices.text: Move all VPCs into a single account.
choices.explanation: This is unnecessary for organization-wide discovery and has significant impact.

choices.text: List the CIDRs in a CloudFormation Export.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid manual entry.

learning.reason: This centrally discovers address usage by VPCs in the organization.
learning.concept: Integrating IPAM with Organizations enables discovery of CIDRs used by resources in the organization.

title: Assign IPv6 Addresses to Pods in an EKS IPv6 Cluster
prompt: A new EKS cluster should use IPv6 as the primary Pod address family, and the VPC CNI should assign IPv6 addresses to Pods. The existing cluster must not be converted later from IPv4 mode. Which creation-time settings are required?

choices.text: Change only the Service CIDR of the existing IPv4 cluster to IPv6.
choices.explanation: The cluster's ipFamily cannot be changed.

choices.text: Set ipFamily to IPv6 when creating the cluster and use an IPv6-compatible VPC and subnet.
choices.explanation: This configures IPv6 Pod networking for a new cluster.

choices.text: Only create a NAT Gateway.
choices.explanation: A NAT Gateway does not change the EKS Pod IP family.

choices.text: Restart CoreDNS.
choices.explanation: Restarting DNS does not change the Pod addressing method.

learning.reason: IPv6 Pod networking can be configured for a new cluster.
learning.concept: The EKS IPv6 family must be specified when the cluster is created.

title: Place EKS Fargate Pods in Private Subnets
prompt: Pods selected by an EKS Fargate profile must be placed in private subnets without direct reachability from the internet. What must be specified so that Fargate recognizes the profile's subnets and assigns networking to the Pods?

choices.text: Assume that placing Fargate Pods in public subnets automatically assigns them public IP addresses.
choices.explanation: Public IP addresses are not automatically assigned to Fargate Pods.

choices.text: Specify private subnet IDs in the Fargate profile's subnets and configure required outbound access separately, such as through a NAT Gateway.
choices.explanation: Pod ENIs are placed in the specified subnets, avoiding direct internet reachability.

choices.text: Add the subnet CIDR to a CoreDNS record.
choices.explanation: DNS records do not select the placement subnets for a Fargate profile.

choices.text: Set the subnet ID in the Service's ClusterIP range.
choices.explanation: The Service CIDR does not specify the subnet where Fargate Pods are placed.

learning.reason: Pod ENIs can be placed in the specified subnets, avoiding direct internet reachability.
learning.concept: A Fargate profile specifies the subnets where Pods are launched, and using private subnets is recommended.

title: Avoid a Rapid Increase in ENIs for Lambda VPC Connectivity
prompt: Many Lambda functions use the same subnet and Security Group to connect to a VPC. Without assuming that each function creates its own ENI, which statement correctly describes the use of AWS-managed shared network interfaces?

choices.text: When Lambda is in a VPC, it automatically has internet access.
choices.explanation: A separate egress configuration, such as a NAT Gateway or an IPv6 route, is required.

choices.text: The Lambda security group only needs inbound port 443.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the egress requirements for communication initiated by the function.

choices.text: Functions that use the same subnet/Security Group combination share a Hyperplane ENI, so an ENI per function is not assumed.
choices.explanation: This correctly describes the ENI management implementation.

choices.text: Every concurrent execution always creates a new customer-managed ENI.
choices.explanation: This is not how Lambda VPC connectivity works.

learning.reason: This correctly describes the ENI management implementation.
learning.concept: Lambda shares a Hyperplane ENI for functions using the same subnet and Security Group combination.

title: Implement Outbound Internet Access for a Lambda Function in a VPC
prompt: An IPv4 Lambda function connected to a private subnet must call an external SaaS API over HTTPS. The Lambda function must remain in a private subnet, and its source must be allowlisted using a fixed EIP. Which option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Associate an Internet Gateway directly with the subnet.
choices.explanation: An Internet Gateway is attached to the VPC and does not perform source translation for a private IPv4 Lambda function.

choices.text: Create an interface endpoint for the SaaS's public API.
choices.explanation: The external SaaS would need to provide an AWS PrivateLink service for this to work.

choices.text: Route 0.0.0.0/0 to a NAT Gateway in the private subnet's route table, and assign an Elastic IP to the NAT Gateway.
choices.explanation: This allows the Lambda function's outbound IPv4 traffic to use a fixed EIP.

choices.text: Automatically assign a public IP address to the Lambda function.
choices.explanation: Lambda VPC connections do not support automatic public IP assignment.

learning.reason: The Lambda function's outbound IPv4 traffic can use a fixed EIP.
learning.concept: A private-subnet Lambda function needs a NAT Gateway or another suitable egress path for IPv4 internet access.

title: Restricting a private API to a specified VPC endpoint
prompt: A private REST API in API Gateway must be callable only through one interface endpoint for execute-api in the organization. Which condition should be used in the API resource policy to inspect the entry point, in addition to using security groups (SGs)?

choices.text: In the resource policy Condition, match aws:SourceVpce to the allowed VPCE ID.
choices.explanation: This can deny API calls from endpoints other than the specified endpoint.

choices.text: Set the VPC CIDR in the API stage name.
choices.explanation: A stage name does not restrict the calling endpoint.

choices.text: Change the API to edge-optimized.
choices.explanation: This would remove the private API endpoint restriction.

choices.text: Set the endpoint policy to the CloudFront distribution ID.
choices.explanation: This is not a resource policy condition for the private API entry point.

learning.reason: This can deny API calls from endpoints other than the specified endpoint.
learning.concept: A private API resource policy can restrict VPC endpoints by using the aws:SourceVpce condition.

title: BGP neighbor fails to establish because of an ASN mismatch
prompt: For a dynamically routed Site-to-Site VPN, the IPsec tunnel is UP, but the BGP neighbor does not reach Established. AWS expects the customer gateway ASN specified in the VPN configuration. Which item should be aligned first?

choices.text: Change the route table destination to 0.0.0.0/0.
choices.explanation: Changing the route table does not fix an ASN mismatch in the BGP OPEN message.

choices.text: Configure the VPN tunnel's pre-shared key as the BGP ASN.
choices.explanation: The PSK is used for IPsec authentication, not as the BGP ASN.

choices.text: Distribute the ASN through the VPC DHCP option set.
choices.explanation: DHCP does not distribute BGP peer settings.

choices.text: Set the customer gateway device's local ASN to match the customer gateway ASN specified for the AWS VPN connection.
choices.explanation: This resolves the BGP peer ASN mismatch and satisfies a prerequisite for establishing the neighbor relationship.

learning.reason: This resolves the BGP peer ASN mismatch and satisfies a prerequisite for establishing the neighbor relationship.
learning.concept: For a dynamically routed VPN, the customer gateway's BGP ASN must match the BGP information in the configuration file.

title: Avoiding the Initial Reconnection Delay of an Unused VPC Link
prompt: If an HTTP API VPC link is unused for a long period, the next request may be delayed while the connection is recreated. The business requires consistently low latency. Which is the most direct mitigation?

choices.text: Allow the VPC link's security group to accept traffic from 0.0.0.0/0.
choices.explanation: This does not prevent the link from becoming unused and also reduces security.

choices.text: Periodically generate real requests through the VPC link and keep the unused period under 60 days.
choices.explanation: This avoids the transition to INACTIVE and the delay caused by recreating the connection.

choices.text: Make the API edge-optimized.
choices.explanation: This does not change the lifecycle of an HTTP API VPC link.

choices.text: Increase the ALB idle timeout to 60 days.
choices.explanation: This is unrelated to the VPC link's unused state.

learning.reason: This avoids the transition to INACTIVE and the delay caused by recreating the connection.
learning.concept: A VPC link becomes INACTIVE after 60 days without use, and its ENI must be recreated when the link is used again.

title: Excluding AWS service name resolution from external forwarding
prompt: A VPC has a Resolver rule that forwards corp.example to on-premises. The VPC Resolver must resolve standard AWS service DNS names on the AWS side instead of accidentally sending them to external DNS. Which behavior should you understand?

choices.text: Change the DNS settings of the NAT Gateway.
choices.explanation: A NAT Gateway does not process Resolver rules.

choices.text: Rely on the Resolver's autodefined rules to process queries for internal AWS domains, and avoid creating an overly broad forwarding rule.
choices.explanation: This avoids misconfiguring AWS service names to be forwarded unconditionally to on-premises.

choices.text: Remove AmazonProvidedDNS from the DHCP option set.
choices.explanation: This would prevent use of the VPC Resolver and contradict the requirement.

choices.text: Create a public hosted zone for each AWS service.
choices.explanation: Users cannot replace the authoritative DNS for standard AWS service names this way.

learning.reason: This avoids misconfiguring AWS service names to be forwarded unconditionally to on-premises.
learning.concept: The Resolver's autodefined rules appropriately process queries for AWS domains and other internal names.

title: Detach VPC associations before deleting a shared Resolver rule
prompt: A Resolver rule associated with multiple VPCs is being retired. Which sequence should be used to avoid dependency errors during deletion and keep the scope of the DNS resolution change clear?

choices.text: Delete the rule first so that the VPC associations are deleted automatically.
choices.explanation: A rule with remaining associations cannot be deleted.

choices.text: Delete the Resolver endpoint ENIs so that the associations are no longer needed.
choices.explanation: VPC associations for a rule are a separate dependency.

choices.text: Delete the VPC's Internet Gateway before deleting the rule.
choices.explanation: The IGW is unrelated to Resolver rule associations.

choices.text: Remove all VPC associations before deleting the Resolver rule.
choices.explanation: This resolves the dependencies and allows the rule to be retired safely.

learning.reason: This resolves the dependencies and allows the rule to be retired safely.
learning.concept: A Resolver rule cannot be deleted while VPCs remain associated with it.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Distinguish signs of missing responses for new connections through a NAT gateway
prompt: Failures of new connections to an external API through a NAT gateway have increased. You want to determine whether the client's SYN packets may be receiving no response rather than encountering port-allocation errors. Which comparison is most appropriate?

choices.text: Compare BytesOutToDestination using Average.
choices.explanation: This shows the amount of data transferred, but does not determine whether new connections were established.

choices.text: Check only IdleTimeoutCount.
choices.explanation: This metric concerns existing idle connections and does not indicate whether new SYN packets received a response.

choices.text: Check only PacketsDropCount.
choices.explanation: This shows that packets were dropped, but does not limit the result to cases where the initial connection received no response.

choices.text: Compare ConnectionAttemptCount and ConnectionEstablishedCount using Sum.
choices.explanation: The difference between the number of initial SYN attempts and established connections can be used to investigate new connections that received no response.

learning.reason: The difference between the number of initial SYN attempts and established connections can be used to investigate new connections that received no response.
learning.concept: When ConnectionEstablishedCount is lower than ConnectionAttemptCount, it indicates that some connection attempts did not receive a response from the client perspective.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Detect a decrease in IPv4 routes accepted by AWS on the same BGP session
prompt: On the target Direct Connect VIF, the IPv4 BGP session remains established, but after a filter change on the on-premises side, only some on-premises networks are reachable. You want to determine whether the number of IPv4 prefixes accepted by AWS from the on-premises side has decreased. Which metric should you use?

choices.text: Check VirtualInterfaceBgpPrefixesAdvertised for the target VirtualInterfaceId.
choices.explanation: This is the number of routes advertised by AWS to its peer, which is the opposite direction from the routes received from the on-premises side.

choices.text: Check VirtualInterfaceBgpPrefixesAccepted for the target VirtualInterfaceId and IPv4 IpAddressFamily.
choices.explanation: This limits the measurement to IPv4 and measures changes in the number of routes AWS accepts from its peer.

choices.text: Use VirtualInterfaceBpsIngress to determine which on-premises prefixes can no longer be used.
choices.explanation: Inbound data volume is not the number of accepted routes or a list of the accepted destinations.

choices.text: Check only that VirtualInterfaceBgpStatus is 1, indicating that the session is up.
choices.explanation: A session can remain UP while filters reduce the number of accepted routes, and this metric does not show that number.

learning.reason: This limits the measurement to IPv4 and measures changes in the number of routes AWS accepts from its peer.
learning.concept: VirtualInterfaceBgpPrefixesAccepted indicates the number of prefixes accepted by AWS from its BGP peer.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Use a state value to identify a partially established VPN tunnel configuration
prompt: In a two-tunnel Site-to-Site VPN configuration using BGP, you suspect that only one tunnel is not ESTABLISHED. Even if at least one tunnel in the VPN connection is up, which TunnelState value indicates that not all tunnels are up?

choices.text: A value greater than 0 and less than 1
choices.explanation: This indicates that at least one tunnel in the VPN connection is not up.

choices.text: ConnectionState equal to 0
choices.explanation: This is a Direct Connect metric, not a VPN tunnel-state metric.

choices.text: Always 1
choices.explanation: This indicates that all tunnels are healthy and does not show that one side is not established.

choices.text: TunnelDataOut equal to 0
choices.explanation: Background monitoring traffic can still produce a value, so this cannot be used to determine the tunnel state.

learning.reason: This indicates that at least one tunnel in the VPN connection is not up.
learning.concept: For a BGP VPN, TunnelState is 1 when the tunnel is ESTABLISHED and 0 otherwise; a value between 0 and 1 indicates that at least one tunnel is not up.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Investigating why users still cannot reach a new authoritative DNS server
prompt: You intended to transfer example.com to Route 53, but users still receive the pre-cutover response after its expiration. Direct queries to the four name servers in the new hosted zone return the new data, while a public DNS trace shows that the parent zone delegates to the old name server group. What should you fix?

choices.text: Update the application load balancer's target group to select the authoritative DNS server again.
choices.explanation: The downstream application configuration does not change the delegation target followed through the DNS hierarchy.

choices.text: Shorten only the A-record TTL in the new Route 53 zone.
choices.explanation: The current parent delegation points to the old servers, so the new zone's TTL is not yet used by clients for resolution.

choices.text: Update the delegation at the registrar to the name server group for the new Route 53 hosted zone.
choices.explanation: When recursive resolvers follow the parent, they can then reach the authoritative DNS servers containing the changed data.

choices.text: Wait after making only the resource records in the new hosted zone reach the INSYNC state.
choices.explanation: The new authoritative DNS servers are already responding correctly; the delegation in the parent zone must be fixed.

learning.reason: When recursive resolvers follow the parent, they can then reach the authoritative DNS servers containing the changed data.
learning.concept: To make a public hosted zone actually serve users, the hosted zone's name servers must be registered in the delegation from the parent zone.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Check Flow Logs delivery status before concluding that no traffic exists
prompt: You added a configuration to send VPC Flow Logs to CloudWatch Logs. Other evidence confirms traffic from the target ENI, but the new log group contains no records. You want to determine whether delivery failed on the configuration side and investigate the failure reason returned by AWS. Which action should you take?

choices.text: Conclude that the target ENI had no traffic because there are no records in CloudWatch Logs.
choices.explanation: A delivery failure can also result in no visible records, so this does not prove that no traffic occurred.

choices.text: Inspect the target Flow Log with DescribeFlowLogs and check its delivery status and error message.
choices.explanation: This separates the presence of traffic records from the configuration-related reason why the logs could not be delivered.

choices.text: Increase the CloudWatch Logs retention period and conclude that records that failed to arrive immediately after configuration will necessarily be recovered.
choices.explanation: Retention applies to logs that have already been stored; it does not restore the cause of a delivery failure or undelivered records.

choices.text: Use only AWS Reachability Analyzer to investigate the error code for delivery permissions to the destination.
choices.explanation: It analyzes network reachability and does not report Flow Logs delivery results or IAM permission errors.

learning.reason: This separates the presence of traffic records from the configuration-related reason why the logs could not be delivered.
learning.concept: VPC Flow Logs delivery errors can be investigated from the flow log status and delivery error message.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Investigating RSTs after an NLB idle timeout
prompt: With a TCP NLB, an RST is returned only when a client sends again on a connection that was idle for a long time. The target is not unhealthy. Which two methods can you use during the initial investigation to confirm the hypothesis that the reset occurred after the NLB idle timeout? Select two.

choices.text: Disable client IP preservation.
choices.explanation: This concerns how the source IP is handled and does not change the tracking lifetime of an idle connection.

choices.text: Extend the deregistration delay.
choices.explanation: This is the grace period for target deregistration, not the NLB idle timeout.

choices.text: Check TCP_ELB_Reset_Count.
choices.explanation: This can confirm an increase in the number of TCP resets generated by the NLB.

choices.text: Increase HealthyHostCount.
choices.explanation: When the targets are healthy, increasing this metric does not eliminate RSTs for connections that expired while idle.

choices.text: Use VPC Flow Logs to investigate the client that retransmitted on the expired flow.
choices.explanation: This can help correlate the reset with the client using an old flow.

learning.reason: This can confirm an increase in the number of TCP resets generated by the NLB. It can also help correlate the reset with the client using an old flow.
learning.concept: An NLB stops tracking a connection after its idle timeout and returns an RST when the client sends afterward. You can investigate this with TCP_ELB_Reset_Count and VPC Flow Logs.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Distinguishing ENI exhaustion in Lambda VPC configuration
prompt: You are updating the network configuration of many Lambda functions in the same VPC. Some deployments failed with ENILimitReachedException. The subnets have sufficient IPv4 addresses, and the required IAM permissions have been verified. What should you check first?

choices.text: Extend the CloudWatch Logs retention period and wait to see whether retries of log writes succeed.
choices.explanation: The failure occurs while creating network interfaces for the function's VPC connection, not while storing logs.

choices.text: Check VPC ENI usage and quotas, and consider cleaning up unnecessary combinations or requesting a quota adjustment.
choices.explanation: The exception is related to the number of ENIs that can be created in the VPC; available subnet IPs alone do not resolve it.

choices.text: Add a forwarding rule for external domains to the VPC DNS resolver.
choices.explanation: Changing name resolution does not change the limit on ENIs that can be created in the VPC.

choices.text: Increase the Lambda function timeout to raise the available network-interface limit.
choices.explanation: Function execution time and the ENI creation limit are managed separately.

learning.reason: The exception is related to the number of ENIs that can be created in the VPC; available subnet IPs alone do not resolve it.
learning.concept: When Lambda returns ENILimitReachedException for VPC networking configuration, check the quota for network interfaces associated with the VPC.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Monitoring Translated Traffic with 1:1 NAT in a Transit Gateway
prompt: An attachment uses 1:1 NAT in a Transit Gateway. You want to monitor only the packets received by the Transit Gateway from SNATed sources separately from the overall PacketsIn. Which metric should you use?

choices.text: Sum PacketsOutNAT by the TransitGatewayAttachment dimension
choices.explanation: These are packets the Transit Gateway sends to DNATed destinations, not packets received from SNATed sources.

choices.text: Sum PacketDropCountNoRoute
choices.explanation: This counts packets dropped because no route matched; it does not measure the volume of NAT-translated packets.

choices.text: Sum PacketsInNAT by the TransitGatewayAttachment dimension
choices.explanation: This lets you aggregate separately the packets entering the target attachment from SNATed sources.

choices.text: Sum PacketsIn by the TransitGatewayAttachment dimension
choices.explanation: This includes all received packets and is not limited to the NAT-translated subset.

learning.reason: This lets you aggregate separately the packets entering the target attachment from SNATed sources.
learning.concept: PacketsInNAT counts packets received by the Transit Gateway from sources SNATed by the attachment's NAT rule.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Detecting Invalid Event Responses from a CloudFront Function
prompt: A CloudFront Function completes execution, but the event object it returns does not meet CloudFront's requirements, causing delivery to fail. Which CloudWatch metric detects this type of problem in production requests at the LIVE stage?

choices.text: Sum FunctionValidationErrors
choices.explanation: This detects cases in which the function executed but returned invalid data.

choices.text: Average CacheHitRate
choices.explanation: This is the cache utilization rate and is unrelated to validation of a CloudFront Function's return value.

choices.text: Sum FunctionExecutionErrors
choices.explanation: This represents runtime errors that prevented execution from completing, which differs from an invalid event returned after execution.

choices.text: Sum FunctionInvocations
choices.explanation: This counts invocations and does not indicate whether the returned event is valid.

learning.reason: This detects cases in which the function executed but returned invalid data.
learning.concept: FunctionValidationErrors indicates the number of validation errors caused by an invalid event object returned after function execution.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Monitoring a CloudFront Function Approaching Its Execution-Time Limit
prompt: A CloudFront Function becomes slower after production traffic increases, and its processing time is approaching the permitted limit. Which metric shows the percentage of the function's execution time relative to that limit?

choices.text: Sum Requests
choices.explanation: This is the number of delivery requests and does not show the percentage of execution time used by the function.

choices.text: Average FunctionComputeUtilization
choices.explanation: This monitors as a percentage how close the execution time is to the limit.

choices.text: Average FunctionThrottles
choices.explanation: The number of throttles should be handled as a Sum, and this metric does not represent the percentage of proximity to the limit itself.

choices.text: p95 OriginLatency
choices.explanation: This is origin response latency, not CloudFront Function execution time.

learning.reason: This monitors as a percentage how close the execution time is to the limit.
learning.concept: FunctionComputeUtilization shows from 0 to 100 the percentage of the permitted execution time used by a CloudFront Function.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Monitoring Dropped Packets at an Interface VPC Endpoint
prompt: An internal API accessed through an Interface VPC endpoint has intermittent missing responses. Operationally, you want to detect endpoint or endpoint service issues early and account for the possibility that arriving packets larger than 8,500 bytes may be dropped. Which metric is most appropriate?

choices.text: Monitor only the Average of ActiveConnectionCount
choices.explanation: The connection count cannot detect whether packets are being dropped.

choices.text: Sum PacketsDropped by VPC Endpoint Id, Subnet Id, and Service Name
choices.explanation: This monitors drops at the target endpoint and enables isolation by service and subnet.

choices.text: Monitor EndpointHealthyENICount
choices.explanation: This is a Route 53 Resolver endpoint metric, not a PrivateLink endpoint metric.

choices.text: Count only REJECT entries in VPC Flow Logs
choices.explanation: This reflects an allow or reject result on the VPC side and does not directly show all packets dropped within the endpoint or service.

learning.reason: This monitors drops at the target endpoint and enables isolation by service and subnet.
learning.concept: PacketsDropped for AWS/PrivateLinkEndpoints represents packets dropped by an endpoint or endpoint service.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Identify an Unexpected Internet Egress with VPC Flow Logs
prompt: Traffic from an EC2 instance on a Nitro system to AWS services was expected to use a gateway endpoint, but a cost analysis suggested that the traffic might be going over the internet. In custom VPC Flow Logs, which field identifies that an egress flow passed through an Internet Gateway?

choices.text: Examine only records whose log-status is OK
choices.explanation: This indicates the log collection status, not the type of network egress.

choices.text: Examine only pkt-srcaddr
choices.explanation: This identifies the original source address but does not determine whether the flow used a gateway endpoint or an Internet Gateway.

choices.text: Examine only records whose action is ACCEPT
choices.explanation: This indicates whether the traffic was permitted but does not show which egress path it used.

choices.text: Include traffic-path and flow-direction, and examine records where flow-direction is egress and traffic-path is 8
choices.explanation: Combining the direction and the path through the Internet Gateway allows the egress route to be verified.

learning.reason: Combining the direction and the path through the Internet Gateway allows the egress route to be verified.
learning.concept: traffic-path indicates the path type, and the example states that 8 represents egress through an Internet Gateway.

category: ネットワーク管理と運用
examDomain: ネットワーク管理と運用
title: Determine on the Instance Whether the EC2 Connection-Tracking Limit Was Reached
prompt: During a load test, increasing the number of simultaneous TCP connections received by an EC2 instance causes some new connections to fail while existing connections continue. There are no security group changes, and the outbound bandwidth limit has not been reached. With the applicable ENA driver, which metric should be checked to determine whether the instance's connection-tracking allowance is the cause?

choices.text: Look only at the value of bw_out_allowance_exceeded.
choices.explanation: This metric concerns the outbound bandwidth allowance and does not indicate that the connection-tracking allowance was exceeded.

choices.text: Monitor only linklocal_allowance_exceeded.
choices.explanation: This metric concerns traffic to link-local services and does not represent the tracking allowance for ordinary new TCP connections.

choices.text: Check the increase in conntrack_allowance_exceeded on the affected instance during the failure period.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes packet drops caused by exceeding the connection-tracking limit from drops caused by a bandwidth limit.

choices.text: Treat the average number of bytes reported by NetworkOut as the permitted number of simultaneous TCP connections.
choices.explanation: Transferred bytes cannot be used to determine whether packets exceeded the simultaneous connection-tracking allowance.

learning.reason: This distinguishes packet drops caused by exceeding the connection-tracking limit from drops caused by a bandwidth limit.
learning.concept: ENA's conntrack_allowance_exceeded counts packets dropped because the connection-tracking allowance was exceeded.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス

title: Authorize Service Calls with IAM
prompt: A private API accessed through VPC Lattice must be exposed only to authorized IAM principals.

choices.text: Add a NAT Gateway
choices.explanation: A NAT Gateway does not provide authorization.

choices.text: Shorten the DNS TTL
choices.explanation: This does not control access.

choices.text: Configure a VPC Lattice service network auth policy for IAM authentication
choices.explanation: This allows service calls based on IAM principals.

choices.text: Use only a security group
choices.explanation: A security group does not authorize API principals.

learning.concept: VPC Lattice auth policy

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Distribute Revocation Information for Internal Certificates
prompt: A client certificate issued by a Private CA must be reported to the validating party after it is revoked.

choices.text: Create only a CloudWatch alarm
choices.explanation: This does not distribute a CRL.

choices.text: Change the certificate name
choices.explanation: This does not communicate the revocation status.

choices.text: Enable CRL configuration in Private CA and publish the CRL to S3
choices.explanation: This allows validators to retrieve the revocation list.

choices.text: Delete the CA
choices.explanation: Deleting the CA does not distribute revocation information for existing certificates.

learning.reason: This allows validators to retrieve the revocation list.
learning.concept: Private CA CRL

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Do not let interrupted connections continue without inspection
prompt: A TCP connection being inspected by AWS Network Firewall resumes partway through after a routing failure, and the firewall no longer has the original connection state. You want traffic without the original state to be denied, with an explicit notification sent to the client so it reconnects and is inspected again from a new session. Which policy setting should you use?

choices.text: Set the stateless fragment default action to Drop.
choices.explanation: This setting handles fragmented packets and does not return a TCP rejection for a TCP stream received partway through.

choices.text: Add Alert to the firewall logs and leave the traffic-processing policy unchanged.
choices.explanation: Enabling logging does not change how traffic without the original connection state is handled or send a response that prompts reconnection.

choices.text: Set the Stream exception policy to Reject.
choices.explanation: This rejects the existing stream and notifies the client with a TCP rejection. When the client reconnects, the new session can be evaluated from the beginning.

choices.text: Set the Stream exception policy to Drop.
choices.explanation: This can discard the original traffic, but it does not explicitly return a TCP rejection to prompt a quick reconnection.

learning.reason: The existing stream is not accepted; instead, the client receives a TCP rejection. Reconnecting allows the new session to be evaluated from the beginning.
learning.concept: The Reject setting for a stream exception policy discards the affected traffic and returns a rejection to the TCP side.

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス

choices.text: Enable Service Connect TLS
choices.explanation: This protects Service Connect service-to-service traffic with TLS.

choices.text: Assign a public IP
choices.explanation: This conflicts with protecting internal communication.

choices.text: Increase CloudWatch log volume
choices.explanation: This does not encrypt data in transit.

choices.text: Increase the CPU in the task definition
choices.explanation: This does not enable encryption.

learning.reason: Service Connect service-to-service traffic can be protected with TLS.
learning.concept: ECS Service Connect TLS

category: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
examDomain: ネットワークセキュリティ・コンプライアンス・ガバナンス
title: Block unnecessary communication between EKS Pods
prompt: Within the same EKS cluster, you want to allow communication only from the frontend Pod to the backend Pod.

choices.text: Change only the node security group
choices.explanation: This does not provide Pod-level traffic control.

choices.text: Remove the NAT
choices.explanation: This is not a Pod-to-Pod policy.

choices.text: Apply Kubernetes NetworkPolicy using the EKS network policy feature
choices.explanation: This can control Pod-to-Pod communication using labels and other selectors.

title: Understand the audit boundary for port forwarding
prompt: A DB is maintained using Session Manager port forwarding. An audit trail of the initiator, time, and similar operational details is required, but recording the contents of the forwarded DB protocol is not required. Which audit design is most appropriate?

choices.text: Assume that Session Manager CloudWatch Logs output alone provides both the port-forwarding contents and the initiator's audit trail.

choices.text: Audit operations such as StartSession with CloudTrail, assuming that no port-forwarding content logs are generated.

title: Restrict access paths to an existing public ALB to your CloudFront distribution
prompt: A service cannot move a public ALB internally, and users access it through your CloudFront distribution. Restrict the ALB's inbound traffic to connections intended for the CloudFront origin, and also prevent other CloudFront distributions from using the listener endpoint. Choose two.

choices.text: Allow general internet CIDRs in the ALB security group and consider this sufficient as long as CloudFront retains a public IP.
choices.explanation: This does not exclude sources other than CloudFront and provides no listener condition that distinguishes the distribution.

choices.text: Set CloudFront's Viewer protocol policy to HTTPS Only and add no restriction on the ALB side.
choices.explanation: This defines the connection method from users to CloudFront, but it does not reject direct access to the ALB or forwarding from another distribution.

choices.text: Only omit the ALB's public DNS name from DNS and leave the security group and listener rules open.
choices.explanation: Not advertising the public DNS name does not restrict the ALB's sources or forwarding conditions.

choices.text: Use an origin custom header configured only for your distribution as a forwarding condition in the ALB listener rule.
choices.explanation: Even through CloudFront, only requests matching the configuration of your specified distribution can be forwarded to the targets.

choices.text: Allow CloudFront's origin-facing AWS-managed prefix list in the ALB security group.
choices.explanation: This limits inbound sources to the CloudFront origin-facing network and restricts direct connections from users.

learning.reason: Limit inbound sources to the CloudFront origin-facing network to restrict direct user connections. In addition, even through CloudFront, only requests matching the configuration of the specified distribution can be forwarded to the targets.
learning.concept: Protecting a public ALB can combine the AWS-managed prefix list for CloudFront origins with a custom header for per-distribution control.

title: Distinguishing FAS from Direct S3 Operations by a Role
prompt: An analytics IAM role sends a query to Amazon Athena. Athena uses a Forward Access Session (FAS) to read data in S3 using the caller's permissions. You want to deny s3:GetObject calls made directly by the same role while evaluating FAS-based reads using the existing permissions. Do not include the type of service as a condition. Which condition should be applied to the explicit deny?

choices.text: When aws:SourceVpce matches the specified S3 VPC endpoint.
choices.explanation: This key identifies the VPC endpoint but does not determine whether the request is using FAS.

choices.text: When aws:PrincipalIsAWSService is false.
choices.explanation: Because FAS uses the caller role's permissions, this condition would deny both direct requests by the role and FAS requests.

choices.text: When aws:ViaAWSService is false.
choices.explanation: This key is true for FAS requests and false for requests sent directly by the role.

choices.text: When aws:PrincipalArn matches the ARN of the analytics IAM role.
choices.explanation: This matches both direct requests and FAS requests that use the same role's permissions.

learning.reason: Limiting the explicit deny to cases where aws:ViaAWSService is false denies direct requests. FAS requests do not match this deny and are evaluated using the existing permissions.
learning.concept: aws:ViaAWSService is a Boolean key that identifies FAS. Use aws:CalledVia and similar keys to identify the service through which a request was made.
